## engine4-2: A found place moves on the map, and the direction word to it changes, once the save is opened again

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/mapview.py:70`
- **Evidence:** engine/mapview.py:70: the drawn positions are used only `if all(i in drawn_now or None not in (x, y) ...)` for every top-level place; otherwise lines 79-126 run the 400-step spring layout for the whole map and line 124 rescales every result into its own frame, with no relation to the drawn coordinates. Places made in play (engine/discovery.py:76 ids x_..., engine/dungeons.py:108, engine/roads.py:177) are top-level with no x/y. In the session that makes one, the layout is already cached and position() puts it at the mean of its neighbours; at world:open of a later session it is on the map before the first layout, so the `all` fails. Measured with audit/work/engine4_map.py (82 top-level places, anchor blackpine_forest at (215.0, 535.0)): the find sits at (215.0, 535.0) in the session that found it and exits.groups labels it 'a track south'; after reopening it sits at (710.3, 702.3) and the label is 'a track east'. The first layout also takes 507 ms instead of 2 ms. In the first session the find sits exactly on its one neighbour, so its heading is degenerate (always south).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player finds a hollow off Blackpine Forest and is told it lies down a track south. They save, quit and load: the same exit now reads 'a track east' and the map pin has jumped across the map, away from the forest it hangs off. tools/sim/map_caches_452_test.py pins that bearing words must not move when a place is found; nothing pins them across a reopen.
- **Fix:** In layout(), when any place is drawn, never run the spring layout: return the drawn and own positions and leave undrawn places out of `pos`, so position() places them by its neighbour rule in every session. The reopened save then matches session one exactly (same pin, same word), no kept recording moves, and the half second to a second at the first map read of such a save goes. As a second step, for the degenerate heading: give a place made in play its own x and y when it is made (the anchor's position plus a direction and distance seeded from its id and its minutes, saved with it), which every later session reads; that changes the direction word in recordings that hold a find, so it is a behaviour change to rebless on purpose. Keep the spring layout only for a world with nothing drawn. Test: the position and the exit label of a find, a dungeon entrance and a road stop are equal before and after closing and reopening the campaign.
- **The finder's first fix:** In layout(), when the map has drawn positions, keep them and place each undrawn place by the neighbour rule position() already uses (mean of placed neighbours, with a small offset seeded from the place id when there is one neighbour so the heading is not degenerate and is the same in both sessions). Keep the spring layout only for a world with nothing drawn. This also removes the half-second first layout on every save that holds a find.
- **The check:** Seen happening on a campaign. Session one: the layout is not cached when the scene is built or the place entered, and is cached after the first line's exit intercept; a find off the Tidepool Caves (131.0, 958.0) then sits at (131.0, 958.0) and its exit reads 'a track south'. After close and reopen: open_world puts the find on the map while the layout is still uncached, the `all(...)` at line 70 fails, the 400-step spring layout runs (1170 ms here, 491 ms in the reporter's script, 2 ms when every place is drawn) and the find sits at (485.5, 0.0), exit 'a track north'. The reporter's own numbers reproduce as well ((215, 535) to (710.3, 702.3), south to east). Drawn places keep their drawn positions in both branches (lines 119-122); what moves is every undrawn top-level place: finds, dungeon entrances (type dungeon, no parent) and road stops. In session one the find sits exactly on its one neighbour, so atan2(0, -0.0) gives 180 degrees: always 'south'. Nothing pins this across a reopen: tools/sim/map_caches_452_test.py pins only the same session ('bearing words must not move'), perf_558 and map_test pin the memo and the frame. docs/design/04_performance_patch.md describes the fast path and says nothing of finds.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/mapview.py layout() 57-127 and position() 148-163, engine/exits.py _heading and groups, engine/discovery.py apply_all and make_place, engine/dungeons.py entrance_place, engine/roads.py:177, scenes/world.py open_world 934-952 (ensure_discoveries, ensure_road_place and ensure_dungeons run before anything reads the map) and scenes/exit_actions.py exit_request (every typed line's intercept reads exits.match, which lays the map out). Ran the reporter's audit/work/engine4_map.py, then my own end to end on a real campaign through the stub (audit/work/sk_engine4_1_check.py): a find added after one line, the campaign closed, opened again with open_world. Searched tools/sim and GOALS.md / docs/design for a pin or a note.

## engine5-1: remove_npc ties off the player's quests on a copy loaded from the save; three callers then commit the scene's own copy over it

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/pulse.py:936`
- **Evidence:** pulse.py:936 `player = store.load_player()` ... 942 `player.quests.remove(q)` ... 951 `store.save_player(player)`. Callers that keep their own player object: engine/events.py:882 (fallen_allies), engine/events.py:199 (defeat_tagged), scenes/road_actions.py:48 (leave_road). scenes/arc_actions.py:821-822 and scenes/world.py run_pulse (f466) do reload. Reproduced with simlib's stub (scratchpad/audit/work/engine5_checks.py, check B): after fallen_allies the save's quests=[] and the scene's copy=['q_audit']; after the operation's save_player(ws.player) the save's quests=['q_audit'] again and obligations.find() for it is None.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A realm ally who gave the player a job (or took a commission) dies beside them after a fight, or a road stop's person who gave a job is left behind. remove_npc removes the quest, its key item and the commission from a fresh copy and saves it, and closes the obligation row as issuer_gone. The turn's commit (scenes/world.py:1267) then writes the scene's older copy back: the quest is in the journal again with nobody alive to hand it to, its obligation row is closed, the key item is back, and the journal line that said it came to nothing is lost.
- **Fix:** The reporter's fix is right and should be the only one: remove_npc stops loading and saving the player behind its caller (it takes the records to tie off, or returns the tie-offs for the scene to apply as drift's deltas are), so the pulse and every scene caller share one path and each character's jobs are tied off, not store.load_player()'s one. Do not add a reload after each call: there are at least seven sites. To find the rest of this class, put f589's stale-save detector (storage/worldrow.py, the world state only today) on save_player and save_place as well. One thing for the owner to rule on: once fixed, a job taken from a person met on the road is struck from the journal the moment the player walks on (remove_npc's rule for 'moved on along the road'); today it survives only through this fault.
- **The finder's first fix:** Make remove_npc tie off the record its caller holds (take the acting record or records as an argument, or return the tie-offs as a delta the scene applies, as drift's deltas are) so every caller is covered by one path; the same change takes store.load_player() (the one player) out of it for multiplayer.
- **The check:** 1a printed, after the fight's line and again one line later: npc gone='died fighting beside Ironbound Vanguard'; quests in the SAVE=['THE JOB']; commissions in the SAVE=['ally1']; open obligation row for the job: False; 'came to nothing' line in the saved item history: False. 1b printed (ops action:move, passage, world, arrival, law, tail; none failed): npc gone='moved on along the road'; quests in the SAVE=['THE JOB']; commissions in the SAVE=['milna_birch']; open obligation row: False; no 'came to nothing' line. So the tie-off remove_npc saves (pulse.py:936-951) is written over by the scene's older copy, and the registry and the journal disagree. The quoted code is there. One correction: events.py:199 is in on_kills (called by guild_actions.record_kills); there is no defeat_tagged. The class is wider than the three callers named (traced, not run): assault_over (events.py:1435) and apply_player_events (events.py:1360, which run_pulse calls after its own reload at world.py:690) reach remove_npc through town_outcome and _catch_people, where a town's toll kills many at once; events.lose and events.finish (events.py:659, 688) and matters.py:515 reach it through apply_effects when an effect is a leave. No test pins the kept job; world_operation_466_test.py:143 pins the opposite for the pulse path (gone after the line, in the scene and in the save).
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/pulse.py remove_npc (919-951), its seven call sites in engine and scenes, the commit at scenes/world.py:1267 and combat_scene.py:1057, and every place the scene takes the saved player again (only arc_actions.py:822, world.py:690, 1608, 1964). Then ran my own script on simlib's stub, through real typed lines, not by calling the functions: C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_engine5_1.py (sections 1a and 1b; campaigns audit_check_engine5_1_*, removed). 1a: a realm ally who gave a job and holds a commission goes down in a real wolf fight that ends through CombatScene.finish. 1b: a road meeting's person gives a job, then the typed line 'I walk back to Parth.' Party of 3: TALK list=20, own 4/12, her oldest repeated -> kept; EXCHANGE list=28, own 0/12, her newest gesture repeated word for word -> kept=True. The reach is wider than the finding says: banter_actions.py:109 passes the other speakers and then self.gesturers(h), which are the same hires again, so a full party of three reaches 16 others' gestures in every exchange and none of the speaker's own is checked; in a plain talk with a full party only her newest 4 are. - **What a player or the owner meets:** The player comes back to an innkeeper who has since been given a clue to hold (kind 'knows', subject ''), heard town gossip, or watched another character. recognition.line takes the newest memory that is not own_life, whatever its subject, so the greeting prompt reads 'The last thing you remember of them: The reeve's seal was on the crate they pulled from the river.' ## situations-2: Who a situation's end credits is read from the 40-row record window: a counted change pushed out by later ones leaves no contributor and the end is read as lost

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/situation_parts.py:606`. **Same place:** situations-1
- **Evidence:** `return sorted({c['by'] for c in th.get('changes') or [] if c.get('by') and c.get('becomes') in better` (606) over a list keep_changes cuts at 1302 `)[-int(RU['window']):]` (situations.yaml:314 window: 40). Run (work/sit_cases.py case 6): blocker won over, 5 kept changes, way met -> resolved, player, achieved; the same with 41 -> record 40, contributors [], status ended, result lost. Run (work/sit_cases3.py, the act path through ws.on_other): one line wins the blocker, a second line said 41 times (3 ruling calls in all) -> the 'open' is gone from the record and contributors is [] while the blocker's part still says open.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A campaign situation with many parts: one ruling may keep 12 changes (rulings.most), so four later rulings push out the change that counted. The threat stays resolved (the part's own willing and now), but when the end comes by anything that is not itself a fresh counted change (a way met, a creature beaten, an effect run out), read_end finds no contributor and calls lose(): fallout, no deed, no reward. With two characters the earlier contributor loses their deed and share while the later keeps theirs.
- **Fix:** As proposed, and shared with situations-1: when the one writer keeps a counted change (a better word on a part of the heart, or a way met that resolves a threat of the heart), add its doer's character id to a set on the thread; contributors() reads the set and the window stays what the record shows. The set is bounded by the characters in the game, so the cap rule holds. The heart is written once, so whether a change counted can be decided when it is kept. moved() at situation_parts.py:1017 ('a change since they took their stance') reads the same window; give the part a mark (the sequence number of the last gain that concerns them) so a gain that has left the window still moves them. Test with 41 uncounted changes after the counted one, and with two characters.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the credit apart from the window: when keep_changes (or a met way) keeps a counted change, add its doer to a set on the thread, bounded by the characters in the game; contributors() reads that and the window stays what the record shows. moved()'s 'a change since they took their stance' (situation_parts.py:1017) reads the same window and needs a per-part mark for the same reason.
- **The check:** Printed, f2: with 5 and with 39 uncounted changes after the counted one: 'contributors now=['player']' and after the end 'status=resolved result=player ending_kind=achieved settled deeds=[('player', 'achieved')]'. With 40 and with 41: 'record rows=40; the blocker still open toward the player='open'; contributors now=[]' and 'status=ended result=lost ending_kind=lost settled deeds=[]'. Printed, f2b (typed lines): 10 repeats: 'record rows=11 an 'open' still on the record=True contributors=['player']' then 'resolved result=player achieved'; 41 repeats: 'ruling calls in all=3 record rows=40 an 'open' still on the record=False the blocker's part willing={'player': 'open'} contributors=[]' then 'status=ended result=lost'. Limit on reach: the credit is lost only when every row left in the window is uncounted (not a better word, or on a part outside the heart), so one character needs 40 such changes in a row after their last counted one; with two characters each one's credit falls out separately, which is the likelier case once multiplayer is on.
- **How it was checked:** Read contributors() (situation_parts.py:600-607), keep_changes (1300-1302) and met_way (1415-1416), both of which cut th['changes'] at rulings.window; data/rules/situations.yaml:312-314 (most 12, window 40). Ran two scripts of my own (campaign audit_check_situations_1, removed in finally). work/check_situations_1_f2.py: a campaign situation with two who block, one harmed, one fixer; the first blocker won over by a gift through ruled() and keep_changes(); then N 'believes' kept on the fixer (a part outside the heart); then the second blocker marked dead and events.read_ends. work/check_situations_1_f2b.py: the same through typed lines only (ws.on_other with the stub's ruling, the dice fixed at success), the second line said 10 and 41 times.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/16_end_reading.md:102-103 defines contributors from th['changes']; docs/design/15_phase2_survey.md:97 notes the window of 40. That the window can drop the credit is not written down.

## trace-fight-6: Dominate on the last standing foe ends the fight as a win at once, with the foe unhurt

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/spellcraft.py:478`. **Same place:** engine7-3
- **Evidence:** elif eid == "dominate" and dfn.alive and dfn.side == "enemy" and getattr(dfn, "category", "") == "undead" and not dfn.boss:
    dfn.counters["turned"], dfn.counters["turned_until"] = 1, combat.round + int(N("rounds", 2))
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Combat.enemies() leaves out the turned, and services/fight.py:404 declares victory when it is empty ('if not f.over and not f.enemies() and not combat.muster(f)'). One undead, or the last one standing: the spell lands, enemies() is empty and the fight is over as a victory inside the player's own action with the undead at full health (stubbed run, work/trace_fight_check2.py: hp 1000000 of 1000000, turned 1, over 'victory'). Nothing is dead and no one yielded, so the player reads 'They got away. You've nothing to show for this one.' while the story says it turned on its own side. Dread Regent's turn_coat guards this case (combat_perks.py:907); Dominate does not. Any fight against undead that are not bosses can be left this way.
- **Fix:** One law for turning a foe, in one function that both turn_coat and Dominate call: a foe is turned only while another foe (not itself turned) stands; otherwise Dominate's blow lands and nothing turns. That covers the lone undead, the last one standing and the two-in-a-row case. A single 'is the fight won' function for services/fight.py round and _talk, finish_round and player_ai is still worth having, but it cannot be the fix by itself (see the run above), and several callers index enemies()[0] or take min() of it, so a fight left running with enemies() empty would need those looked at first.
- **The finder's first fix:** One 'is the fight won' function used by services/fight.py round and _talk, finish_round and player_ai that does not count a foe turned for a few rounds as gone; or Dominate refuses, as turn_coat does, when no other enemy stands.
- **The check:** The quoted lines are at engine/spellcraft.py:478-479. Run: Dominate landed on 48 of 60 casts and the fight was a victory at once on 48 of 48 (first case: undead hp 999979 of 1000000, turned 1, enemies() [], over 'victory'; story 'The first foe turns on its own side, a stronger will on it (Dominate)'). With two undead, dominating one leaves enemies() ['e2'] and no win, but dominating the second a round later empties enemies() and wins with both unhurt. victory() then finds no dead and no yielded and prints 'They got away. You've nothing to show for this one.'; beyond the report, finish() also calls dungeon_fight_over('victory') (chamber_cleared) and road_fight_over('victory') (loot_camp), so a crypt chamber is cleared and a road camp looted without a blow that mattered. The first fix the report offers does not work alone: with the instant test skipped, finish_round gives the lone dominated foe its turn, turned_turn finds no old side, sets fled and tells 'flees, its old side broken', and the round ends over = 'victory' with hp 100 of 100.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/spellcraft.py on_hit and the dominate branch (478-480), Combat.enemies() (combat.py:443, leaves out the turned), services/fight.py round (404-405) and _talk (424), finish_round (3058) and player_ai (3079), engine/combat_perks.py turn_coat (902-915, guarded at 907) and turned_turn (918-931), scenes/combat_scene.py victory (1096-1106) and finish, scenes/dungeon_actions.py dungeon_fight_over, scenes/road_actions.py road_fight_over. The expression is reachable: engine/ability_slots.py assign_expressions draws one of the element's damage expressions for a necrotic ability. tools/sim/element_effects_test.py 277-280 pins only that an undead turns for 2 rounds and comes back. Ran work/skeptic_tf_b.py and skeptic_tf_d.py: a necrotic ability carrying 'dominate' cast through combat.act_ability on a lone undead, then the test services/fight.py:404 makes.

## engine7-3: Death's Door writes the target's health to zero itself instead of going through the damage path, so the floors and on-fall stages do not run

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium (first given as low). **Place:** `engine/spellcraft.py:487`. **Same place:** trace-fight-6
- **Evidence:** engine/spellcraft.py:487-488 `floor = 1 if ((combat.mentor and dfn.side == "player") or combat.duel) else 0` / `dfn.hp = float(floor)`. Every other loss of health goes through C.take_damage and the stages of engine/damage.py (boss_last_stand, deathless, deathward, yields_floor, on_fall, after_damage, healing_after_damage, release, morale, avenger). Here two of the floors are re-made by hand and the rest are skipped. tools/sim/element_effects_test.py:284 pins only that the target dies. The bypass was read end to end; which skipped stage shows in play was not run.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A foe at or under the data's 15% is finished by Death's Door. A foe who would yield at its floor is killed instead; a hold the fallen had is not let go by battlefield.release in that step; a pack whose leader falls this way never rolls morale (behaviors.morale_on_death), so the rout's dice are not drawn; a death ward or a boss's last stand does not answer (that one may be meant, and is the owner's call).
- **Fix:** Do not send the remaining health through C.take_damage as proposed: the blow path would put it through resistance, barrier, wards and the Unbroken cap, so 'kills outright' (the card's words in data/rules/spellcraft.yaml) would stop being true. Declare an outright-kill path beside dot_tick and tear in data/rules/stages.yaml (the floors that must hold: tick_floor's mentor and duel floor and yields_floor, plus whichever of deathward, breath and deathless the owner wants to answer; then health, on_fall, after_damage, healing_after_damage, release, morale, avenger) and have Death's Door call damage.resolve on it. The same path can serve the other direct kills in tools/purity.py HP_EXEMPT, whose list then shrinks as its rule asks. Test it on the yielding foe and on a pack's morale, not only on the 15% line.
- **The finder's first fix:** Deal the target's remaining health through C.take_damage (a kill of its own kind if it must pass armour and wards) so the floors and the on-fall stages are the pipeline's, and drop the hand-made mentor and duel floor.
- **The check:** Seen happening, four ways. (A) A foe that yields (yields_at 0.25, 'never dies' by engine/combat.py:212) at 26% health, struck through combat.apply_damage: without Death's Door it ends at hp 1, fled; with it hp 0.0, alive False, log 'foe 1 falls', felled_by set. The pipeline's yields_floor leaves it at 1 hp, which is under 15%, so Death's Door then kills it. The only such foe in the game is Orenna's Bound Executioner (scenes/orenna_actions.py:195-196, rank elite, so the boss guard does not cover him): he would be told as fallen, counted and looted as a kill by CombatScene.victory (the 'not dead and not yielded' branch at combat_scene.py:1102 is the one the fight is written for), then the yield is narrated and he returns bound in the High Keeper's fight. (B) A pack's leader at 10%: an ordinary kill draws 2 morale dice and one of the pack runs; by Death's Door 0 draws, nobody runs. (C) After the kill the dead foe's id stays in the others' engaged_with (ordinary kill: []), and combat.hit_parts still gives a ranged-weapon fighter 'point-blank ... -15' against the next target. (D) Orenna's Last Breath on the target is not asked (ordinary blow: restored to full). The other outright kills outside the path (combat_perks.py:621-623, summons.py:147-150, on_dot_death at combat_perks.py:342-351) release by hand, and the affliction death rolls morale by hand; Death's Door does neither. Severity raised from low: a quest foe who must live is killed and recorded as a kill, and two numbers of the fight are wrong, though only for a character whose necrotic ability drew this expression.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/spellcraft.py:204-212 and :486-489, engine/damage.py whole, data/rules/stages.yaml, the caller engine/combat.py:1451-1454 and :1599-1618, behaviors.morale_on_death, battlefield.release and the raw readers of engaged_with, scenes/orenna_actions.py:186-201 and :272-285, scenes/combat_scene.py:1015-1108, tools/purity.py:40-74. Ran a CPU script with fighters built as tools/sim/element_effects_test.py builds them (scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_engine7_3_deaths_door.py), each case beside an ordinary killing blow. The one test (element_effects_test.py:284-286) pins only that the target dies and a boss does not.
- **Already recorded:** Not in GOALS.md or docs/design. The write itself is a recorded exemption: tools/purity.py HP_EXEMPT lists ("engine/spellcraft.py", "dfn.hp = float(floor)") under 'floors and clamps outside a blow' (pinned by tools/sim/hp_writes_505_test.py, 'the list may only shrink'), and engine/damage.py's docstring names the exemptions. What the bypass skips is not recorded anywhere.

## fight-abilities-5: A charged spell or a wind-up technique loses every bonus fixed when it was begun: Archmage's Focus, Overchannel's blood, Headsman and the other heavy-ability perks

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/spellcraft.py:1107`
- **Evidence:** engine/spellcraft.py:1107 `C._act_ability(combat, f, move, t, rng or _RNG, None, True)` (the release goes straight to the inner function, as an echo); engine/combat.py:2087 `free_cast = move.resource == "mana" and not att.archmage_used and "archmage" in am and not echo`, with archmage_used set at the wind-up; combat.py:2030 and 2039 set tier_now and pop blood_cast in act_ability's wrapper, which the release never enters.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Bare fights under the stub, 24 to 39 seeds each (audit/work/fa_edges.py archmage, fa_edges2.py release_perks). Archmage's Focus: a first spell that is a bolt hits 27.6 against 18.4 without it; a charged one 55.1 against 55.1 (it is free, and the 50% is spent and lost). Overchannel: a bolt paid in blood 26.7 against 17.8; a charged spell 53.3 against 53.3, the health still paid. Headsman: a kill by a plain heavy technique sets the free next heavy, a kill by a wind-up heavy does not. By the same reading Bulwark Engine, Blood for Blood and War Drum (combat_perks.py:105, 117, 168, 261 read tier_now) and reach_now (777) never see an ability that was wound up.
- **Fix:** As proposed: the wind-up keeps in att.charging what the payment settled (the Archmage share, blood_cast, who it is for), and the release enters act_ability with its own flag (released, never echo) so the wrapper sets tier_now and reach_now and the kept bonuses apply when the blow lands. Add that after_cast owes its repeats (Spell Echo, Grave Chorus) at the release and not at the wind-up, so an echo of a gathered spell is a second blow rather than a second wind-up. charging is part of the saved fight row, so what it keeps must be plain data.
- **The finder's first fix:** The wind-up stores in att.charging what the payment decided (the Archmage share, blood_cast, the recipient), and the release goes through act_ability with a flag of its own (released, not echo), so the wrapper sets tier_now and reach_now and the stored bonuses apply when the blow lands; echo keeps meaning only a perk's repeat.
- **The check:** sk_fa5.py, 40 seeds, mean damage: Archmage's Focus on a bolt 26.1 without, 39.0 with (free); on a charged spell 91.1 without, 91.1 with (free, the 50% gone, and archmage_used is spent at the wind-up). Overchannel: a bolt paid in blood 39.0 against 26.1; a charged spell 91.1 against 91.1 with the 76 health still paid. Headsman: a plain heavy killed in 33 of 40 and set the free next heavy in 33; a wind-up heavy killed in 33 and set it in 0. sk_fa5b.py: Blood for Blood, bleeding and blinded, a plain heavy missed 0 of 200 with the perk (100 without); a wind-up heavy missed 100 of 200 with it. War Drum: a plain heavy landed 80 of 100 and set the drum on the companion 80 times; a wind-up heavy landed 80 and set it 0 times. Bulwark Engine reads the same counter (by reading). The same root has one more face, not in the finding: the repeats are owed at the wind-up too. sk_fa5c.py: Spell Echo on a third charged cast tells 'Thunderhead, three times running, and the third time it happens twice', then only 'You begin to gather Thunderhead' a second time; blows per cast [1, 1, 1] against [1, 1, 2] for a bolt. Charged is 45% of heavy single-target spell forms and wind-up 12% of technique forms (spells.yaml:77, martial.yaml:38), so the reach is every such ability held with one of these perks.
- **How it was checked:** Read combat.act_ability and _act_ability (2004-2187), spellcraft.wind_up and release (1068-1110), combat.start_turn (2637-2638), every reader of tier_now, reach_now and blood_cast (combat_perks.py 105, 117, 168, 182, 261, 318, 777) and the perk and legendary texts. tier_now is set only at combat.py:2030 and popped in the same wrapper's finally; the release calls _act_ability directly with echo=True. Ran audit/work/sk_fa5.py, sk_fa5b.py and sk_fa5c.py: a bolt against a charged spell and a plain heavy against a wind-up heavy, same seeds with and without each perk.

## fight-abilities-3: A Bound summon made anew by casting its spell in a fight is gone again at the next fight: only a cast outside a fight mends the bond

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/summons.py:115`
- **Evidence:** engine/summons.py:113-115 `for f in make(combat, att, move):` / `C.enters(combat, f)` / `combat.bound_id = move.id` (written to the fight only); 249-250 `if fight.bound_fell and getattr(character, "bound_summon", ""):` / `character.bound_broken = True`. The only code that clears bound_broken or sets bound_summon is form_outside (summons.py:261, 264), called from scenes/world.py:4128 alone.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Through the real scene under the stub (audit/work/fa_scene.py bound; the same on a bare fight in fa_edges.py bound_between): a summoner's Warden is destroyed in fight 1 and the note says 'Cast its spell again to make it anew.' In fight 2 the player casts Call the Warden (mana paid, 'your Bound summon takes shape beside you') and it survives; after the fight character.bound_broken is still True, and fight 3 begins without it and without a note. The same holds for a character whose bound_summon is empty or names another spell: a Bound cast made in a fight is never written to the character. Every summoner class has exactly one Bound summon (ability_slots.plan).
- **Fix:** summons.after_fight writes what the fight ended with: destroyed (bound_fell) stays broken; a Bound summon of the bonded spell standing at the end clears bound_broken. Take the character's own fighter (bound_of(fight, owner)) rather than fight.player, since after_fight is called per character and multiplayer is a goal. Test the recast, a recast that is destroyed again, and a second Bound spell (which must still be refused in a fight).
- **The finder's first fix:** summons.after_fight, the one place a fight's summon state is written back, records what the fight ended with: a Bound summon of that spell standing at the end clears bound_broken (and sets bound_summon when the fight's bound_id says the bond is this spell's); one destroyed stays broken. Test it with a second Bound spell as well as the recast.
- **The check:** sk_fa3.py: fight 1 the Warden walks in, is destroyed, note 'Your Bound summon was unmade in the fight. Cast its spell again to make it anew.', bound_broken True. Fight 2: it does not walk in; the spell is cast (not refused, 23 mana paid, told 'You call on Warden, and your Bound summon takes shape beside you') and stands to the end; after_fight returns '' and bound_broken is still True. Fight 3: it does not walk in, and nothing says why. Only form_outside mends it (fight 4 walks in). core/models.py:267 describes the flag as 'unmade in a fight and has not been cast again', and summons_test.py pins only the cast outside a fight, so nothing pins the in-fight recast as meant to be lost. Lines are one off from the quote (make at 114, enters 115, bound_id 116). Part of the scenario is wrong: a character whose bond names another spell cannot make a Bound cast in a fight at all; sk_fa3b.py shows summons.refuse (line 98) answering 'Another Bound spell holds your bond; a Bound summon can only be changed outside a fight.' with no mana paid. The empty-bond case does behave as said (cast accepted, nothing written), but creation always writes the bond for a summoner and only a summoner is taught summon spells, so I found no way to reach it in play.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/summons.py whole, services/fight.py begin (277) and companions_after (758), scenes/world.py:4126-4128, core/models.py:266-267, character/creation.py:324, engine/lessons.py:212-218 and tools/sim/summons_test.py (134-154). Searched every tracked file for bound_broken and bound_summon: the only writers are summons.after_fight (sets) and summons.form_outside (clears or switches). Ran audit/work/sk_fa3.py and sk_fa3b.py: the same calls the service makes (join_bound at the start, after_fight at the end) over four fights under the stub.

## engine7-1: truth.coined calls a given name 'no one' when it carries a contraction other than 's (Maren'll, Maren'd), so a sound reply is sent back to the model

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `engine/truth.py:625`
- **Evidence:** engine/truth.py:602 `_NAME = r"[A-Z][a-z]{2,}(?:['’][a-z]+)?"` and :625 `if re.sub(r"['’]s?$", "", w).lower() not in have:`. Only a trailing 's is taken off before the word is looked up among the given words (split as [a-z]+ runs). Ran truth.coined on CPU (scratchpad/audit/work/engine7_coined.py) with given 'WHO IS HERE: - Maren: the miller - Tal'eth the smith': "Ask at the mill, Maren'll know." -> "Maren'll"; "If you wait, Maren'd tell you herself." -> "Maren'd"; "No, Maren’ll know." -> "Maren’ll"; "Go and see Tal'eth about it." -> "Tal'eth"; "That is Maren's mill." -> '' (passes). check_speech returns the complaint and llm/gateway.py:325-328 rejects the reply.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A townsperson says "Maren'll know" about a person named in their own brief. The check answers "'Maren'll' is no one and nowhere you were told of", the gateway asks again (one more model call on the turn), and the same complaint twice ends the tries. The stiff-speech check (f714) pushes speakers toward contractions, so this is the very phrasing the engine asks for. A given name with an inner apostrophe (a model-made name such as Tal'eth) is refused every time it is spoken.
- **Fix:** In coined, look the word up the way the given words are split: take the [a-z]+ runs of the lowered word (truth._WORD) and pass it when the first run is given and every later run is either given or one of the clitics (s, ll, d, re, ve), instead of stripping only a trailing 's. That covers 'll, 'd, 've, a curly apostrophe, a name with an inner apostrophe and that name's possessive in one rule. Test on a case other than Maren'll: a player named with an inner apostrophe, said mid-sentence and as a possessive, plus an invented name with a contraction ("Harlan'll") still caught.
- **The finder's first fix:** In coined, look up the part of the word before the apostrophe (and, for a name with an inner apostrophe, both halves, as the given words are split) rather than stripping only 's. Test it with 'll, 'd, 're and a curly apostrophe so the whole class is covered.
- **The check:** It happens as described. Given 'Maren: the miller': "Ask at the mill, Maren'll know." -> 'Maren'll'; "Maren'd tell you herself" -> 'Maren'd'; curly "Maren’ll" -> refused; "The road to Parth'll be mud" -> 'Parth'll'; "Maren've" -> refused; "Maren's mill" and "Greywood's" pass; a name that opens the sentence passes (dropped as the sentence's first word). check_speech returns "'Maren'll' is no one and nowhere you were told of..." and gateway.py:325-328 and :389-395 send the reply back, ending the tries when the same complaint comes twice. Two corrections to the finding. (1) Residents' names are built by the engine from data/world/name_sounds.yaml (npc/names.py), which has no apostrophes, and no place, region, people or creature name in data/world has an inner apostrophe; the inner-apostrophe case comes from the PLAYER's own name, which scenes/goddess.py:428-433 takes as typed (strip, 40 characters at most). For a player named Kel'thar: "Well met, Kel'thar." and "That is Kel'thar's doing." are both refused, every time the name is said anywhere but first in a sentence, because the name's words are stored split ('kel', 'thar') and the spoken word is looked up whole. (2) Rate: the played run has 0 such rejections in 154 calls and no mid-sentence capitalised word with an apostrophe in its spoken replies, so the contraction case is rare with Gemma; the player-name case is every reply that names them.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/truth.py:602-627 and the caller llm/gateway.py:312-395; ran truth.coined and truth.check_speech on CPU (scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_engine7_1_coined.py, skeptic_engine7_1_player.py), on both roads a name reaches the check (the prompt text, and Scene.known_words). Searched tools/sim for a test that pins it (truth_test.py:116-124, pulse_v2_test.py:62-63, cataclysm_v2_test.py:52, frame_test.py:27: none uses a contraction other than a sentence-opening "I'll"). Searched the played run's 154 calls for the rejection and for the phrasing. Searched GOALS.md and docs/design for coined and check_speech: nothing.

## logs-sendbacks-5: RE-RATE llm-checks-9: the back-to-work check is half of all frame send-backs (71 of 141, 9.5% of frames); 15 are false alarms the proposed pattern only partly clears, and dropping the sentence in place settles all 71 with no call

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `llm/contracts.py:1297`. **Same place:** llm-checks-9
- **Evidence:** m = _BACK_TO_WORK.search(self.after or "")  /  raise ValueError(f"after shows them going back to what they were doing ('{m.group(0)}'): end on what the words changed, or leave after empty")  (1297-1300). All 71 logged answers are still sent back by today's pattern (work/logs_sendbacks/frame_btw.py).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Read all 71: 42 right, 14 borderline ('turns back toward the hearth'), 15 false alarms (21%): 'returns their gaze', 'frogsong resumes its rhythm', 'A comfortable silence returns', 'returns to his feet', 'until you return', 'turns back toward you and Calsa', 'You turn back to face', 'turns back toward the room, waiting for a decision'. The first round's pattern (the verb, then 'to', then not the listener) clears about 6 of the 15: 'returns their gaze', 'silence returns', 'resumes' and 'turns back toward the room' still hit. What the retry buys: of 62 second tries taken, 34 came back with `after` empty and 7 with `before` unchanged as well; 9 were sent back again. 101 s thrown away and 72 s of second tries on the 5090, the largest reason in a task that spends 12.1% of its model time on retries.
- **Fix:** As proposed, in two parts, both the owner's to approve since the test's wording moves. Narrow the pattern first (the going-back verb, then 'to' or 'toward', then anything but the listener; 'returns' with a direct object or no object is not it), so fewer right sentences are touched. Then drop instead of sending back: remove the sentence of `after` that carries the hit and keep the rest, counted as a repair so the night's measure shows how often; when what is left would open on a pronoun with nobody named, leave `after` empty. A false alarm then costs one sentence and no call. No prompt rule, and no length limit: the reason already offers 'leave after empty'.
- **The finder's first fix:** Do what the reason already offers: in the validator, drop the sentence of `after` that carries the hit and keep the rest (48 of the 71 have one sentence, so `after` becomes empty, which is what the model does on the retry more than half the time). No call, and a false alarm then costs one sentence instead of a call. The narrower pattern of llm-checks-9 is still worth having, so fewer good sentences are dropped. Low becomes medium.
- **The check:** The counts hold: 750 frames asked, 141 tries sent back, 71 of them for this (9.5% of frames); today's pattern still refuses all 71; 48 have a one-sentence `after`; of 62 second tries taken 34 came back with `after` empty (7 with `before` unchanged too), 28 rewrote it, and 9 were sent back again; 3 requests were lost. 100.7 s in the refused tries, 72.2 s in the next ones; retries are 135.8 of the task's 1,121 s (12.1%). Reading the 71 I count 11 to 15 with no going back to work in them: 'she returns their gaze', 'the frogsong resumes its rhythm', 'A comfortable silence returns', 'Tamstan returns to his feet', 'until you return', 'before returning to your face', 'Dynn turns back toward you and Calsa', 'You turn back to face', 'turns back toward the room, waiting for a decision', and 'the clerk continues his work', which is about someone else. What limits the finding: frame_test.py 64-65 pins that a frame sending them back to their work 'is sent back', so for the true hits the second call is the chosen design (f347) and only the false alarms are a defect; dropping the sentence keeps what f347 wants but changes the mechanism that test names.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/contracts.py 1282-1325 and tools/sim/frame_test.py 56-70. Printed all 71 logged answers with the sentence that hit, the number of sentences in `after`, today's pattern on each and what the next try returned (work/sk_logs_sendbacks_1/btw.py, lost.py).

## logs-fields-5: A hire's detail weights are thrown away for one hire in three: the model gives seven (five details and two secrets) and the contract keeps only a list of five

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `llm/contracts.py:2200`. **Same place:** llm-checks-14
- **Evidence:** llm/contracts.py:2199-2200 `w = [str(x or '').lower().strip() for x in (self.weights or [])]` / `self.weights = w if len(w) == len(self.details) and all(x in ('light', 'personal', 'heavy') for x in w) else []`; the field is `weights: list[str] = []` (:2193), free in the grammar. data/rules/quirks.yaml:456 'Last, give each detail as you wrote it a weight' follows the two secrets. Record: 172 persona_details answers (141 play, 31 live check): weights kept in 114, dropped in 58; 57 of the 58 are seven weights for five details and two secrets. Every one of the 821 values in the play record was light, personal or heavy.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A hire signs on and their details are written once (scenes/quirk_actions.py:75). The model weighs the secrets too, the count is seven, the list becomes [], and engine/gravity.py:34-36 falls back to the weight of the subject each detail was written to, for good: the prompt's own rule ('a regret about a broken plate is light') is not applied to that hire. About 17 tokens (0.55 s on the 3060) are written and dropped each time.
- **Fix:** Hold the list in the grammar: weights as a list of light, personal, heavy with exactly five items (Literal items with min_length = max_length = 5, the form many_reply already uses at contracts.py:2349-2350, so no new helper is needed). I built it: llm/gbnf.py gives weights ::= '[' item (',' item){4,4} ']' with the three words as the only items. The model is then stopped after the five details' weights, which in every seven-long answer of the record come first. The schema changes, so a rebless of its own.
- **The finder's first fix:** Hold the list in the grammar, since the engine knows both the set and the count: items an enum of light, personal, heavy with minItems = maxItems = 5 (llm/gbnf.py reads both), through one helper for 'a list as long as a count the engine knows' that other contracts can use. Cutting a seven-long list to its first five would assume the order and is not the fix.
- **The check:** Seen: the script printed 'seven weights kept: []' with the five details and two secrets intact, and for a member whose four rolled subjects are heavy, gravity.of_detail gave personal, heavy, heavy, heavy, heavy after the seven-long answer against personal, light, personal, light, light after a five-long one. There is no way out on the path: quirk_actions.py:83-84 stores the weights only when the list survived, and nothing writes detail_weights afterwards. Record, accepted answers only: on the game's own prompt (the record's system text is today's, 141 of 141) 52 of 131 carried seven weights, two in five, in every run folder whatever the sampling. The live check's 30 answers use a different, shorter system prompt and should not be pooled (1 of 30), so 'one in three' understates it. In all 53 seven-long answers the last two are heavy, heavy: the secrets. The fallback is not close to the judgement: in the five-long answers the judged weight differs from the subject's for 272 of 540 details, in the first five of the dropped lists for 148 of 265, and every one of the 53 hires has at least one detail weighted otherwise than the model judged. tools/sim/gravity_test.py:163 pins that a wrong value drops the list; nothing pins the count. The effect is which details a hire raises unasked and when (engine/gravity.py choose, heavy_allowed), not a wrong number or a crash.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/contracts.py:2189-2228, scenes/quirk_actions.py:57-90, engine/gravity.py:31-47, engine/quirks.py:664-702, data/rules/quirks.yaml:447-459 and tools/sim/gravity_test.py:159-163. Ran my own CPU-only script (audit/work/sk_lf1_code.py; no campaign, no model): PersonaDetails.model_validate with five details, two secrets and seven weights, then gravity.of_detail on the member. Recounted the record by accepted answers and by run folder (sk_lf1_measure.py, sk_lf1_weights.py, sk_lf1_weights2.py) and built the proposed grammar with llm/gbnf.py.

## min-card-1: A retry is never asked of the budget: every try after the first, and the looser last pass, is handed at least the 8 s floor however far over the turn already is

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium (first given as high). **Place:** `llm/gateway.py:239`
- **Evidence:** llm/gateway.py:184 `budget.allow(task, _chars(system, user))` is asked once, before the loop; :239 `for attempt in range(retries + 1):` and :243 `limit = budget.deadline()` ask nothing; engine/budget.py:185 `return max(self.floor, self.remaining())`. Run on the game's own gateway with a stand-in source (audit/work/min_card_budget_gaps.py): 'with 8.1 s left, one required call made 5 tries; limits handed: 8.1, 8.0, 8.0, 8.0, 8.0; the budget's own count after them: 101.1 s spent of 55; refused: []'.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A line that is legal and has no runaway in it: a first arrival and a first talk price at 47.5 s on the minimum card at each task's recorded median; the reply is rejected and tried again (510 of the 11,125 recorded calls are retries, on 424 of 2,620 lines), then the looser pass runs (2 more tries): 67.5 s on the budget's own arithmetic, nothing refused until the next call's first try. In the 44 tracked runs priced at the profile's rates, 12 retries began with under the 8 s floor left (98 s between them) and 39 lines' count passed 55 s; one line reached 62.2 s to its last required call on narrate's third try alone (prose_a1/both/play_hunter_107, turn 27). An estimate, not a 3060 measure.
- **Fix:** Ask by the rule the first try is asked by, so every task and both loops are covered: before each later try and before the relaxed pass call the Budget's own allow() (the method itself, not the verdict f675 keeps for an operation's first ask). A required task under the floor then raises BudgetSpent and an optional one Deferred or Dropped by its row in budget.yaml, and each site takes the budget path it already has and already tests (a passage told by a stand-in, a reply's line not taken, an exchange queued for a later turn), with the turn log naming the budget. Keep the tally of the rejected draft. A recording made before the change must replay as recorded: a meta switch, as f538 did with budget_cached. Test on narrate (the stand-in), on an optional deferred task (exchange) and on the relaxed pass of a reply. Worth weighing with it: before a speaker's reply is given up for the budget, check the draft in hand again under relaxed_context (no model call) and keep it if it passes, so a reply refused only by a style guard is not lost.
- **The finder's first fix:** Ask the budget before every try after the first and before the relaxed pass, in the gateway's one loop so every task is covered: a required task's next try is refused when what is left is under the floor (the tries end with the last reason, as a reason given twice already ends them), an optional one's when its estimate no longer fits. f714's room_for_passage check at gateway.py:359 is the pattern; test it on a task other than the reply.
- **The check:** The quotes are there: gateway.py:184 asks budget.allow once, :239 the loop and :243 limit = budget.deadline() ask nothing, :198 the relaxed pass calls _generate with no ask, budget.py:185 returns max(self.floor, self.remaining()). My script printed: '1a required, 8.1 s left, every answer rejected, relaxed pass: tries=5 limits=[8.1, 8.0, 8.0, 8.0, 8.0] ... spent=101.1 remaining=-46.1 refused=[]'; with 7.9 s left the first try is refused (BudgetSpent, tries=0); an optional dialogue_frame begun with 29.7 s left made 3 tries and ended at -2.9 s. Nothing prevents it and no test pins it: budget_468_test.py pins only that a rejected draft is charged twice. budget.py's docstring and the f468 commit state 'allow() before a call's first attempt' as the design, and decision 9 is about the charge, so it is a gap in the design and not a slip; f714 (gateway.py:359) already makes one send-back wait on the budget. The record agrees: 510 retries on 424 of 2,620 lines as reported; by my reckoning of the budget's count 13 required retries (narrate 10, npc_conversation 2, road_event 1) began with under 8 s left, 111 s between them (the finder: 12 and 98 s). A retry prices at 4.5 s at the median and 453 of the 510 fit inside the 8 s floor, so on the minimum card they would be made, not cut. Why medium and not high: the reach is small and bounded. Those retries made 13 lines about 8 s longer; to the last required call 3 of those lines were over 60 s as recorded (70.0, 62.2, 61.3 s) and 1 still is with the retries left out (63.5 s); all three are in prose_a1/both, a sampling arm that was not kept. On the shipped sampling the 5 affected lines ended at 52 to 57 s, inside the limit only because of the 5 s margin. The worst the code allows is 4 more tries of 8 s each, about 87 s. The 47.5 s first-arrival example I did not re-derive.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/gateway.py generate() and _generate() and engine/budget.py end to end; wrote and ran audit/work/skeptic_mc1_budget.py (the game's own gateway and budget with a simlib.stand_in source, no model, no campaign); re-ran the finder's min_card_budget_gaps.py; searched tools/sim, GOALS.md and docs/design for anything that pins or records a retry made past the budget; recounted the 44 tracked runs with audit/work/skeptic_mc1_recount.py and skeptic_mc1_late.py.
- **Already recorded:** engine/budget.py's docstring (line 8) and the f468 commit state it as the design: allow() before a call's first attempt, every attempt charged ('decision 9', whose text is in the rebuild plan outside the repo). GOALS.md line 206 records the deadline 'from what is left'. Nothing in GOALS.md or docs/design says a retry is not asked.

## aged-save-1: Every answer a contract refuses pins the whole stack of its turn in memory for the rest of the sitting

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `llm/gateway.py:384`. **Same place:** llm-checks-8
- **Evidence:** llm/gateway.py:383-384 `except ValidationError as e:` / `last_error = e` (kept past the except block; :403 `raise err from last_error`). scratchpad/audit/work/aged_save/leak_check.py, the game's gateway under the stub: one answer refused by a validator's ValueError and the second taken leaves an object held in the calling frame 'STILL ALIVE after gc.collect()', 40 of 40 calls; with pydantic's own type error, broken JSON or a plain exception kept the same way it is freed. In play (3,000 stubbed lines, warrior, seed 7): 496 exceptions, 2,744 frames and 161 frames of WorldScene.play alive after a collection; the process at 223 MB against 104 MB for the same play with the tracebacks let go after each line (77 MB new; 358 MB at 6,000 lines).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** pydantic-core's ValidationError holds the validator's ValueError where Python's collector cannot see it (gc.get_referrers of that ValueError returns nothing), so the cycle the local makes (the error, its traceback, _generate's frame, last_error) is never collected, and the ValueError's traceback keeps every frame above the validator, up to the line's own, with what they hold: the decoded world state, the operation's snapshot of the dice, the copies of the people here. It happens at every refused answer, whether the retry is taken or not (llm/contracts.py raises ValueError in 160 places). Under the stub 2% of first tries are refused and the process grows 4.0 to 4.7 MB a hundred lines, 0.72 MB a refused answer; the measured baseline's first tries on speech tasks are refused 2 to 14% of the time (data/measured/bundle_d_baseline.yaml), so real play pins at least as often. One sitting only (closing the game frees it), and line time did not change when the tracebacks were let go; a night's bot run or a long sitting carries it.
- **Fix:** The finder's fix is right and I ran it: in the except branch set `reason = _summarize(e)` and then `last_error = LLMError(reason)`, so every task is covered at the one place all calls pass. For the test, beside the single call (a marked object held by the caller is collected after a refused first answer), add the guard for the whole class: after a stubbed play of a few hundred lines, gc.collect() leaves no ValidationError alive, which also catches any later site that keeps one.
- **The finder's first fix:** In _generate keep the refusal's words and let the exception go: after `reason = _summarize(e)` set `last_error = LLMError(reason)`, as line 381 already does for the gateway's own checks, so the final error still says why and every task is covered at the one place all calls pass. Its test in tools/sim: after a call whose first answer a contract refused, a marked object held by the caller is collected (leak_check.py's mended shape is freed).
- **The check:** It happens. leak_mine.py printed for 'first refused by a contract, second taken': before gc (ALIVE, ALIVE), after gc (ALIVE, ALIVE); forty such calls: 40 of 40 marked objects alive; gc.garbage 0; the ValueError inside the ValidationError has no referrer the collector can see. With the mend the same case is freed before any collection, 0 of 40 alive, and the final error still says why (cause LLMError('text: say it another way')). In play, as the code is: exceptions alive after a collection 51 / 87 / 201 / 318 / 411 / 496 at lines 500 to 3,000 (165 of them ValidationErrors), 2,905 frames, process 226 MB. The same play with the mend (same day, level and save size at every checkpoint): 0 exceptions, 0 frames, 103 MB. 123 MB over 165 refusals is 0.75 MB each. Nothing prevents it: gateway.py:383 is the only `except ValidationError` on the model's path, llm/contracts.py raises ValueError 160 times, and no tracked code or test reads a ValidationError from __cause__ (the tests that read __cause__ check transport errors). Reach, from the real records (matched by the wording of contracts.py's own messages, so an estimate): the tracked prose runs hold about 680 contract refusals in 2,664 turns (0.26 a turn), about 530 of them the night bot's own player_line and about 150 the game's tasks (0.06 a turn, the stub play's own rate); the played session of 42 lines has none (its three refusals came by the gateway's own checks, which already keep only the words). So a person's sitting of a few hundred lines pins tens of megabytes at most, and a night's bot run some hundreds: real and unbounded within a sitting, never a crash. Two small corrections: the existing `last_error = LLMError(reason)` is line 382, not 381; and the finder's own figures stand otherwise.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/gateway.py _generate (217-403). Wrote my own check, C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_aged_save_1/leak_mine.py: the game's gateway under simlib's stub, a marked object in the caller's frame and another two frames up, weak references, gc.collect(); then the proposed mend tried on a copy of _generate patched in memory. Then played 3,000 stubbed lines twice (C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_aged_save_1/aged_run.py: the finder's play under campaign audit_check_aged-save_1 with my own counters, the save removed in finally), once as the code is and once with the mend in memory. Searched tracked code for every `except ValidationError` and every reader of __cause__. Counted contract refusals in the real records (C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_aged_save_1/real_pins.py: the played session and the 44 tracked prose runs).

## trace-threads-3: Embedding requests never carry the turn's deadline: a stalled embedder holds the turn for the full 120 s hang guard, then embeddings are off for the session

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `llm/llama.py:435`
- **Evidence:** status, payload, wall_ms, _ = self.embed_server.request("POST", "/v1/embeddings", embed_body(texts), None, flag)
llm/llama.py:241  limit = float(self.no_deadline or config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT) if deadline is None else float(deadline)
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The embedder's process is alive but not answering (the runtime restarts only a dead child, llm/runtime.py:1013). The turn's first embed waits config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT, 120 s, twice the 60 s turn target; llm/embed.py:75-80 then marks the embedder failed and every later lookup this session goes without vectors. A chat call on the owner's thread in the same position is cut at the budget's deadline. Traced in code; not seen in a run, so how often it happens is unknown.
- **Fix:** In LlamaServer.embed pass a limit instead of None: budget.deadline() when the calling thread owns an open budget, else a short embed limit kept with the server's numbers in data/runtime. Where budget.deadline() is None because the machine is below the minimum (f526), keep the hang guard, as the owner decided for slow machines. Worth adding: treat a deadline on the embedder as embed_call treats a dead one (stop it and start it once more) before embeddings go off for the session.
- **The finder's first fix:** Give the embed request a limit: the turn's budget.deadline() on the owner's thread, else a short embed limit kept with the other server numbers in data/runtime, so a stalled embedder costs seconds and not two minutes.
- **The check:** Printed: 'config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT in the tree: 120', 'budget.deadline() on the turn's thread: 2.0', 'chat with the turn's deadline: Failure(deadline) after 2.0 s', 'embed.vectors on the turn's thread: None after 6.1 s (hang guard set to 6 s, budget deadline 2.0 s)', 'embed.failed(): True | embed.available() after: False', 'the next lookup: None after 0.00 s'. So the embed waits for the hang guard whatever the budget says (120 s in the tree; the slow machine's hang_seconds below the minimum card), a deadline failure is not 'unreachable' so runtime.embed_call does not restart the embedder, and llm/embed.py:75-78 turns embeddings off for the session. Embeds are on the turn's path: 106 calls in 39 of the 42 typed lines of the played run (2.04 s in all). Not shown: that an embedder ever stalls while alive; none did in the run, so how often is unknown, and it is paid once a session.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/llama.py:236-257 and 429-444, llm/runtime.py:824-857, llm/embed.py:55-81, engine/budget.py:261-267 and llm/gateway.py:243-248 (a chat call is handed budget.deadline()). Searched tools/sim for a test that pins an embed without a limit: only load_and_slow_526_test.py:195 pins the hang guard for a machine below the minimum. Ran scratchpad/audit/work/check_trace_threads_3_embed.py: a plain local socket that accepts and never answers stands in for the embedder (no model, no llama-server), the hang guard set to 6 s for the check, the turn's budget opened with 2 s left. Counted embeds in the played run's turns.jsonl.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/17_multiplayer_survey_and_plan.md line 130 lists 'One failed embedding turns embeddings off for everyone' as a multiplayer item; the wait of the full hang guard is not written anywhere.

## llm2-2: An embed call has no turn deadline: a stalled embedder holds the turn for 120 seconds

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `llm/llama.py:435`. **Same place:** leftovers-6
- **Evidence:** llama.py:435 `status, payload, wall_ms, _ = self.embed_server.request('POST', '/v1/embeddings', embed_body(texts), None, flag)`; llama.py:241 `limit = float(self.no_deadline or config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT) if deadline is None else float(deadline)`; config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 120. backend.embed(texts) and llm/embed.py vectors() carry no deadline, while every chat try is given budget.deadline().
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The played session made 106 embed calls in 42 typed lines (up to 7 in one turn), about 20 ms each. If the embedder's server stops answering (hung, or starved of card memory), an embed inside a turn waits the full 120 s before it fails as 'deadline', far past the 60 second turn, and llm/embed.py then turns embeddings off for the session. Runtime.embed_call (runtime.py:845-847) also restarts a dead embedder inside the calling turn, waiting up to server.start_seconds plus a 60 s warm-up.
- **Fix:** Give embed a limit through the interface: backend.embed(texts, deadline=None) handed down to every source (LlamaServer.embed, Runtime.embed_call, StandIn, the replayer), with llm/embed.py passing budget.deadline() inside a turn, or a short embed limit kept in data/runtime/server.yaml; never in the recorder's request. With it, llm/embed.py must treat a 'deadline' as that call's own fallback (as it treats too_big) and turn embeddings off only after a set number in a row, or one slow answer under a tight turn limit would cost the session its embeddings. Keep the restart inside the call (the pinned behaviour) but bound its wait by the same limit instead of start_seconds plus 60 s; moving it off the turn's thread, as proposed, would need embed.py to tell 'not yet' from 'off', which the f524 review comment at runtime.py:829-831 warns about. Test it with a fake embedder that accepts and holds.
- **The finder's first fix:** Give embed the turn's limit: pass budget.deadline() (or a short embed limit kept in data/runtime/server.yaml) through backend.embed to Server.request, and start a dead embedder again off the turn's thread while this call takes its fallback.
- **The check:** The script printed: 'shipped config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 120', 'the turn's deadline for a chat try now: 2.0', 'embed.vectors returned None after 3.0 s (the hang guard's 3 s, not the turn's 2.0 s)', 'embeddings off for the session now: True | available: False', 'a chat try on the same stalled server ended after 2.0 s: Failure deadline'. So llama.py:435 passes None, line 241 turns that into config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT (120 shipped; hang_seconds on a machine below the minimum), and backend.embed has no deadline to pass. GOALS.md's 60 second rule counts 'the embed calls those need' in the required path. Two limits on reach: the stalled embedder is a fault the played run never showed (106 embeds, 2.04 s in all), and it can happen once a session, because llm/embed.py turns embeddings off on any failure but too_big. The second half of the scenario is by design, not a defect: the restart inside the call (runtime.py:845-847) is what tools/sim/embed_review_524_test.py pins ('two calls on one dead embedder start one new one, and both are answered'), the same as the chat server's restart inside chat_call.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/llama.py Server.request and LlamaServer.embed, llm/backend.py embed, llm/embed.py vectors, llm/runtime.py embed_call and _start_embed, engine/budget.py deadline, config.py. Ran audit/work/v_llm2_2_embed_deadline.py: a LlamaServer whose embed Server points at a plain socket that accepts and never answers (no model, no llama-server), a budget open with 2 s left, config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT set to 3 for the run. Searched tools/sim for REQUEST_TIMEOUT and no_deadline: nothing pins an embed without a limit as intended.

## shell1-8: In the built game crash.log, refusals.jsonl and the audit log land inside _internal, not in the logs folder the player is pointed to

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `main.py:194`
- **Evidence:** main.py:194 `console.out(f"(For a bug report, see logs/llm_calls.jsonl and logs/crash.log: {e})")`. engine/crashlog.py:19,26 `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` / `return ROOT / getattr(config, "CRASH_LOG_PATH", "logs/crash.log")`; the same anchor in engine/refusals.py:25,37 and llm/audit.py:21,45. The turn, call, session and pulse logs use a path relative to the working folder, which main.py:25 sets to paths.APP.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** build_exe.bat builds --onedir with an unpinned PyInstaller (6.x): a frozen module's __file__ is under sys._MEIPASS, the _internal folder, so these three are written to Meravia\_internal\logs\ while the rest are in Meravia\logs\. A tester who sends the logs folder sends no crash.log, the file f449 added so the next upload carries the fault. Read from the code and PyInstaller's documented __file__; not run in a build.
- **Fix:** One helper in core/paths (for example log_path(relative) that joins onto paths.APP at call time, and returns an absolute path unchanged so nightrun's and rerun's overrides keep working), used by crashlog.path(), refusals.note() and audit.path(), and preferably by turnlog, gateway and pulselog too so no log depends on os.chdir. Add to frozen_531_test: with paths reloaded as frozen, crashlog.path(), the refusals path and the audit folder all sit under APP and none under BUNDLE.
- **The finder's first fix:** Anchor the three on core.paths.APP through one helper in core/paths (llm/runtime.py:652 already does this for its own logs), and add the case to tools/sim/frozen_531_test.py.
- **The check:** The three anchor on the module's file: engine/crashlog.py:19,26, engine/refusals.py:25,37, llm/audit.py:21,45. llm/audit.py uses the same ROOT for its data (`ROOT / "data" / "rules" / "audit_log.yaml"`) and its log folder, and build_exe.bat:13 packs data with `--add-data "data;data"`, so in a built game ROOT is the bundle (core/paths.BUNDLE = sys._MEIPASS), not paths.APP; core/paths.py's own docstring says logs/ belongs in APP. With --onedir and PyInstaller 6 the bundle is Meravia\_internal. PyInstaller is unpinned (build_exe.bat:11) and this machine's Python is 3.14.6, which only PyInstaller 6.x supports, so the layout is the _internal one. The other logs are relative to the working folder (engine/turnlog.py:48,240, llm/gateway.py:445, engine/pulselog.py:13), which main.py:25 sets to paths.APP. One thing the finding missed: llm/runtime.py:984-989 writes the model server's notes to paths.APP/logs/crash.log, so a built game can have two crash.log files, the one in logs/ holding server notes only and the turn faults (scenes/world.py:1301,1514,1688) in _internal\logs. No code or test moves the anchor when frozen (frozen_531_test covers core.paths only). With PyInstaller 5 the bundle was the exe's folder and this would not happen.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/crashlog.py, engine/refusals.py, llm/audit.py, core/paths.py, build_exe.bat, requirements.txt, tools/sim/frozen_531_test.py, llm/runtime.py:652 and 984-989, and every other log writer (git grep of the *_LOG_PATH names and of `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`). Traced from the code and from the repository's own packaging; NOT run in a build (no PyInstaller here, and dist/.buildenv are off limits).
- **Already recorded:** Not recorded as a fault. docs/design/11_send_logs_feature.md ('What exists') assumes crash.log, refusals.jsonl and audit/ are in logs/ beside the exe; GOALS.md:207 (f449) says the fault is written to logs/crash.log.

## people-1: Traits and the speech profile are rolled from the same seed, so a person's culture decides which traits they can have

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `npc/life.py:268`
- **Evidence:** life.py:162, 236, 632: `assign_traits(npc, catalog, npc_rng(store.meta.seed, npc.id))`; life.py:268: `return voice_profile.ensure_npc(npc, npc_rng(store.meta.seed, npc.id), world.places[npc.location].region, taken)`. Both start a fresh random.Random(f'{seed}:{npc_id}'), so the first draw of ensure_npc (resident_culture, rng.choices) is the same uniform number that picks the first trait. Measured over 4000 ids (seed 7, Parth's region, 70 traits; scratchpad/audit/work/people_seed_share.py): heartland humans (2802 of 4000) only ever get a first trait from catalogue positions 0..34; rimelands (163) only 34..38, five traits; sunscar 38..42; saltmarches 42..52; frontier 52..63; gloaming 64..69. Dwarves: ironvein 0..14, heartland 14..60, rimelands 60..69. Elves: eldervale 0..16, heartland 16..69. With the speech roll on a seed of its own, every culture spans 0..69. The later draws (second trait against fluency, accent strength, tells) are tied the same way.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Every generated resident in every campaign: all rimelands-born humans share one of the same five first traits, and no heartlander can have a first trait from the back half of the catalogue. Variety of people is narrowed by an accident of seeding, and culture and personality look linked when no data says they are.
- **Fix:** Roll speech on a stream of its own (npc_rng(seed, npc.id + ':speech'), or engine/streams.fixed(seed, npc.id, 'speech')), as ':motive' and ':goal' already are. To cover the class and not this one pair: give npc_rng a required purpose (traits keep the bare seed, so no saved or recorded person's traits move) and add a sim test that fails when two call sites share a purpose. People who already hold npc.speech keep it (ensure_npc only rolls when it is empty); people first spoken to after the change get a different culture and kit, so the goldens go through the rebless process.
- **The finder's first fix:** Give the speech roll its own salted seed, as the motive and goal rolls already have (life.py:208 ':motive', 224 ':goal'): npc_rng(seed, npc.id + ':speech'). People already saved keep their stored speech; new people change, so the goldens go through the rebless process, not a quiet re-record.
- **The check:** data/traits.yaml is ordered by rarity (35 common, 26 uncommon, 9 rare), so the tie is by rarity, stronger than reported. Printed, seed 7, humans in wend_vale: heartland {'common': 2100}; saltmarches {'uncommon': 298}; sunscar {'uncommon': 113}; gloaming {'rare': 49}; frontier {'uncommon': 288, 'rare': 33}; rimelands {'uncommon': 101, 'common': 18}. Seed 12345 gives the same shape. Every gloaming-raised human's first trait is one of vengeful, cold, reclusive, manipulative, haunted, obsessive; no heartlander ever has an uncommon or rare first trait. The second trait is tied to the second speech draw: heartland 'light' people take it from catalogue deciles 0-1 only, 'strong' from deciles 4-6. End to end under the stub: 19 heartland humans all 'common', 6 saltmarches all 'uncommon', the one gloaming human 'rare'.
- **How it was checked:** Read npc/traits.py:72-82 (npc_rng, roll_traits), npc/life.py:162, 236, 268 and engine/voice_profile.py:20-61: the first draw of roll_traits and the first draw of ensure_npc (resident_culture -> _pick) are each one rng.choices on a fresh random.Random(f'{seed}:{npc_id}'), so they read the same number. Re-ran the reporter's script (same figures) and two of my own: scratchpad/audit/work/check_people_1_plain.py (3000 ids through voice_profile.ensure_npc itself, seeds 7 and 12345) and check_people_1_campaign.py (34 people made by life.populate_place under simlib's stub, speech rolled by life.ensure_speech; campaign audit_check_people_1, removed). Searched tools/sim for a test that pins the tie (none: the tests call ensure_npc with their own random.Random) and GOALS.md and docs/design for npc_rng / ensure_speech / resident_culture (nothing).

The first step of every arc is a contact (arcs.pattern), so with an empty pool line 213 evaluates `pool[0 % 0]`. The comprehension at 206 also calls store.npc_names() once per name (16 full reads of the table for one story), which is small. It is an exception inside the accepting operation, not the process: the contract cannot be taken on any turn where the call is deferred or fails, and with a 1200 token answer priced against a 60 second turn on the minimum card that is the usual path. No test covers it. ## scenes1-5: A captive's arc step is matched by node id alone, so another arc's captive answers for, and completes, the current arc's step

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/arc_actions.py:492`
- **Evidence:** arc_actions.py:492 `if (n["kind"] == "contact" and n.get("npc") == npc.id) or (pr and pr.get("node") == n["id"]):` (secret_for) and :826-830 `n = arcs.node(arc, pr["node"]) if arc else None` ... `self.advance_arc(data, arc, n, True, ...)` (drop_prisoner). Node ids are n1..nN in every arc and neither place compares pr["arc"]. Stub run (work/scenes1_check.py): a captive recorded for another arc -> secret_for returned the active arc's node n2; releasing them left that arc `[('n1','contact','done',False), ('n2','boss','done',True)] state active current None`.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A lair leader taken in one arc is still escorted when that arc ends (its deadline fails it). The player takes a new missing-person contract; when its current step has the same id, questioning the old captive gives the new arc's secret, and releasing, killing or handing them over completes that step as a partial. On a boss step this leaves the arc active with no current step: it cannot be finished and it holds the place of the next arc until its own deadline.
- **Fix:** As proposed, plus two guards so the kind cannot recur: one helper that gives a captive's step only when pr['arc'] is the arc in hand, used by secret_for, drop_prisoner and on_hand_over/settle_prisoner's node_pending; clear the captive's node when its clue is given (give_secret, trail_goes_cold) and when its arc ends (finish_arc, fail_arc); and let advance_arc refuse to complete an arc's last step as a partial (the finale ends only through finish_arc), so no arc can be left active with no current step.
- **The finder's first fix:** One helper that returns a captive's node only when `pr["arc"] == arc["id"]`, used by secret_for, drop_prisoner and the secret's aftermath, and clear a captive's node when its arc ends (finish_arc, fail_arc).
- **The check:** Printed: captive `{'arc': '2ab427af', 'node': 'n2'}`; `arc A state: failed`; arc B steps `[('n1','contact','known'), ('n2','boss','hidden')]`; `secret_for(arc A's captive) -> {'kind': 'arc', 'arc': '3a2b8109', 'node': 'n2', ...}` (arc B's secret); after the release `[('n1','contact','done',False), ('n2','boss','done',True)] | state active | current None | quest B progress 0`. One correction to the finding: no contract has a time limit (engine/quests.py:151, f491), so an arc does not end by a deadline and the stuck arc does not clear by one either: arc A ends when the player gives the contract up or wins it, and arc B stays active with no step until the player gives it up. While it stands no new missing-person contract is posted (quests.py:348). The same completion happens with no choice by the player when the captive slips their bonds (arc_tick -> drop_prisoner, partial_node=True). Reach is limited: a lair captive must still be held (escape odds 15% a day rising to 60%) when another arc reaches the step of the same number; after a chain the next arc is a short one (contact n1, finale n2), and a lair is commonly n2.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/arc_actions.py:485-497, 562-586, 590-608, 813-830, 732-759, engine/arcs.py:30-31 and 188-213 (every arc numbers its steps n1..nN; active() is the first active arc), engine/quests.py:147-154 and scenes/guild_actions.py:477. Grep: pr['arc'] is written at make_prisoner and never compared; pr['node'] is never cleared (not by give_secret, finish_arc or fail_arc). Ran verify_scenes1_1.py part 5 with no hand-made record: arc A's lair leader taken alive through camp_battle and CombatScene.finish(), arc A ended by arc_quest_gone, arc B built, its first step done, the captive released.

## scenes1-6: A threat is recorded as a promise of mercy: the captive's deal is read by substring

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/arc_actions.py:507`
- **Evidence:** arc_actions.py:507-508 `if any(w in speech.lower() for w in PR["deal_words"]):` / `pr["deal"] = True`, with data/rules/arcs.yaml:78 `"let you go", "let you live", "won't kill", ... "walk away", "no harm"`. Stub run (work/scenes1_check2.py): "Talk, or I won't let you live." -> deal True; "You will not walk away from this." -> deal True; "I won't let you go until you talk." -> deal True.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player threatens a captive. The engine records a promise to spare them: the captive is told 'They promised to spare you if you talk', the secret opens with no check (line 524 `open_ = (pr and pr["deal"]) or ...`), and if the player then kills them the outlaw reputation takes kill_after_deal and the narrator is told 'They had been promised mercy' (lines 858, 873). A state change and a reputation cost come from a line that said the opposite.
- **Fix:** Prefer the engine reading: one shared reader for 'said, and not denied' per clause (the negation test yield_intercept already has as YIELD_NOT, and scenes/world.py NEGATED and engine/truth.py _NEGATED are two more copies), used for the deal and for the yield, with the phrases staying in data/rules/arcs.yaml; the play-faults plan allows a negation guard over the line when it is named beside the census count. - **The finder's first fix:** Let the promise come from the reading the engine already checks: the reader of the player's line returns an offered-mercy field validated in llm/contracts.py, and the engine sets the deal from that.
