## scenes1-4: One beaten foe counts twice toward a hunt or bounty: once when it yields, again when it is finished or handed to the watch

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/arc_actions.py:799`
- **Evidence:** scenes/combat_scene.py:1108 `ws.tally_foes(yielded)  # (f669) a foe taken alive counts for the contract as one killed`; scenes/arc_actions.py:96 `self.record_kills(foes)` (finish_yielded) and :799-800 `if bounty:` / `bounty["progress"] += 1` (on_hand_over). Stub run (work/scenes1_check2.py): three bandits beaten, one bound -> progress 3, after handing that captive over -> 4; two wolves, one yielded -> 2, after finishing it -> 3.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A contract for six bandits: the player beats three, one of whom yields and is bound, then hands the captive to the watch, and four are counted from three foes. A foe that yields and is then killed on the player's word is counted twice in the same way, so contracts complete early. The second counts predate f669 and were left in when the win began to count the yielded.
- **Fix:** Count a foe once, and settle with the owner where a bound captive counts, because two recorded decisions meet here: review Q28 says a bounty taken alive counts at hand over, and f669 counts every foe taken alive at the win. Either the win tallies only the yielded who are not bound (those count at hand-over or when put to death), or it tallies all and marks the captive's record so on_hand_over and finish_yielded skip the contract count. finish_yielded should keep its CreatureKilled notices and remains but not tally again. Test with a hunt and a bounty, a bound person and a beast that yields.
- **The finder's first fix:** Count a foe once: keep the f669 tally at the win and have finish_yielded and on_hand_over skip the contract count for a foe already tallied (a mark on the fighter and on the captive's record), keeping the rest of record_kills (remains, records) as it is.
- **The check:** Printed: `three bandits beaten (one of them yielded and bound): progress 3 | captives ['prisoner_kell']` then `after handing that captive to the watch: progress 4 (three bandits in all)`; `two wolves beaten (one dead, one yielded and waiting): progress 2` then `after finishing the one that yielded: progress 3 (two wolves in all)`. The win tallies the yielded (combat_scene.py:1108, f669); finish_yielded calls record_kills -> tally_foes again (arc_actions.py:96, guild_actions.py:505); on_hand_over adds one more with no place check (799-800). The effect is one count too many per yielded foe, capped at the contract's count.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/combat_scene.py:1094-1130, scenes/guild_actions.py:496-520, scenes/arc_actions.py:66-109 and 784-811. tools/sim/tally_669_test.py only checks tally_foes([foe]) adds one; parley_test's hand-over checks coin only; nothing pins the second count. Ran verify_scenes1_1.py part 4 through CombatScene.victory(), on_hand_over and yield_intercept.
- **Already recorded:** GOALS.md owner's decisions table: 'A bounty taken alive counts: "at hand over"' (review Q28); docs/design/21_play_faults_plan.md D7 and 'As built (f669)'. Both rules are recorded; that together they count one foe twice is not.

## aged-save-2: Word of Recall is refused in the town reached after any road stop: the stop is remembered as the town behind you and is no longer on the map

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/field_actions.py:919`
- **Evidence:** scenes/field_actions.py:909 `town = pulse.town_of(self.world, place_id)` (a stop has no parent, so it is its own town; :910 passes over dangerous places only) and :919-920 `dest = next((t for t in reversed(self.fld.get("towns", [])) if t != here), None)` / `if not dest or dest not in self.world.places:`. scratchpad/audit/work/aged_save/recall_check.py, one walk under the stub: Parth, a road stop, Willowmead gave towns = [parth, road_0f3254ad, willowmead], the stop off the map, and field_word_of_recall answered "There's no town behind you to return to yet." and returned None.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Any walk between two towns that makes a stop on the road (a camp, a landmark, a meeting: 63 stops in 3,000 lines of the mage's play, 6 in 2,000 of the priest's). In the town the walk ends in, the newest other entry of the list is the stop, which leave_road has taken off the map, so the ability refuses with a line that is false (Parth is behind you) until another town is entered with no stop on the way. journal_data's 'the last one you stood in' (scenes/world.py:2149) reads the same list and gets the stop's id. At 6,000 lines the list held 71 entries in a world of 32 places first visited.
- **Fix:** The finder's fix stands. Make it one rule: a helper for 'this place is a road stop' (type road and no parent, the test pulse.home_town and roads.anchor already repeat) that note_town, the last_in writer in enter() and the standing writer all ask, so a stop is never recorded as a settlement; and when the list is written, drop every id no longer on the map, which mends old saves and caps the list at the number of settlements. Test it on two stops in a row and on a save that already holds stop ids.
- **The finder's first fix:** Do not record a road stop as a settlement: note_town returns for a place of type 'road' (one rule for 'is this a settlement' that the standing and last_in writers use too, see aged-save-9), and both readers skip ids that are no longer on the map, which also mends saves that already hold stops. Test it on a walk with two stops in a row, not only the one that found it.
- **The check:** It happens. Control, Parth then Willowmead with nothing on the road: towns [parth, willowmead], 'The world folds, and you stand in Parth.' With one stop: road_event returned 'stopped', the stop is type road with no parent and danger None, towns [parth, road_fe565141, willowmead], the stop off the map, and the ability answered 'There's no town behind you to return to yet.' and left the player where they stood. Two stops in a row: the same refusal. journal_data's 'last' is the stop's id. In the warrior's 3,000 lines, of the lines spent in a town the ability would have been refused in 23 of 82, 0 of 73, 86 of 91, 76 of 77, 85 of 105 and 2 of 100 (windows of 500); at line 3,000 the list held 19 ids, 14 of them stops, 13 no longer on the map, so it also grows by one for every stop with no cap. Nothing prevents it: no place in data has type road, a stop has no danger so note_town's one test passes it, and the test pins 'returns you to the last town you left', so the refusal is not meant. Limits: a refused use starts no cooldown (field_actions.py:72-73) and no state is damaged; only characters who have the ability meet it.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/field_actions.py 61-74 and 907-930, engine/pulse.py town_of and home_town, scenes/road_actions.py leave_road and road_event (383-397), engine/roads.py make_stop, scenes/world.py enter (785-806) and journal_data (2146-2161), and tools/sim/field_functions_test.py 335-341. Ran my own script, C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_aged_save_1/recall_mine.py (campaign audit_check_aged-save_1, removed in finally): the stops made by the game's own road_event (kind find), walked on from with finish_journey; a control walk with no stop; two stops in a row. In the 3,000-line play I counted, after every line spent in a town, whether the ability would be refused.

## scenes2-2: A yes to a person's request, said where a guild clerk stands, goes to the board and can take an unrelated contract

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/guild_actions.py:397`
- **Evidence:** if npc and not self.clerk_here():
    self.take_personal(npc)
    return
- **What a player or the owner meets:** In a hall with its clerk present, someone else there has asked the acting character for something (an open 'request' obligation). The line is read as accept_quest with target = the asker. Because a clerk is here the personal request is skipped and the words are matched against the board (pick_posting, where one shared word is enough when the line has two content words). Probe (stub, seed 3, clerk and herbalist present, request 'Bring 2 ...' open): 'yes, I will bring it' took the board's 'Bring 2 bear hide' and left the herbalist's request waiting; 'I'll do it, Tam' and 'I accept your request' showed the board and took nothing. A request made by the clerk can never be taken by words at all.
- **Fix:** The proposed fix leans on intent.target, which the reader is not asked to fill for this kind. Decide what a yes means in the engine from what is open here: every open request of someone present (obligations.current) and the board's postings are candidates for one matcher, scored by the words against each title and by who is being answered (the conversation partner or last spoken to, a name in the line, intent.target). The request wins when its asker is the one being answered or the words name no posting; the board wins only when the words name a posting (pick_posting's score or a number) better than they name the request; a tie asks (ask_next). The membership and clerk checks belong to the board branch only. Also declare the target for accept_quest in engine/actions.py so the reader says who was answered. Test with a request open beside a clerk for a member and a non-member, and with the clerk as the asker.
- **The finder's first fix:** Decide by who was addressed, not by whether a clerk is in the room: when intent.target names a present asker with an open request (or the words name no posting and exactly one request is open here), take the personal request; go to the board only otherwise.
- **The check:** Printed, as a rank F member: 'yes, I will bring it' -> holds [('Bring 2 bear hide', 'guild')]; request still waiting: True. "I'll do it, Tam", 'I accept your request' and 'yes' -> the board is shown, nothing taken, request still waiting. 'Yes. I will bring them to you, Tam.' -> "That's a rank-E contract, and you're rank F." As a non-member every one of the five lines -> 'Only guild members can take contracts. Joining costs 3 silver. Ask the clerk.' Control with the clerk out of the room: the same words -> holds [('Bring 2 moonpetal', 'request')], request no longer waiting. A request made by the clerk can be taken only from the pane, by trace (clerk_here() is true whenever they are present).
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/guild_actions.py on_accept_quest (394-456), pick_posting (372-392), clerk_here (69-70), take_personal, board_click (#boardrequest still takes a request from the pane), engine/actions.py:114 (accept_quest is not a targeted kind, so the reader is not told to fill target) and guild.yaml taking_words. git blame: the 'not self.clerk_here()' guard is from the initial commit. Searched tools/sim for on_accept_quest and accept_quest: no test has a request open with a clerk in the room. No other path takes a request on a yes (grep take_personal, request_of). Ran my own script (audit/work/check_scenes2_2_yes.py, removed its campaign): guild_house, a clerk and a herbalist present, the herbalist's request 'Bring 2 moonpetal' open through record_quest_offer, on_accept_quest called with target = the herbalist.

## scenes2-1: A request handed in to the asker: the thanks (trust +5) is written on a second copy of them and then overwritten by the scene's own copy

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/guild_actions.py:648`. **Same place:** scenes2-9
- **Evidence:** stakes.done(self, q)   # guild_actions.py:648
engine/stakes.py:175-180: n = ws.store.load_npc(q["issuer"]) ... regard.step(n, ws.acting, G.get("issuer_thanks_trust", 5), cause="job done", ...) ; ws.store.save_npc(n)
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Any personal request handed in to the person who asked: they stand in ws.present, so the scene holds their record. turn_in moves trust on the held copy (line 626 and the ContractDone reaction), then stakes.done loads a fresh copy from the save (load_npc has no cache), adds the +5 thanks, and saves that. The held copy never has it, and the next save of the held copy (npc/life.py after their reply, or any later reaction) writes the old JSON back. Probe on simlib's stub (seed 7): trust 50, held copy 56, save 61; after the held copy is saved again the save reads 56 and the 'job done' move is gone. The same shape loses a concern set by stakes._concern or settled by stakes._release when a board posting's issuer stands in the scene.
- **Fix:** The proposed fix is right in kind but covers four functions; the fault is a class. turn_in's own obligations.close(..., npc=None) at guild_actions.py:620 loads a third copy the same way. Cover the class in one place: either the store hands back the scene's held record for anyone the scene holds (one live record of a person per session, which is what ws.npc_by_id does by hand), or save_npc refuses a record older than the row it writes over (a revision stamp on load), so the suite finds every remaining stale write instead of one at a time. Until then stakes.done, _release, _concern and taken take ws and reach the person through ws.npc_by_id. Test on two cases: a request handed in to a present asker by a talk turn, read from the save after the reply; and a board posting whose issuer stands in the hall when it is posted and when it is paid.
- **The finder's first fix:** Let stakes.done, _release, _concern and taken reach the person through ws.npc_by_id (the scene's held copy when they are here, as engine/reactions.py does) and load from the store only when they are elsewhere. Test it by handing a request in to a present asker and reading the save after their next reply.
- **The check:** Printed: before: save trust 50. Saves of the asker this turn as (trust written, was it the scene's held copy): [(50, True), (56, True), (61, False), (56, True), (56, True), (57, True), (56, True), (57, True)]. After the turn: held copy 57, save 57; moves in the save [(3, 'paid'), (3, 'deed'), (1, 'talk')], no 'job done'. So stakes.done wrote 61 on a second copy (engine/stakes.py:175-180) and the reply's save of the held copy put 56 back; the save should read 62. The talk hand-in is the ordinary way a request is handed in (scenes/world.py:1549 and 3738), so the +5 thanks is lost every time the reply stands. The second half of the finding (a board issuer's concern set by _concern or settled by _release being written over) has the same load, change, save shape and a guild master issuer does stand in the hall, but I did not show that state arising: that part is plausible, not shown.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/guild_actions.py turn_in (593-653), engine/stakes.py done/_release/_concern/taken, storage/campaign.py load_npc (744-751: a fresh parse each call, no cache), scenes/world.py npc_by_id/notice/operation (a commit saves the player and the talk, never the people held), engine/reactions.py remember (saves the held copy) and npc/life.py converse (458, 503: saves the held copy after the reply). Searched tools/sim: stakes_test.py reads the save straight after turn_in() with the clerk as payer; no test hands a request in to a present asker and reads the save after their reply. Ran my own script (audit/work/check_scenes2_1_thanks.py, campaign audit_check_scenes2_1, removed): one whole talk turn (ws.turn) handing a finished personal request in to the asker standing in present, with a spy on store.save_npc.

## scenes2-4: The answer to the watch is the first choice in menu order with any matching word start: 'fine, take me to jail' pays the fine, 'I won't pay, I run' pays

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/law_actions.py:478`
- **Evidence:** pick = next((k for k in d["keys"] if any(re.search(rf"\b{w}", said) for w in self.WORDS[k])), None)
WORDS = {"pay": ("pay", "fine", "settle", "coin"), ... "bribe": ("bribe", "slip", ...), "jail": ("jail", "cell", "prison", "serve", "time")}
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A guard stops a wanted character and the next typed line answers. The match has no negation, no order of the player's words and no check for two choices named, and it is a word-start match ('payment', 'timely', 'reasonable', 'slippery'). Probe with the game's own table: 'fine, take me to jail' -> pay; 'I slip him a few coins to forget it' -> pay (a bribe was meant); 'I won't pay. I run' -> pay; 'no time for this, I run' -> jail (on the arrest menu). The engine then settles it: coin taken, or days in a cell, that the player did not choose.
- **Fix:** As proposed, with the reader put where the other answers are read: one 'which choice does this answer name' function in engine/questions.py for every question with named choices (the law, the fork, the reforge), whole words, a negated choice dropped (the yes/no reader there already knows 'I do not'), settled only when exactly one choice is left, else asked again through the tries the question has; the words per choice in questions.yaml, without 'fine', 'time' and 'coin'. tools/sim/line_patterns_648_test.py counts the searches over the line per file, so its table moves with the code. Test with lines that name two choices, negate one, or use a choice's word as ordinary speech.
- **The finder's first fix:** Collect every choice the line names (whole words, a negated one dropped); settle only when exactly one is left, else ask again through the tries the question already has. Keep the words in data (questions.yaml) and drop the ones that are ordinary speech ('fine', 'time', 'coin').
- **The check:** End to end on the arrest menu ('Pay the fine, serve time in jail, offer a bribe, or run'): 'Fine, take me to jail.' -> 'You pay 0g 37s 50c' (3750 copper taken, no jail); 'No time for this. I run.' -> 'You serve 2 days and pay 0g 18s 75c'; "I won't pay. I run." -> the fine is paid. By the expression alone: 'I slip him a few coins to forget it' -> pay; 'I will not pay a copper. Take me to the cells.' -> pay; 'I refuse to pay and bolt for the gate' -> pay; "Fine. I'll go quietly." -> pay; on the confront menu "That's a reasonable sum, but I'd rather talk" matches 'reason'.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/law_actions.py 464-530 (the quote is exact; settle takes the fine or serves time), scenes/world.py ask_next and take_line (2289-2380: the next typed line goes straight to on_answer_law, before the interpreter, no model reads it) and data/rules/questions.yaml (yes/no words only; the law's words are in code). tools/sim/law_test.py answers only with single plain words ('pay', 'I pay the fine', 'talk', 'bribe', 'jail', 'run'); nothing pins the misreadings. Ran audit/work/check_scenes2_3_coin.py (the game's own expression over LawActions.WORDS) and audit/work/check_scenes2_4_law.py (an arrest, then ws.handle(line); campaign removed).
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/21_play_faults_plan.md, theme B ('A typed line is read for what it asks, not for a word in it') and B2 ('An answer to the game's own question is read against that question', built as f658 for the clarify answer only); tools/sim/line_patterns_648_test.py lists scenes/law_actions.py:on_answer_law in its census of places a pattern reads the line. The law answer's own misreadings are not written down.

## typed-patterns-1: The hire's follow-up is the reader wrong most often: after a hire speaks, the next line goes to them as chat unless it opens like an action, whoever the player was talking with

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/party_actions.py:474`
- **Evidence:** hire_followup 474: `if self.action_line(text) or any(self.npc_addressed(text, n) for n in self.present) or self.not_to_them(text, last[0]):` / `return None`; nothing reads self.partner. 501: `TOWARD = re.compile(r"\b(?:to|toward|towards|for|into)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?P<rest>.*)")`: `.*` takes the rest of the line, so finditer tests only the first to/for/into. PROPOSAL (365) is anchored at the line's start.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Measured on the 1,888 logged lines with their logged plan, a hire set as having spoken the turn before (work/tp/bench_run.py hl): 178 lines (9.4%) are taken by the hire intercept and never read; the model had read 9 as a talk to a hire and 169 otherwise (127 a talk to someone else here, 116 of them the person the player was already talking with; 22 a parting; 9 a walk; 2 a purchase; 2 a quest taken). In the old runs 86 of 2,759 typed lines went to a hire as chat; of the 77 distinct ones, 38 still do today at Parth's square and at least 16 of those are a step or a deed. Stub runs (work/tp/dbg_goes.py, dbg_hire.py): 'We need to get to the Adventurers' Guild House before we do anything else.' (the first 'to' is 'need to'), 'Parth is our priority; let's move out.', 'We need to reach Riverhaven before the light fails completely.', 'I don't have time for mercy; I finish off the lizardfolk.' and, with the chandler as conversation partner, 'Six copper a bundle seems fair; tell me, have you noticed anything unusual in the market lately?' are all answered by the hire: no walk, no kill, no purchase. A hire had spoken the turn before on 497 of 2,175 lines typed with a party in the old runs.
- **Fix:** The direction is right and is doc 26's 5.1 part 4, but doc 29 leaves it out of the contained half (after parts 1 to 3), so until then the lines go into the corpus with not_by: [hire], in more wordings than the five found. Two notes. (1) goes_to_place's one-match fault is a plain bug in f708's own rule and can be fixed now with no word list: test the words after every to / toward / for / into. In memory this kept the 18 follow-up lines hire_goes_708_test pins and sent 3 of 5 new lines to the reader; 'we need to reach <town> now' and 'let's move out' still went to the hire, which is why no pattern finishes this. (2) The offer costs an interpreter call on every reply to a hire that costs none today (the hire is already passed as last spoken to at scenes/world.py 3232-3234), so it is kept only by doc 29's measure of calls and seconds a turn.
- **The finder's first fix:** Not another round on its word lists (f290, f384, f386, f708 were four): the follow-up stops being a taking. When a hire spoke last, that hire is offered to the interpreter as the likely addressee and the plan's talk.target decides; hire_followup, not_to_them, goes_to_place and party_proposal as guards go with it. The real lines above become corpus cases with not_by: [hire].
- **The check:** The code is as quoted: 474-476 test action_line, npc_addressed and not_to_them and nothing else; TOWARD (501) ends in (?P<rest>.*), so finditer gives one match a line; PROPOSAL (365) opens with ^\W*. My bench run at Parth's trading square, a hire set as having spoken the turn before and a chandler present: all five lines of the report were handled by 'hire' (hire=['Gorz Skorgarth']), with the chandler as conversation partner and without; the same five with no hire having spoken went to the interpreter. For 'We need to get to the Adventurers' Guild House before...' TOWARD tested one stretch only ("get to the adventurers' guild ..."). The state arises without the bench's shortcut: a row added to the hire's `said` between hire_said_marks and note_hire_spoke (what a remark in the tail does) left _hire_last at (hire, turn-1) with ws.partner still the chandler, and hire_followup returned the hire for the chandler's line. Counts I re-read: 178 of 1,888 lines taken by the hire in the hire-spoke-last replay, 9 of them read by the model as a talk to a hire only; 86 lines of the old runs went to hire_chat with no interpreter call, 38 of the 77 distinct still go to the hire today, and by my reading at least 16 of those are a walk or a deed. Limits: the 9.4% holds only for lines typed after a hire spoke (my rough count: hire_chat ran the turn before on 481 of 2,647 turn pairs; the report's 497 of 2,175 I did not re-count exactly); in a fight, or with a yielded foe waiting, the hire intercept is not reached, so 'I finish off the lizardfolk' is taken only outside one. The tests pin only the bare case (a question after the hire spoke, nobody else in talk); the docstring's 'not for a stranger by the pillar' shows that taking a reply past bystanders is meant, but nothing pins taking a line from the person the player is talking with.

## task-failures-4: A once-only writing that fails on the model is never asked again: a hire keeps no details or secrets, an arc its plain story, a companion's own words go unread

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/quirk_actions.py:58`. **Same place:** llm-rest-5
- **Evidence:** scenes/quirk_actions.py:58 `m["details"] = []    # set first, so a failure is not retried on every line`; :88-89 `if isinstance(e, budget.Deferred):` `self.defer("persona", {"member": m["id"]})`: only the budget's deferral is queued. scenes/arc_actions.py:178-182 the same (plain is set only under Deferred, and redress_arc returns unless plain). engine/canon.py:566-567 `except LLMError:` `return {}`. Runs: party with persona_details failing (each way): all three hires end with 0 details and 0 secrets (baseline 5 and 2 each); with canon_extract failing the page is the same ('...that much I promise.') and the players table differs: the claim and the promise are not kept.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** One refused, cut off or oversized answer, or a moment without the server, at the first line that touches a new companion: for the rest of the campaign they have nothing of their own to talk about and no secrets. The same for an arc's story (plain for good; by reading) and for what a companion says of themselves in a reply that stood (never read again, so a later reply can contradict it). The queue that would try again exists (scenes/world.py:1627 defer, 1636 run_deferred) and already knows 'persona' and 'arc'.
- **Fix:** As proposed, with one correction: the queue drops an entry older than retention.deferred_turns (3 lines), so an outage longer than that would lose the retry again. Give a model failure its own count of tries in the entry (a number in data/rules/budget.yaml), each try restarting its age, and let it go only when the tries are spent; the queue stays capped. For the canon reading queued after the fact, keep only the claims that do not contradict what is known (the line has been shown and cannot be written again). Mark an arc plain on any failure so redress_arc can take it up.
- **The finder's first fix:** One rule where the queue already is: a once-only optional writing that fails for any reason goes on the deferred queue, with a tries count beside its age so a call that always fails is let go, and the canon reading of a line that stood becomes a queued kind of its own (speaker and line). No new store: the queue is capped by retention.deferred_turns.
- **The check:** Seen: with PersonaDetails failing on the first line, both hires end with details [] and no secrets, the deferred queue empty; over the next six lines PersonaDetails is called 0 times and they stay at 0 details and 0 secrets (a hire that succeeds gets 5 and 2). The key is set before the call (quirk_actions.py:58) and only budget.Deferred is queued (:88-89). Canon: with the extract failing the reply stands (fix ''), known stays 0 and nothing is queued; with it answering the same reply adds 'I grew up on a herring boat.'. By reading: canon_extract is named required in budget.yaml yet its one site swallows every LLMError (canon.py:566), BudgetSpent among them, so a spent budget drops the reading too; an arc dressed plain on a model failure has no 'plain' mark (arc_actions.py:178-182) and redress_arc returns without it. It has happened in the tracked record: in docs/measure/prose_a2/play_hunter_107 the details of the hire Tamstan Oxlow were refused by the validator on both tries at turn 2 ('write exactly five details, one sentence each ...') and were not asked for again in the run's 54 typed lines, while the two other hires got theirs at turns 3 and 4 (one hire in the 45 runs, 143 persona rows). The arc's plain story is a working fallback, so that part is the weakest of the three.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/quirk_actions.py:51-90, scenes/world.py:1627-1673 (defer, run_deferred, run_deferred_one), scenes/arc_actions.py:160-202, engine/canon.py:554-587 and 652-672, scenes/party_actions.py:781-817, engine/budget.py:93-112, data/rules/budget.yaml. Ran work/tf1_f45_companion.py (two hires, PersonaDetails failing at the first line that touches them, then six more lines with the model answering) and work/tf1_f4_canon.py (canon.read and canon.settle called as hire_talk calls them, the Extracted call failing and not). The arc part is by reading only. No test pins 'never asked again' (quirk_test pins only that a success is written once).
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/20_phase3_plan.md:394 and docs/design/23_untold_after_walks.md:21 describe the deferred queue as the budget's (banter, persona and arc work). That a model failure never enters it is not written down. First round llm-rest-5 (scenes/quirk_actions.py:59) is about when the details are written, not this.

## scenes3-3: A pending errand holds the hire's dict by reference: after any operation that does not stand (or a reload) the answer is paid for and the hire never hears it

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/quirk_actions.py:397`
- **Evidence:** `self._errand = (m, E)` (line 397) keeps the member dict itself; errand_intercept (lines 426-433) spends `c.coins -= E["cost"]` on the live character but writes `m["quirks"]["errand"] = "yes"`, `m["bond"] = ... + 3` and rules.remember(m, ...) on that dict. give_back (scenes/world.py:1606-1608) puts back deep copies of the scene's `_` attributes and reloads self.player, so m is no longer in the party. Ran ..scratchpad/audit/work/scenes3_errand.py: control -> coins paid 300, errand 'yes', bond 38; with one operation that did not stand between the ask and the yes -> coins paid 300, live hire errand '', bond 35, quirks.errand(live) still offers it. `_errand` is not in the save either: a game closed after the ask loses it while errand_day and the open obligation stay.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A companion asks for an advance as the player arrives. In the same turn a situation is born (situation_births stands down to ask the model, an ordinary rollback), or a pane click's operation fails. The player says yes: 3 silver and the time are spent, the companion's trust and memory do not change, and they ask for the same thing another day.
- **Fix:** Better than a new saved field: the pending ask is already in the save. errands() opens an errand obligation (obligations.open_, holder hire:<id>, with self.acting) in the same transaction as the ask. Make that row the one record of a pending errand: errand_intercept and obligations.lapse read obligations.current(store, 'errand', who=self.acting), find the member by id in the acting character's live party when the answer comes, and take the errand from quirks.Q['errands'][the member's motive] (terms['errand'] is always '' today, because no errand row has a `kind` key); drop `_errand`. No new store, already capped by obligations.trim, and it holds across rollbacks, stand-downs, a reloaded record and a closed game. ask_next with on_answer_<kind> (f460) is the other existing way and would do as well.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the pending errand as data: the hire's id and the errand's kind in the acting character's saved record, the member looked up from the live party when the answer comes. That covers rollbacks and reloads for every errand, and keeps the store to one entry.
- **The check:** Printed. On arriving the hire says 'An advance on my pay, 3 silver. I'd rather not say what for.' Control (nothing between): the pending member is the party's own dict; yes -> coins paid 300, errand 'yes', bond 38, one memory, the save the same. An operation that failed between: the pending member is no longer the party's dict; yes -> coins paid 300, live and saved errand '', bond 35, no memory, quirks.errand still offers it. An ordinary restartable operation that stood down once to ask the model and then committed (no failure at all): the same result. Two things detach it, both read: engine/session.py rollback puts every `_` attribute back from the deep copy taken as the operation opened (202-204), and asked_operation puts the player's fields back from a deep copy (world.py 1483-1485), so the party's dicts are new objects either way. Not shown: how often an operation falls between the tail's ask and the next line in play; in the plain arrival turn of my control none did. What can fall there, by reading: a passage told after the tail (1889), take_up_rulings and situation_births (1891-1892; a town's birth is due on arriving, which is when errands are asked), the next line's take_up_acts (1815), a pane command, and anything that replaces the record (run_pulse 690, arc_actions.py 822). The reload half is as claimed by reading: `_errand` is not saved, lapse closes the open ask as no_answer on the next line, and the hire asks again another day.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/quirk_actions.py 103-113 and 381-456, engine/session.py begin_turn and rollback (150-210), scenes/world.py asked_operation (1452-1499), give_back (1597-1625), turn (1799-1895), run_pulse (682-704), engine/obligations.py lapse (105-118), data/rules/quirks.yaml errands. Ran my own script with every line through WorldScene.turn (a look, a walk to the guild house so the tail asks the errand, then 'yes, of course'), three ways: C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_scenes3_3_errand.py.

Worse, from the same line 727, and the reason I raise the severity: a night slept at a stop makes it last_rest (world.py 4444; my typed line 'I make camp and sleep until morning.' printed last_rest 'road_9f45b126'). A fight lost there then wakes the player at the stop itself (threshold 291 finds it still on the map) with player.road None. That save opened again: location road_9f45b126 not on the map, ws.place raises KeyError, the first steps of WorldScene.run (open_world, recover_unshown, enter(location)) raise KeyError 'road_9f45b126' with nothing to catch it before main.py's scene.run(), and a typed line returns False with 'That didn't happen. ## scenes3-4: A failed rewrite in voice.fresh throws away the valid draft

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/voice.py:128`. **Same place:** llm-flow-8
- **Evidence:** fresh() lines 127-128: `with gateway.tagged(rewrite_of_draft=why):` / `redo = generate(task, system, request + nudge, schema, ...)` has no handler, so an LLMError from the second call (every attempt refused, a timeout, the budget refusing another call) leaves fresh() although `result`, a draft that passed its contract, is in hand. Ran ..scratchpad/audit/work/scenes3_checks.py part A with voice.generate stubbed (a valid draft holding 'cool morning air', then LLMError): 'LLMError out of fresh() with a valid draft in hand ... calls made: 2'. In the measured session 6 of 26 narrate calls were rewrites and one rewrite attempt (call 110) was itself rejected before its retry passed. The function already keeps the draft when the rewrite loses blow markers (lines 131-133).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A passage's draft trips the stale-phrase or worn-word check late in a slow turn and the rewrite is refused for budget, or fails its attempts. The passage operation fails and the player reads the stand-in line (or a companion's frame is dropped) though a checked passage had been written.
- **Fix:** As proposed: catch LLMError (BudgetError is one) around the rewrite alone, record turnlog.rewrite(task, why, 'draft') and return the draft, as lines 131-133 do for lost markers. NeedAnswer, Drift and Interrupt are BaseException and still pass, so an operation asked outside is not disturbed: a failed answer is replayed as the same failure at the same point and the draft stands on the re-run too. It pulls against none of the owner's rules (no length limit, no sampling change, no prompt rule).
- **The finder's first fix:** Catch LLMError around the rewrite, record turnlog.rewrite(task, why, "draft") and return the draft, as the marker case does. One place covers the narrator, the fight's telling and the frames.
- **The check:** Line 128 has no handler, as quoted. Printed: ok: returned the rewrite, calls [draft, rewrite]. refused (every rewrite attempt holds a game label, which the gateway rejects): LLMError 'narrate: no valid response after 2 attempts' out of fresh() with the checked draft in hand, calls [draft, rewrite, rewrite]. budget (the draft left a second of the turn): BudgetSpent 'the turn's budget is spent (-1 s left, the floor is 8 s)' out of fresh() after the draft alone. The played run: 26 narrate records, 6 of them rewrite attempts for 5 rewrites (calls 53, 74, 110, 111, 126, 153); call 110 was a rewrite attempt rejected by a check and 111 passed on the second and last attempt, so one more rejection would have thrown that passage's draft away. It did not happen in that run. The cost when it does is one written, checked passage replaced by a stand-in line (or a frame dropped); no state is harmed.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/voice.py 90-135, llm/gateway.py generate (161-201), engine/budget.py allow and the BudgetError classes (93-158), engine/asked.py; searched tools/sim for a test of a failing rewrite (rewrite with fail, refus, budget or LLMError: none; playthrough3_test.py:119 pins only the neighbouring rule, the draft stands when the rewrite loses blow markers). ## dead-families-1: A deed the engine refused, its passage lost, is told to the player as done: "You see it through."

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1438`. **Same place:** task-failures-1
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:1435 `rows = [r for r in ledger.this_turn() if r.get("facts") and not r.get("told")]`, :1438 `return failures.stood_lines(rows, rng) if rows else [failures.stood_any(rng)]`; engine/ruling.py:272 `ledger.add("refused", say=f"What the player tries does not happen: {v['answer']}")` (no facts). Run under the stub with every Narration call failing (work/check_dead_families_12_stood_play.py): the turn's one row is `refused`, and the only line shown is "You see it through."
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player types "I fly up onto the guildhall roof." The ruling is no. The refusal is told only by a passage (ruling.refuse calls ws.narrate), and that call fails (the model unreachable, a timeout, the turn's budget spent). stood_standin drops the row because it has no facts and prints a stood_any line ("You manage it.", "That's done.", "You see it through."): the opposite of what the engine decided, and nothing else is shown. By reading, the same holds for a way that ends (scenes/part_actions.py:126, kind `end`: "no way further in" is told as done). The line written for the case, stood.refused "That part didn't happen: {what}." (data/rules/failures.yaml:185), can never be picked. docs/design/23_untold_after_walks.md point 3 sets the rule this breaks (a stand-in never says what it cannot know).
- **Fix:** Make the stand-in agree with what the engine decided, for every lost passage and not only the refused act: (a) stood_standin reads every untold row of the turn, not only rows with facts; ledger.KINDS declares for each kind whether its row records a deed done or a no (refused, not_done, end, closed), and a line that says 'done' (stood_any) is never drawn while an untold row of the turn is a no; (b) the same for outcomes that write no row: either the passage entry carries how the deed came out when narrate() queues it (done, not done, failed), or a failed attempt writes a row of its own, so a failed roll's lost passage is not told as done either. A no with no fact to fill needs a plain 'that did not happen' list, which is new player-facing text for the owner to read first. Passing facts at the two `refused` adders is not enough by itself: three of the six stood.refused lines ('Everything else went through, but not this: {what}.', 'No luck with {what}. The rest is done.', 'All but {what} got done.') claim other steps were done and would be false on a one-step line, so they may be drawn only when another operation of the line stood. Test on the refused act, the dead end and the failed roll. No prompt rule is involved; this is engine code and data.
- **The finder's first fix:** In stood_standin read every untold row of the turn, not only the ones with facts, and never fall to stood_any while one of them is of a kind that records a no (refused, not_done, end, closed: one flag per kind in ledger.KINDS); pass facts at those adders (what was tried is in hand at each) so their own lists fill. Test it on the refused act and on the dead end.
- **The check:** Saw it happen. (1) 'I fly up onto the guildhall roof.', ActRuling sense no: turn() -> True; the turn's one row is `refused | facts: None | say: What the player tries does not happen: You leap, and the ground keeps you.`; the only thing shown to the player is narrate 'You see it through.' (a stood_any line); 3 Narration tries, the passage operation ended as stand_in. A second act ruled no ('lift the whole fountain') showed only 'That's done.'. (2) A dead end in tidepool_caves grown to its budget: row `end | facts: None | say: There is no way further in than the dripping chamber.`; shown 'You manage it.' (plus an unrelated weather line). (3) Comparison, a buy: the `paid` row has facts and the player reads 'You settle up with the herbalist: ...'. The quoted code is as reported: world.py:1435 filters rows on r.get("facts"), :1438 falls to stood_any; ruling.py:272 adds `refused` with no facts and ruling.refuse shows nothing but the passage (no console.note, unlike WorldScene.refuse at world.py:1942); part_actions.py:126 adds `end` with no facts. Both `refused` adders (ruling.py:272, world.py:1947) pass no facts, so failures.yaml:185-190 can never be picked. Nothing tells it later: rows live one turn. The reach is wider than the finding says: an act ruled at a cost whose roll FAILS writes no ledger row at all, and with its passage lost the player read 'Attempt: failure' followed by 'You finish what you set out to do.' (the dice line is true there, so it is a contradiction on the page, not a silent falsehood). Not rare in principle: lost passages (budget spent, three failed tries) are recorded several times in the two play journals of 15 and 16 November; none in the 42-line played session. Note docs/design/21_play_faults_plan.md A2 (as built, f644) says stood_any was 'read against the record' and is 'true as [it] stand[s]' because it is said only after the deed's own operation committed; this shows an operation that committed a refusal is not a deed done. f644 already holds the right rule for part_stood (world.py:2452: 'a step the game said no to did not do it'); stood_standin does not apply it.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/world.py stood_standin (1432-1438), line_standin (1706-1711), narrate/mark_passage/run_passages (3020-3035, 1395-1430), engine/ruling.py refuse (268-277), scenes/part_actions.py go_deeper (105-130), engine/failures.py stood_lines/stood_any and data/rules/failures.yaml. Searched tools/sim for a test that pins a stood_any line after a refusal (none: the four tests that name stood_any pin it for a deed that did stand, or call stood_lines directly). Then ran my own stub scripts with every Narration call failing, as tools/sim/passage_stands_464_test.py does it: audit/work/skeptic_dead_families_1_stood.py (two acts ruled no, a dead end, a buy for comparison) and audit/work/skeptic_dead_families_1_failed_roll.py (an act ruled at a cost whose roll fails). Campaign audit_check_dead-families_1, removed in finally; git status unchanged afterwards.

## task-failures-1: A lost passage is stood in for by 'No trouble. It's done.' whatever the deed came to: a failed theft, a half success, a hurt, an arrival

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1438`. **Same place:** dead-families-1
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:1435-1438 `rows = [r for r in ledger.this_turn() if r.get("facts") and not r.get("told")]` ... `return failures.stood_lines(rows, rng) if rows else [failures.stood_any(rng)]`. Only 8 of 33 ledger.add call sites pass facts (arrived x2, happened, paid x2, carried, left x1), so 17 of the 24 `stood` lists in data/rules/failures.yaml (102 lines: moved, found, gained, took, hurt, refused...) can never be shown, and no row says how a roll went. Runs with narrate failing (each of the four ways): party input 11 'Theft: failure' then 'No trouble. It's done.'; short input 38 'Attempt: partial' then 'You get it done.'; mentor input 6 'You come in at the wrong moment and come away bruised.' then 'You finish what you set out to do.'; every arrival in a new place 'You manage it.' with no place named.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The narrator's passage for a line fails (refused twice, cut off, too big, the server gone, or the line's budget spent by another task's failed tries). The deed stands and the player reads one of six lines that all say it went well. A failed theft is an event the engine marks NOTHING (scenes/law_actions.py:197); the code has the true line for it (voice_rules.ATTEMPT_ONLY, scenes/world.py:3092) but only where the model answered, and the unguarded rewrite at scenes/world.py:3086 falls to the same stood_any when it fails.
- **Fix:** The finder's fix stands, with two points. (1) Keep what the deed came to on the operation where the engine decides it (the theft's degree, an act's degree in engine/act.py resolve, a check's degree), beside `did`; stood_standin picks its list by that, and the same field is what finding task-failures-3 needs at a road stop, so it is built once. (2) Every ledger writer passes the facts its kind's list names, and data_check fails a kind that has a stood list and a writer without facts (and a list no writer can reach). The line for a deed that came to nothing belongs in data/rules/failures.yaml with the others (today's one such line, voice_rules.ATTEMPT_ONLY, is in code); new lines are the owner's to read first. Also catch the failure of the rewrite at scenes/world.py:3086 and show the attempt-only line, as the code already does when the rewrite still contradicts.
- **The finder's first fix:** Build the passage's stand-in from the operation's own record in one place: the degree of its roll, kept on the operation as `did` is (engine/operation.py:44), picks the list (done, half done, came to nothing), and every ledger kind's writer passes the facts its `stood` list needs, with data_check failing a kind that has a list and a writer with no facts. New lines are the owner's to write.
- **The check:** Seen: theft degree=failure with the narrator failing printed '[note] Theft: failure' then '[narrate] You see it through.' (a stood_any line; the ledger held no row, ops: action:steal stood, passage told by stand-in). Partial and success printed 'That's done.' and 'No trouble. It's done.'; their 'gained' row has no facts, so stood.gained is never used. A walk to the south fields with its passage lost printed only 'That's done.', no place named. A death in a fight with the narrator failing ended '[note] You have died.' ... '[narrate] You manage it.'. The finder's counts are slightly off: 7 of 33 ledger.add sites pass facts (court.py:126, matters.py:299 and 366, inventory_actions.py:341 and 358, shop_actions.py:216 and 252), covering 5 kinds (arrived, happened, paid, carried, left); failures.yaml has 23 stood lists (138 lines), so 18 lists (108 lines) can be filled by no row, and 3 of them (ended, gathered, worked) have no writer at all. The rewrite at scenes/world.py:3086 is not guarded, as claimed: its LLMError fails the passage and falls to stood_any. How often: in the 45 tracked play records narrate's last attempt errored 15 times in 1,673 rows, so the path is taken in ordinary play.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/world.py:1395-1438 (mark_passage, run_passages, stood_standin), 3020-3099 (narrate, _narrate_now), engine/failures.py, engine/ledger.py, scenes/law_actions.py:120-211, data/rules/failures.yaml. Ran work/tf1_f1_theft.py (stub, a real ws.turn, law.attempt fixed to each degree, the Narration call failing as passage_stands_464_test fails it) and work/tf1_f6_arrival.py (a walk whose arrival passage fails). Counted the ledger writers with an AST script (work/tf1_f1_counts.py). Counted final failures of narrate in the tracked records (work/tf1_records.py). No test in tools/sim pins a stood_any line for a failed deed (passage_stands_464_test pins only a buy, whose row has facts).
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/21_play_faults_plan.md section 3, A2 ('stood_any and round_stood were read against the record and are true as they stand ... only after the deed's own operation has', and 'Saying what came of a deed is group E's (the facts of a turn), not this'; group E is designed, not built) and docs/design/23_untold_after_walks.md item 3 (a stand-in never says what it cannot know). Neither records that a committed operation can be a failed deed, or that 18 of the 23 stood lists have no writer passing facts.

## world_py-1: A silent line's telling is asked inline inside the tail: when the narrator fails the player reads nothing at all and the tail's ticks are lost

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1928`
- **Evidence:** said_nothing (1921-1932), called inside the tail operation: `if ledger.untold(): self._narrate_now('Tell what the game did this turn, as the player would see it, and nothing more.', text)`. Stub run (audit/work/world_py_silent.py) with the narrator down: ops stood [action:look, world, arrival, law]; world ops failed [(tail, 'narrate: no valid response after 3 attempts')]; stand-ins []; coins 1000 -> 1007 (saved); turn count 1 -> 1; the player read [].
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A handler does its deed and shows nothing (the f416/f692 case) and the narrator call fails or the line's budget is spent. The deed is committed, the whole tail (turn count and the turn's ticks) is rolled back, and no stand-in is queued, so the player gets a blank turn with no word that anything happened. When the call works it is still made with the tail's transaction open (f470: calls before transactions).
- **Fix:** The proposed fix is right; I tried it in memory. said_nothing calling self.narrate(...) queues a passage operation that run_passages() (world.py:1889) tells after the tail commits. Narrator answering: the same page, the call now in operation 'passage'. Narrator failing: the tail stands, turn count 1 -> 2, stand-ins ['passage'], the player reads 'You get it done.' and the heard-of line. Two additions: give the 'took' row facts so stood_standin can name the contract instead of the generic line (any new line is the owner's to read first), and add the failing-narrator case to heard_not_answer_692_test on the real on_accept_quest path.
- **The finder's first fix:** Ask through self.narrate() so mark_passage queues a passage operation with its stood_standin after the tail commits, as every other telling of a line does. Add a sim test where the narrator fails on a silent line.
- **The check:** Code as quoted at scenes/world.py:1927-1928. Narrator answering: ops stood [action:accept_quest, world, arrival, law, tail], turn count 1 -> 2, the narrator call made as ('Narration', operation 'tail', transaction depth 1), the player read the passage and 'Heard of: the Tidepool Caves'. Narrator failing: 3 Narration tries inside the tail; world ops failed [('tail', 'narrate: no valid response after 3 attempts')]; stand-ins []; contracts held 0 -> 1 (saved 1); turn count 1 -> 1; the player read []. So this is the ordinary path of every contract taken by a typed line, not a rare handler: the deed is saved, the page is blank, and the tail (the turn's count, the heard-of line, the ticks) is rolled back. A spent budget would do the same by the code (budget.BudgetSpent is an LLMError; not run). It goes against what the owner set for lost tellings (GOALS.md decisions, the f711 row: what changed is 'told if its passage is lost'). The inline call itself is recorded residue (tools/sim/prepared_470_test.py RECORDED: 'narrate stays for its inline uses'); the blank turn is recorded nowhere.
- **How it was checked:** Read said_nothing, turn_ticks, turn, operation, asked_operation, narrate, mark_passage and run_passages (scenes/world.py), engine/asked.py call() and llm/gateway.py generate; data/rules/budget.yaml (narrate is not in asked_outside, so the call is made inside the tail). Searched tools/sim for said_nothing: turn_record_416, heard_not_answer_692, turn_driver_721 and registers_633 run it only with the narrator answering; none pins a failure. Ran my own stub script audit/work/check_world_py_1_silent.py on the REAL quiet deed (a contract taken at the board: scenes/guild_actions.py:446 adds its row passage_only and shows nothing), campaign audit_check_world_py_1, removed after; then tried the proposed fix in memory (check_world_py_1_silent_fix.py).

## world_py-3: A pane walk's arrival tail runs after the input has closed: no budget, not restartable, tellings asked inline

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1982`
- **Evidence:** pane_arrival (called from close_input, line 1152): `with questions.fence(), self.operation('tail', f'arrival at {self.player.location}', world=True):`. Probe (audit/work/world_py_pane.py): typed walk's tail ran with budget open True, serving True, collecting True; the #goto walk's tail ran with budget open False, serving False, collecting False, transaction depth 1.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player clicks a place on the map pane (#goto, #mapgo, #goroad). The arrival's ticks run in a plain operation outside the input: tasks that data/rules/budget.yaml lists under asked_outside (exchange, overheard, mentor_chat, canon_extract and the like) are called with the transaction open, no line budget bounds them (nothing holds the 60 second rule here), and a telling is asked inline instead of as a passage operation with a stand-in.
- **Fix:** As proposed, with one addition so it covers the kind: run the arrival inside command_input's input as asked_operation('tail', ..., world=True) followed by run_passages(), and take its ticks from the same function turn_ticks uses (pane_arrival's list is a hand-kept subset of it), so a typed and a pane arrival cannot drift apart. Add a pane walk with a party to prepared_470_test so the ratchet sees it. Check the goldens first: a recording that holds a pane walk with a party will move (the order of operations, what the budget defers) and is for the rebless skill, never a re-record to pass.
- **The finder's first fix:** Run the pane arrival inside command_input's `with self.input(...)` as asked_operation('tail', ..., world=True) followed by run_passages(), the same path turn() takes.
- **The check:** Code as quoted at 1982, called from close_input:1152 after command_input's `with self.input(...)` has closed. Typed walk: the ticks ran with operation tail, budget open True, serving True, collecting True. Pane walk: operation tail, budget open False, serving False, collecting False, depth 1, and the calls it made were ('Exchange','tail', depth 1, budget False, serving False), ('Extracted','tail',1,False,False), ('DialogueFrame','tail',1,False,False): exchange, canon_extract and dialogue_frame, all three named in budget.yaml asked_outside, made with the transaction open; operation.legacy() gained exactly those three, none of them in the f470 ratchet's RECORDED. With no budget open budget.deadline() is None, so each try may run to config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT (120 s, llm/llama.py:241) instead of the turn's deadline. What I could NOT show is a wrong result: with the Exchange failing (2 tries) the site's fallback stood, nothing was said, the walk was saved and no operation failed. The plan for f721 (docs/design/27_infrastructure_plan.md, 'One turn driver') has the tail inside the one driver, before its close; this path runs after it.
- **How it was checked:** Read play, command_input, input and close_input (1073-1164), pane_arrival (1975-1991), turn_ticks, narrate and mark_passage, engine/asked.py, llm/gateway.py generate, engine/budget.py deadline() and llm/llama.py:241. Searched tools/sim: mentor_test.py:357 pins only that a pane arrival runs Maren's goodbye; tutorial_stages_461_test pins the fence; turn_driver_721_test never walks by a pane. Ran check_world_py_1_pane.py against the stub: a party of two, the arrival's talk made due (banter chance 100, in memory only), a typed walk then '#goto trading_square', every model call logged with its operation, transaction depth, budget and serving; then the same with the Exchange call failing.

## pane-commands-3: The #enchant question keeps list positions: a pane command before the answer reorders the list, and 'yes' binds another enchantment into another item at another fee

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:2058`
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:2016  gear = list(c.equipment.values()) + [i for i in c.inventory if items.base_of(i).slot != "none"]
scenes/world.py:2058  self.ask_next("enchant", f"Bind {option.name} into {target} for {money.fmt(enchanting.fee(item, option))}" ... args=args)
scenes/world.py:2075  self.enchant_command(asked["data"]["args"], confirmed=True)
Run under the stub at eldervale_workshop (work/pane_commands/enchant.py): '#enchant 1 1' asks 'Bind Keen into the copper longsword for 0₲ 6Ş 0₵? 95% chance of success. (y/n)' and keeps {'args': '1 1'}; '#gearequip' of a greatsword runs and leaves the question standing (as ask_next's docstring says a command does) and the worn order becomes body, main_hand; 'yes' answers 'The enchantment takes. Your item is now the copper chain shirt of Warding.' and takes 1092 copper where 600 was asked. The longsword lies untouched in the pack.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** At an enchanter the player asks for Keen on the sword in hand, is asked to confirm, and before answering clicks Equip or Unequip in the Gear pane (or uses anything that moves the pack's order). The yes is then read against the new list: a different item gets a different enchantment, a slot on it is spent, and nearly twice the quoted fee is paid, with no second question.
- **Fix:** As proposed: keep the item's uid, the option's id and the quoted fee in the question's data, find both again at the answer, and say the offer no longer stands when either is gone or the fee differs (the reforge question at scenes/field_actions.py:776 is the pattern). Since enchant is the only question that breaks ask_next's 'ids and names' rule, that closes the kind; a small check in tools/sim that no question's data is a bare position would keep it closed.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the item's uid, the option's id and the quoted fee in the question's data (ask_next's own contract: ids and names, as the reforge question does), find both again when the answer comes, and say the offer no longer stands when either is gone or the fee has changed.
- **The check:** Printed. Control, no command between: question 'Bind Keen into the copper longsword for 0₲ 6Ş 0₵? 95% chance of success. (y/n)', kept data {'args': '1 1'}; 'yes' -> 'Your item is now the copper longsword of Keenness.', paid 600. With '#gearequip t-great' between: the question still stands, worn order becomes ['body', 'main_hand']; 'yes' -> 'The enchantment takes. Your item is now the copper chain shirt of Warding.', paid 1092, the longsword untouched in the pack. With '#gearunequip main_hand' between: the same wrong result, 1092 paid. Of the question kinds (fork, reforge_keep, reforge_take, discard, give_wanted, law, mentor, orenna_name, orenna_ruin, executioner, seal, enchant, allocate, clarify) enchant is the only one whose data is a list position; the others keep ids or names.
- **How it was checked:** Read enchant_command and on_answer_enchant (world.py:2003-2076), ask_next's contract (2289-2302), engine/equipment.py equip (pops the slot and re-adds it, so the worn dict's order changes on every swap) and unequip. Checked that a # command leaves a question standing (command_input never reads the question) and that the page may send one then (the question ends the line at the main prompt; server.py:217). Listed all ask_next callers to see whether others keep positions. Searched tools/sim for a test of the answer: only enchant_command('') is called (actor_caches_634_test, prefs_636_test). Ran my own stub script at eldervale_workshop with a control (work/check_pane_commands_1_enchant.py none | '#gearequip t-great' | '#gearunequip main_hand').

## pane-commands-2: An attribute point spent in a fight refreshes the fighter in memory only: the fight's row is not saved, so the next typed line or a reopen puts the old fighter back

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:2117`. **Same place:** world_py-12
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:2117  self.combat.refresh_player()
scenes/world.py:2118  self.store.save_player(self.player)        (no save_combat; the same at 2244-2245, and none in refresh_player, combat_scene.py:965)
scenes/world.py:1611  self.combat = CombatScene.resume(self, saved_fight) if saved_fight else None
Run under the stub (work/pane_commands/attr_row.py, attr_why.py), a level 8 mage with 6 points: after '#attradd constitution' and '#attradd intelligence' the character and the fighter in memory have con 21, int 33, hp 88/133, mana 114/128, and the saved row still has con 20, int 32, 85/130, 111/125. After the next typed line ('I attack the wolf.') the fighter is con 20, int 32, hp 75/130, mana 111/125 while the character keeps con 21, int 33 and maximum health 133. give_back ran in that line (the 'line' operation stands down for the round) and resumed the fight from the row.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** In a hard fight the player spends saved points on constitution and intelligence from the Character pane (the reason f508 built the refresh). The bars rise; on the very next action they fall back, the 3 hp and 3 mana gained are gone, and the fight is worked out with the old attributes, ward and maximums to its end, while the sheet shows the new ones. The same after closing and reopening straight after the click, and the same through '#allocate con 2 int 2' and 'yes'. If a draught is used before the next line (#useitem saves the row, combat_scene.py:963) the refresh is kept, so the outcome turns on what the player happens to do next.
- **Fix:** Do not fix it in refresh_player alone. Write the fight's row with every operation's commit, where save_talk() already writes the conversation 'with the operation that moved it' (world.py:1266): if a fight is on and its to_json() differs from the row, save it inside the same transaction. That covers every handler that changes a fighter in memory, today's and later ones, rolls back with the operation, and makes 'the fight in memory equals its row at the end of an operation' true by construction (GOALS.md's Bundle E row asks that the saved fight be consistent across a reload). Keep it per fight, not per self.player.
- **The finder's first fix:** Save the fight's row where the fighter is refreshed (refresh_player, or the one step after a standing command that pane-commands-1 proposes), so the row and memory never differ at the end of an operation; a check at commit that the fight in memory equals its row would catch every case of this kind.
- **The check:** Printed, level 8 mage: after '#attradd constitution' and '#attradd intelligence' (both stood True) character and fighter in memory con 21 int 33 hp 88/133 mana 114/128; saved row con 20 int 32 hp 85/130 mana 111/125; 'memory == row: False'. After the next typed line 'I attack the wolf.': fighter con 20 int 32 hp 75/130 mana 111/125 while the character is con 21 int 33 with maximums 133/128. After closing and reopening instead: fighter con 20 int 32 hp 85/130. With '#useitem healing draught' between (it saves the row, combat_scene.py:963) the refresh is kept: fighter con 21 int 33 hp 117.9/133 after the round. combat_allocate_test prints ALL PASS because it calls attribute_click directly and reads the fighter at once.

## typed-patterns-3: join_guild_rewrite takes the joining fee on substrings of the line and of the model's own summary: 'The guild hall feels warm tonight.' joins the guild

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:2585`
- **Evidence:** 2583: `low = f"{text} {a.summary}".lower()`; 2585: `about_guild = at_desk or any(w in low for w in ("guild", "registry", "register", "registration", "membership"))`; 2587: `and (any(w in low for w in ("join", "fee", "pay", "sign", "enrol", "enroll", "register"))`. on_join_guild (scenes/guild_actions.py:353) then does `c.coins -= G["joining_fee"]` and sets rank F with no question.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A character who is no member, the guild clerk present, any talk. Logged line (case 189): 'I tip my head slightly as a sign of respect. It has been an honor meeting all of you today.', read by the model as a talk to the smith with the summary 'express gratitude to the guild master': the repair made it join_guild ('sign' from the line, 'guild' from the summary). It was the repair's only firing on 1,888 real lines. Stub run (work/tp/verify_a.py): 'The guild hall feels warm tonight.' ('fee' in 'feels'), 'I tell the smith his design would suit the guild's door.' ('sign' in 'design'), 'Ella, I'm only paying a visit to the guild today.' and 'I nod to the smith. Good day to you.' with a summary that mentions the guild's sign-in desk all become join_guild. The model never gave join_guild itself on 1,896 logged lines.
- **Fix:** Agreed in principle: a repair should not spend coin or change standing on a suspicion, and the model's summary is not the player's words. In two parts. (1) The word tests read the typed line only, as whole words with their inflections (join_guild_rewrite 2583-2587, coin_offered 2608; is_bribe at scenes/inventory_actions.py:510 reads the summary the same way). Tried in memory: it cleared all five false joins above and kept 'I pay the fee and sign the register' and 'I'd like to join the guild'. (2) What still matches without asking to join ('I admire the guild's sign above the door.') is asked through ask_next / on_answer_ with the fee in the question. Part 2 adds a fixed line for the owner to read, and the plain forms the corpus pins (cases at 53-72, intercept_test 104-109) should go on joining at once.
- **The finder's first fix:** For every repair that turns a talk into a deed that spends coin or changes standing (this one and coin_offered, which reads `f"{text} {a.summary}"` the same way at 2608): the repair may not do the deed. join_guild is a kind the interpreter can choose; when the engine only suspects it, it asks through the pending question it already has (on_answer_*), with the fee in the question. The model's summary is never read as if the player had typed it.
- **The check:** Whole lines through ws.turn, a non-member with 1,000 copper at the guild house, the clerk at her desk, the reading one talk: 'The guild hall feels warm tonight.', 'I tell him his design would suit the guild's door.', 'I'm only paying a visit to the guild today.', the logged line 'I tip my head slightly as a sign of respect...' with its logged summary 'express gratitude to the guild master', and 'Good day to you.' with a summary naming 'the guild's sign-in desk' each ended at rank 'F', coins 1000 -> 700, the repair recorded as 'talk:... -> join_guild' and the note 'You join the adventurers' guild at rank F. Paid ...' (3 silver). Controls stayed talk with the coins untouched: 'Good day to you.' with the summary 'greet them', and 'The hall is warm tonight.'. After the repair the plan is a single join_guild step, which raises no audit flag (money_context needs a buy, sell, give, talk, other, work or commission step), so nothing asks first. The tests pin only the meant forms (paying the fee joins; 'I don't want to join' and 'I'll register later' stay talk). One limit on the report: case 189 fired only in the replay, which runs every logged line as a non-member; in that logged run the character already had three hires, so `if self.rank` (2579) held the repair off and no fee was taken. The window is a character who has not joined, with the clerk present: every new character's first visits to the hall.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/world.py 2577-2613 (join_guild_rewrite, coin_offered), NEGATED / UNPAID (84-85), scenes/guild_actions.py 341-363 (on_join_guild), understand() (repair, then audit) and engine/intent_audit.py risk_flags; the corpus cases at data/replay/interp_cases.yaml 53-72 and tools/sim/intercept_test.py 104-109, playthrough3_test.py 69-73. Ran scratchpad/audit/work/check_typed_patterns_1_bench.py (the kind after repair) and check_typed_patterns_1_scene.py (whole lines through ws.turn on the stub with the real on_join_guild; campaign audit_check_typed-patterns_1, removed), and a trial of the word tests in check_typed_patterns_1_fixes.py.
