## min-card-3: A try cut at the turn's deadline is charged the task's expected size, not the time it ran: the budget then counts room that is already gone

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `llm/gateway.py:263`. **Same place:** llm2-3
- **Evidence:** llm/gateway.py:262-263 `if failure not in FREE:` / `budget.charge(task, chars)   # (f468) a try that failed cost what it would have written`. Same script on the game's gateway: 'the reply's one try was handed a limit of 45.5 s and was cut at it; charged for that try: 9.6 s (the task's expected 120 tokens), so the budget counts 19.1 s spent and 35.9 s left; seconds really gone by: 55.0'.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Any call that runs away or stalls where its failure does not end the line (a second action's reply, a passage that falls to its stand-in, an optional frame or exchange with a fallback). After it the budget allowed a 19.7 s telling, a 27.4 s situation_parts, a 29.7 s board_stakes and a required narration with a 35.9 s limit: the line can reach about 55 + 36 = 91 s. The same line errs the other way for populate_place: a try that failed after 16 s is charged 47 s (1,500 expected tokens against 275 written at the median), so the reply and the passage's rewrite are refused with time in hand.
- **Fix:** The proposed fix is right in kind: on a failure of kind deadline charge the limit the try was handed, through one Budget method (arithmetic, no clock); other failures as today. Two things to add: under budget.SLOW the limit is None, so the expected size stays the charge there; and a recording that holds a deadline cut made before the change must replay with the old charge (a meta switch, as f538's budget_cached), which budget_468_test.py's own recorded cut would exercise. The over-charge of a failed populate_place is llm-hot-14's matter (expected sizes taken from the logs), not this one.
- **The finder's first fix:** On a failure of kind `deadline`, charge the limit the try was handed (it is max(floor, remaining), the budget's own arithmetic, so no clock is read and a replay charges the same) through one Budget method; other failures keep the expected size, which llm-hot-14 would take from the logs. Test both directions in tools/sim/budget_468_test.py.
- **The check:** gateway.py:262-263 is as quoted. My run: '3a required reply cut at the deadline: limits=[45.5] ... charges=[(npc_conversation, 9.6)] spent=19.1 remaining=35.9'; the finder's script then had thread_telling, situation_parts, moment, board_stakes and a required narrate all allowed with a 35.9 s limit. The other direction too: populate_place failing as a server error was charged 53.1 s a try (3 tries, 159.4 s counted). The path on exists: a later step that fails halts only the chain of actions (world.py abandon), and the line still goes to its passage, the world's operations and the tail (world.py:1843 to 1895); a first action that fails ends the line (world.py:1840), so there the charge changes nothing. Why low: the record shows no reach. There is no transport failure in the 14,035 rows (a 5090). At the minimum card's prices its deadline would have cut 45 recorded tries; 34 had limits under 20 s, where the expected-size charge is about the limit or more; the 11 with 20 s or more are all a townsperson's reply writing journal_note, 10 of them the line's first action with no call after and 1 followed only by populate_place. So in 2,620 recorded lines none would have run on because of this. It needs a runaway or a stalled server on a later step, a passage or an optional call, and min-card-2's fix removes the only runaway seen.
- **How it was checked:** Read the failure branch of llm/gateway.py _generate() and Budget.charge/estimate; ran audit/work/skeptic_mc1_budget.py (cases 3a to 3c) and the finder's script on the game's gateway with a stand-in source; traced what a failed operation lets the line go on to in scenes/world.py turn() and abandon(); counted in the 44 tracked runs which tries the minimum card's deadline would have cut and what followed them (audit/work/skeptic_mc1_errors.py).

## llm2-3: A background call's logged seconds include its wait for the card, so the call log overstates model time

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/gateway.py:274`. **Same place:** min-card-3
- **Evidence:** gateway.py:240 `start = time.perf_counter()` is taken before `backend.chat(...)`, which for the background lane waits in Worker._admit (worker.py:142-161, up to max_wait_seconds); gateway.py:274 `elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start` is what _log writes as seconds. Played session, record 123: populate_place, lane background, seconds 132.29, tokens read_ms 638, write_ms 10209, wait_ms 1433.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Any background call that waits for the player's reading time. tools/latency.py (calls_table 'Total s' and 'minutes in the model in all') and tools/night_measure.py sum this field, so populate_place shows 143 s and 36% of the session's model time when the model spent about 21.5 s on it; the audit's own by-task summary of this session carries the same error.
- **Fix:** Let the worker hand back each background call's own wait (the time in _admit plus any send the turn took back; it already adds the first to waited_ms) and have LlamaServer.chat put it in the reply's usage as queued_ms beside slot and lane (f602's pattern). Keep seconds as the wall and make the readers total seconds less queued_ms (tools/latency.py calls_table, tools/night_measure.py per_day, tools/card_profile.py scaled) so 'in the model' means it. One test: a background call held by a foreground call logs its wait apart.
- **The finder's first fix:** Have the worker hand back how long the call waited (it already adds it to waited_ms) and log it as its own field beside the call (queued_ms in usage), with seconds counted from the send, so the readers total model time alone.
- **The check:** Record 123: populate_place, lane background, seconds 132.29; its tokens say read 638 ms, write 10,209 ms, wait 1,433 ms, 12.28 s of wall on the server, so 120.0 s was the worker's wait (max_wait_seconds exactly). It was the run's only background call. The log's seconds sum to 397.5 s while the server's own wall sums to 277.2 s; populate_place shows 143 s (36%) in audit/calls_gemma.md. tools/latency.py line 84-85 totals this field as 'minutes in the model in all' and its 'Total s' column; tools/night_measure.py line 199 sums it for the situation tasks, and card_profile.scaled keeps 'the rest as measured', so a 3060 estimate of a background call carries its wait too. Nothing in play reads the field (the budget charges characters), so only the measures are off. The field itself is documented as wall seconds (latency.py line 19); it is the readers' label that overstates.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/gateway.py _generate (start at 240, elapsed at 274, _log's seconds), llm/llama.py LlamaServer.chat (the background lane goes through Worker.background), llm/worker.py _admit, tools/latency.py calls_table, tools/night_measure.py per_day and tools/card_profile.py scaled. Read record 123 and every background call of the played run with audit/work/v_llm2_1_slots.py.

## llm2-6: A thinking call's room is worked out against 32,768 tokens while a slot holds 16,384

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/llama.py:120`
- **Evidence:** llama.py:120 `room = backend.think_room(req.messages, req.max_tokens) if getattr(req.sampling, 'think', None) else 0`; backend.py:157 `fits = int(config.NUM_CTX) - chars // 3 - int(max_tokens) - 256`; config.py:14 NUM_CTX defaults to 32768; the server log shows n_ctx_slot = 16384, and llama_body is handed the slot's size (machine slot_ctx) without using it. Computed with the pure functions (audit/work/llm2_think_room.py): a 30,000 character prompt with max_tokens 2048 gets n_predict 10,240, about 17,740 tokens against the slot's 16,384.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Only when a measuring run turns thinking on (DND_THINK_TASKS) for a task with a large prompt; npc_conversation's ceiling is 36,500 characters. The guard meant to keep thinking inside the context lets it run past the slot, the answer ends 'length' with the slot full, and the gateway files the call as a request too big with no relaxed try, so a measure of thinking is skewed by refused calls.
- **Fix:** One source for the context a call has: think_room should use the slot's size from the settings (data/runtime/server.yaml server.slot_ctx, the same on every machine), not config.NUM_CTX, and NUM_CTX should either default to it or go, since its only other live use is the stand-ins' num_ctx option. Do not read the source's granted slot_ctx (a machine fact from /props): think_room feeds neutral_request's max_tokens, the recorder's fingerprint, which must hold nothing of the machine. tools/sim/num_ctx_425_test.py ('the game's own context is 32,768') and thinking_room_534_test.py pin the old number and move with it; kept recordings do not think, so no golden moves.
- **The finder's first fix:** Let backend.think_room read the slot's context (the source's facts slot_ctx, or server.yaml's slot_ctx) instead of config.NUM_CTX, so the body and the recorder's neutral request still agree.
- **The check:** Printed: 'config.NUM_CTX 32768 | THINK_ROOM 8192 | THINK_TASKS [] | the slot 16384'; 'prompt 30000 chars, max_tokens 2048: room 8192, n_predict 10240; ... at 4 chars a token 7500 (+n_predict = 17740); the slot leaves 8884 ...; with the slot's size the room would be 4080 (n_predict 6128)'; at 36,500 characters n_predict is still 10,240 where the slot leaves 7,259. The played run's server log says n_ctx_slot = 16384. config.NUM_CTX is the old client's per-call context; nothing sets DND_NUM_CTX by default, and llama_body ignores the machine's slot_ctx. Limits: THINK_TASKS is empty unless a measuring run sets DND_THINK_TASKS, so no player meets it; and I did not run a model, so the slot actually filling is traced, not seen. The consequence is narrower than stated: with the loose guard a long thinking ends 'length' with the slot full and is filed as too_big (refusals 'request_refused', no relaxed try) where the right guard would end it 'thought_out', also with no relaxed try. It mislabels and lengthens such calls; it does not fail calls that would otherwise pass (the right guard, at three characters a token, gives less room, not more).
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/llama.py llama_body, llm/backend.py think_room, legacy_kwargs and neutral_request, config.py (THINK_TASKS, THINK_ROOM, NUM_CTX), llm/gateway.py's length handling (283-310, ENDS and REFUSED), tools/think_ab.py room_for, tools/sim/thinking_room_534_test.py and num_ctx_425_test.py. Searched tracked files for DND_NUM_CTX. Ran audit/work/v_llm2_6_think_room.py with the real pure functions (no server, no model).

## llm2-4: After a chat restart fails, Try again brings the model back without the embedder for the rest of the session

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/runtime.py:963`
- **Evidence:** runtime.py:963-964 `if self.embed_on or self.embed_state in ('ready', 'loading'):` / `self.embed_state, self.embed_why, self.embed_on = 'failed', 'the model server stopped', False`; load() decides again only `if self._closed:` (877-878) and _load starts the embedder only `if self.embed_on is None:` (942). Run against tools/sim's fake llama-server (audit/work/llm2_try_again_embed.py): after the failed restart and a second rt.load(): state ready, chat answered, facts embedder False, embed_failure 'the model server stopped', no embedder child.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The chat server dies in play and its one automatic restart fails (the card still busy, a slow start). The could-not-wake page's Try again (launch.py:339: the same runtime loaded again, never closed) loads the model and play goes on with embed.available() False: every meaning check uses its word-list fallback until the game is closed, and nothing says so beyond embed_failure in the facts.
- **Fix:** The proposed fix would not reach this path: Screen._load sets rt.state to 'loading' before load() runs (launch.py:272), so a check for state 'failed' inside load() never fires on Try again. Fix it where the decision is thrown away: in _load's failure handler (runtime.py:963-964), when the embedder was on and the runtime stops it with the chat server, leave the decision undecided (embed_on None, embed_state not_started) instead of False; an embedder that failed on its own at the load keeps False, as the 524 test pins. Checked with the same script and that one change made by hand before Try again: 'state ready | facts embedder True | embedder child True | embed.available(): True'. While failed, facts still say no embedder and _start_embed still refuses, so the pinned checks hold. Add the Try again case to tools/sim/embed_review_524_test.py.
- **The finder's first fix:** In load(), when the runtime's state is failed (not only when it was closed), put the embedder's decision back to undecided (embed_on None, embed_state not_started) so the next load that succeeds starts it again; add the case to tools/sim/embed_review_524_test.py.
- **The check:** Printed: '1. the launch's load: True | state ready | facts embedder True'; '2. the chat server killed; the call that found it: Failure unreachable | state failed | facts embedder False | embed_failure 'the model server stopped' | old embedder alive False'; '3. the next call, the page answered Try again: answered | state ready | facts embedder False | embed_failure 'the model server stopped' | embedder child False | source has an embedder False'; 'embed.available(): False | embed.vectors: None'. The live embedder is stopped by the runtime itself (_stop_children) and marked off (embed_on False), and line 942 starts one only when embed_on is None. The same holds for 'Play slowly on the processor'. Rare: it needs the one automatic restart to fail first.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/runtime.py load, _load (the failure handler at 960-965 and the decision at 942), _died, chat_call, _start_embed, facts, and llm/launch.py Screen._load, wait and recover. Ran my own audit/work/v_llm2_4_try_again.py on the tests' fake llama-server (tools/sim/fake_llama.py, a Python stand-in, no model, in a folder of its own under audit/work, settings written by hand): the real Screen wired to a Runtime, the chat child killed with its restart made to fail, then a foreground call answered 'Try again' on the could-not-wake page. Read tools/sim/embed_review_524_test.py: it pins embeddings off while the runtime is failed, and nothing about a later load.

## llm2-5: An update's forced exit no longer stops the model server: stop_for_game knows only the dormant start

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/runtime.py:1198`
- **Evidence:** core/updates.py:104-109 calls `runtime.stop_for_game()` then `os._exit(0)` ('the model server it started stops first (os._exit runs no atexit)'). runtime.py:1200 `rt, lock, undo = _GAME.pop('rt', None), _GAME.pop('lock', None), _GAME.pop('undo', None)` reads only what start_for_game filled. With data/rules/launch.yaml present, main.py:92-100 starts the server through launch.Screen (launch.SCREEN), so _GAME is empty and the call does nothing. The header (runtime.py:30-31) says updates reach it through llm.backend.close(), which nothing calls.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A player installs an update from inside the game and the normal quit has not finished within 10 seconds (updates.py:135, the Timer): _leave ends the process with the llama-server child still running and run/server.json and run/server.pid left behind. On Windows the Job Object then kills the child as the process's handles close, so the card is freed, but not by the path the code states, and not at all if the job could not be assigned.
- **Fix:** One stop for the game's server, used by main.py's finally, the atexit hooks and updates._leave alike: either _leave calls launch.stop() and runtime.stop_for_game() as main.py does, or stop_for_game() itself also closes launch.SCREEN's screen, so no caller has to know which start ran. Correct the header's line about backend.close(). Test it in tools/sim/updates_test.py or load_and_slow_526_test.py with a runtime started by the screen: after the update's stop the child has ended and the run files are gone.
- **The finder's first fix:** Make one stop cover both starts (stop_for_game also calling launch.stop(), or _leave calling backend.close() as the header says) and test it with a runtime started by the screen.
- **The check:** Printed: 'launch.screen_on() with the tracked data/rules/launch.yaml: True', 'runtime._GAME before: {}', 'after runtime.stop_for_game(): the screen's runtime closed 0 times; the screen still held: True', 'after launch.stop(): closed 1 times'. So on the shipped tree main.py starts through launch.Screen and _leave's stop does nothing. Nothing in the tracked tree calls llm.backend.close(), which runtime.py's header (line 30-31) names as the update's path. Reach is small: install() only goes this far in a built Windows game, where the kill-on-close Job Object (runtime.py _Job) ends the child when the process does, and the next start's stop_stale clears run/server.pid; what is left is run/server.json for a developer tool that attaches, and a stop that depends on the job having been assigned (AssignProcessToJobObject's result is not checked). The forced exit only matters when the normal quit has not run main's finally within the 10 s timer (a turn still in a model call).
- **How it was checked:** Read core/updates.py _leave and install, llm/runtime.py start_for_game and stop_for_game, llm/launch.py Screen, SCREEN and stop, main.py main and play, ui/gui/__init__.py and ui/gui/server.py's /update. Searched every tracked file for backend.close, stop_for_game and launch.stop. Ran audit/work/v_llm2_5_stop.py (no server: the screen's runtime a stand-in that counts its close).

## shell1-17: The built game's --terminal cannot read a line: the build has no console

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `main.py:53`
- **Evidence:** main.py:53 `parser.add_argument("--terminal", ..., help="play in the terminal (the built app opens a window by default)")`; build_exe.bat:12 `--onedir --noconsole`, and its closing message 'run it with --terminal for the text version'; ui/console.py:60 `return input("> ").strip()`. main.py:41-42 already treats a None stdout as the windowed build's case.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Meravia.exe --terminal: a windowed executable has no stdin and its stdout is the null device, so nothing is shown, the model server is started, and the first input() raises RuntimeError (lost sys.stdin). guarded() records it, and its finally calls input() again (main.py:215), which raises again. The text version runs only with both streams redirected. Read from the code; not run in a build.
- **Fix:** Decide one way for the built game. Either drop --terminal from the frozen game's help, the docstring and build_exe.bat's closing line; or, when --terminal is asked and sys.stdin is None on Windows, attach the parent's console (AllocConsole when there is none) and reopen CONIN$/CONOUT$ before utf8_streams(), or build a second console exe from the same folder. In either case guarded()'s closing input() should not run without a stdin, so the first fault is the one reported.
- **The finder's first fix:** Either take --terminal out of the built game's help, the docstring and the build script's message, or attach a console and reopen the streams when it is asked for, before the first prompt.
- **The check:** pythonw printed: `stdin=None`, `stdout=None`, `stderr=None`, `input: RuntimeError: lost sys.stdin`. The guarded() run printed: `guarded() raised: RuntimeError - lost sys.stdin`, `raised from the finally's input(): True`, `the first error (kept as context): RuntimeError - lost sys.stdin`, and crashlog.record was called once with 'outside a turn'. build_exe.bat:12 builds `--onedir --noconsole` and line 26 tells the builder 'run it with --terminal for the text version'; main.py:7 and :53 say the same; main.py:38-42 already treats a None stdout as the windowed build's case and sends it to the null device, so nothing would be seen either. Before the first prompt play() has already begun the model server's load (main.py:92-98) and made the release check (main.py:116-118); main()'s finally stops the server. It works only with both streams redirected.
- **How it was checked:** Read main.py (options, main, play, guarded), ui/console.py:57-60, scenes/home.py choose(), build_exe.bat; git grep of tracked files for AttachConsole, AllocConsole and sys.stdin (no console is attached anywhere). Ran two scripts: scratchpad/audit/work/shell1_2_pythonw.py started under pythonw.exe with nothing redirected (the same windowed subsystem as a --noconsole build), and shell1_2_terminal.py, which calls main.guarded(lambda: console.ask(), None) with paths.FROZEN True, sys.stdin None and crashlog.record replaced by a list. NOT run in a built exe.

## shell1-6: Quitting or closing the window during character creation leaves a dead game in the Load list

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `main.py:156`
- **Evidence:** main.py:156-160 `character = ThresholdScene(session=session).run()` / `if character is None:` ... `saves.discard(name)`: only the #menu path discards. scenes/goddess.py:104 `raise SystemExit(0)` on quit; ui/gui/bridge.py:231 `raise Closed()` (a SystemExit) when the window is gone. Repeated main.py's steps before creation (CampaignSession.open, saves.touch) in a scratch folder: list_saves() gave ready False, 'no character yet: creation was not finished', and index last pointed at it.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** New Game, then type quit at the Threshold (the game says 'No character was saved'), close the window, press Ctrl+C, or a model failure ends creation. The folder game_<time> with its campaign.db and its index row stay, the session is never closed, and Load shows one more row that 'can't be opened', counted in 'Load a game (N saved)'. Each such exit adds another.
- **Fix:** Cover every way out, not only the three named: (1) for a new game call saves.touch(name) only once its character is saved, so a game enters the Load list when it has a character and even a killed process or a call cut off at exit leaves no dead row; (2) put creation in try/finally: when no character was made, for any reason (Main menu, quit, the window closed, Ctrl+C, a model failure, a fault), close the session first (the folder cannot be removed on Windows while the database is open) and call saves.discard(name) when kind == "new"; this replaces the #menu special case with the one path.
- **The finder's first fix:** In play(), wrap creation in try/except BaseException: close the session, call saves.discard(name) when kind == "new" (it already refuses a game with a character), and re-raise.
- **The check:** Printed: `typed quit: raised SystemExit(0) through play(); session.closed=False` / `folder kept: True | in index: True | index last: audit_check_shell1_1_a`; the same for the closed window (`raised Closed(None)`); Main menu: `closed and discarded`, folder and index row gone. Next start: list_saves() gave both as (ready False, 'no character yet: creation was not finished'), the menu showed `[l] Load a game (2 saved)`, the Load list two rows reading 'no character yet: creation was not finished', and picking one is refused. The game had just said 'You leave the Threshold. No character was saved.' Severity lowered from medium: nothing is lost or corrupted, Continue skips the row (saves.last), the row says why and the player can delete it (d and its number); each one leaves about 170 KB and one line in the list.
- **How it was checked:** Read main.py:127-179 and :182-215 (guarded re-raises SystemExit), scenes/goddess.py:92-146 (quit raises SystemExit(0) on the first page at :144 and in the loop at :104), ui/gui/bridge.py:52 and :222-239 (Closed is a SystemExit, raised by ask when the window is gone), ui/gui/__init__.py:21-43, storage/saves.py (touch, summary, list_saves, discard) and scenes/home.py:51-153. tools/sim/home_test.py:58 pins only that such a row is listed as not ready with its reason; lines 161-175 pin that a new game left by Main menu is discarded, which is the stated intent (main.py:157 'there is no game yet, so a new one is not kept'). Ran check_shell1_6_quit.py (same work folder): main.py's own steps for a new game in a scratch saves folder, left by typed quit, by a closed window and by #menu.

## trace-threads-5: A turn that waits on a background job waits with no limit of its own and outside the budget

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `npc/backfill.py:80`. **Same place:** trace-threads-1
- **Evidence:** backend.promote(job.get("thread"))
backend.waiting(job["done"].wait)
engine/budget.py:267  return b.deadline() if b is not None and b.mine() else None
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player walks back into a place whose rest-of-the-people job is still pending (npc/life.py:180 settle, inside the enter), or picks passives before the creation job is done (character/creation.py:120-121). The turn blocks on Event.wait() with no timeout while the job's thread runs its call with deadline None, since budget.deadline() answers only the owner's thread: nothing is charged to the turn and the only bound is the 120 s hang guard. Usual cost on the 3060 is about 20 s the budget never sees (613 answer tokens at 31.7 a second), added to a turn that was priced without it. When recording (STRICT) every input edge waits this way.
- **Fix:** In backfill.collect, when the calling thread owns an open budget, wait with budget.deadline() as the limit and charge the job's call to the budget at its estimate, as a foreground populate_place is charged (an estimate, not the seconds waited, so the budget stays the same on replay). When the limit runs out, populate_place returns the people who exist without planning again while the job is pending; they come in at a later edge. With no budget open (creation, the edge) it waits as today.
- **The finder's first fix:** When a turn promotes a job, hand the promoted call the turn's remaining deadline and wait with that limit; on expiry leave the people missing, which collect already handles on the next visit.
- **The check:** Printed: 'the turn's budget: deadline 2.0 s, spent 8.0', 'the turn waited 2.9 s on the job; budget spent after: 8.0; charges: []', 'calls while the budget was open: [(ResidentSet, background thread, None)]', and for the same entry made in the foreground under the same budget '[(ResidentSet, turn's thread, 2.0)]; charges: [(populate_place, 5.09)]'. So the job's call carries only the hang guard (120 s a try) and the turn's wait on it is neither limited nor priced. The reach is narrower than reported: creation has no budget open and its foreground retry has no deadline either, and the STRICT wait is at the input's edge before the budget opens (recording only). What is left is a turn that re-enters a place whose job is still running, which takes leaving and coming straight back inside the job's time (about 20 s on the 3060).
- **How it was checked:** Read npc/backfill.py:64-99, npc/life.py:175-188, character/creation.py:90-123, engine/budget.py:129-185 and 261-267, llm/gateway.py:243-248 and the worker's promote. tools/sim/backfill_test.py:67-72 pins the wait itself as intended ('re-entering settles the running job instead of asking again') and budget_468_test.py:149 pins that another thread's call is not charged; no test pins a wait without a limit or a price. Ran scratchpad/audit/work/check_trace_threads_5_wait.py on the stub behind a probe that records the deadline each call is handed and its thread; the background call was made to take 3 s and the turn's budget opened with 2 s left.

## trace-threads-1: Background residents are applied outside any transaction and a fault in the apply is swallowed, leaving people saved at the place who are not its residents

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `npc/backfill.py:88`. **Same place:** trace-threads-5
- **Evidence:** life._apply(store, world, catalog, pid, job["slots"], job["result"])
except Exception:
    pass
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The rest of a place's people come back from the background call and the main loop applies them at the input edge (scenes/world.py:1062), where no transaction or operation is open. life._apply saves each person in its own save_npc transaction and writes the place's resident list last. If making the third person raises, or the game is killed part-way, the earlier ones stay in the npcs table at that place but never enter place.residents; the job is popped, nothing reaches the crash log, and the next visit plans the missing slots again. Run on the stub (scratchpad/audit/work/tt_half_apply.py): 4 of 8 residents, 6 rows at the place, 2 saved but not residents, no crash log; after the next visit 8 of 8 residents and 10 rows, the 2 extras permanent and still returned by retrieval.people_at.
- **Fix:** Open one store.transaction() inside life._apply itself (it joins an operation's transaction when one is open), so both callers at the input's edge, backfill.collect and repopulate(), are all or nothing; and in collect replace the bare pass with crashlog.record(err, 'background people', place=pid). The transaction alone was shown to leave no stray people and a clean second try.
- **The finder's first fix:** Apply each job inside one store.transaction() (or as an operation) in collect, so a fault rolls the whole batch back and the next visit asks again, and write the fault to the crash log instead of pass.
- **The check:** As the code stands: 'armed=False depth=0 in_operation=0', 'nothing raised to the caller; residents 4 of 8; npc rows at the place 6; saved but not residents 2 [adeina_greenwell, heslyn_yorke]', 'job still pending False', 'crash log written: False', and after the next visit 'residents 8 of 8; npc rows at the place 10; still saved but not residents 2' with guild_contractor at 5 where the place is written for 3. With the apply inside one transaction: 0 saved but not residents, and 8 of 8 with 8 rows after the next visit. What narrows it: the trigger is a second fault inside _apply (engine code that already ran for the first batch; none is known, and the model's reply cannot cause one) or the process dying inside the apply, which took 2.6 ms and 4 separate commits on the stub. The certain part is that any fault there is swallowed with no line in logs/crash.log, against f449's own rule (config.py:57 'every fault the game went on without').
- **How it was checked:** Read npc/backfill.py:64-93, npc/life.py:134-172, scenes/world.py:858-865 and 1059-1063, storage/campaign.py:354-371, 729-732 and 781-794. Looked for what could make the apply raise on a real reply: llm/contracts.py:768-778 requires exactly slots 1..n, so a bad slot number cannot index out of range. Searched tools/sim for a test that pins the swallow (backfill_test.py does not test a failing apply). Ran my own scripts on simlib's stub (save audit_check_trace-threads_1, removed): scratchpad/audit/work/check_trace_threads_1_apply.py injects a fault at the third person's doings.doing_for, once as the code stands and once with the apply inside one store.transaction(); check_trace_threads_1_time.py times the apply and counts its commits.

## people-5: A person whose goal has ended is handed a new one at their first conversation, past the engine's cooldown

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `npc/life.py:238`. **Same place:** llm-rest-12
- **Evidence:** life.py:238 `has_motive = bool(npc.motive) or motive_roll(npc, store)`. motive_roll is seeded per person (life.py:208) and so returns what it returned at birth. When a background person's engine goal ends, engine/drift.py sets `npc.motive, npc.motive_since, npc.motive_done_at = "", 0, t`; inner_life then returns early (line 220, motive_done_at >= 0), and line 238 rolls True again. profile_request tells the model they have a motive and to write one, and line 254-256 stores it with motive_since = now. motive_done_at stays set and motive_step is not reset. data/rules/pulse.yaml: lasts_days 24, cooldown_days 12, base_chance 0.25.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A resident nobody has spoken to finishes their goal on day 24; the player first talks to them on day 26. They get a new goal invented by the model on the spot, ten days before the drift would allow one, and not drawn from the engine's seeds.
- **Fix:** has_motive = bool(npc.motive): after inner_life the engine has decided, and the drift alone hands out the next goal. profile_request's 'THEY HAVE A MOTIVE: write one' branch then has no caller left and can go with its parameter, so the model only ever restates a goal the engine gave. No golden should move unless a recorded person was in this state.
- **The finder's first fix:** After inner_life has run, the engine has already decided: has_motive = bool(npc.motive). Keep motive_roll for inner_life only.
- **The check:** Printed: 'Walmon Radfield: goal at birth to see this year out better than the last, since 540, done_at -1, roll True'; 'after the drift: motive "", since 0, done_at 1980'; 'first conversation 2 days later: the profile request said write one; motive now work toward a goal, since 4860, done_at 1980'; a goal inside the cooldown: True; from the engine's seeds: False. Control, one born without a goal: the request said none, motive ''. So anyone whose birth goal has ended is told to have a new one, written by the model, the first time they are spoken to, whatever the cooldown says; motive_done_at stays set beside the new goal. The same line also fires if a trait change moves their chance past the stored roll.
- **How it was checked:** Read npc/life.py:203-256, engine/drift.py:134-175, engine/motives.py:36-58, npc/prompts.py:45-50 and data/rules/pulse.yaml (cooldown_days 12, lasts_days 24). After inner_life has run, either npc.motive is set or motive_done_at >= 0, so 'or motive_roll' at line 238 can only fire for someone the engine has already left without a goal. Showed it under simlib's stub (scratchpad/audit/work/check_people_1_campaign.py, campaign audit_check_people_1, removed): a person born with an engine goal, the goal ended by drift.catch_up as inner_life_test does it, then life.promote two days later. tools/sim/inner_life_test.py pins only that promotion keeps a goal that is there.

## llm-checks-11: A townsperson reply's remember goes into their memory with no bound and no check

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `npc/life.py:576`
- **Evidence:** npc/life.py:576 `memory.keep(npc, ans.remember.strip(), day=clock.day(store.meta.minutes), turn=store.meta.turn, kind="told", subject=who,`. llm/contracts.py:1108 `remember: str = ""` has only blank_placeholders; data/rules/hygiene.yaml:10 prose_fields does not list remember, so hygiene.problem never reads it; engine/memory.py:97 keep() does not cut the text.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A side field with no bound is where Gemma ran on in this run (journal_note: 974 characters with '[THE GAME HAS DECIDED...' and 'REMAINED IN CHARACTER as ...' inside). The same in remember would be kept whole as that person's memory of the player and given back in their later prompts. In the three runs remember was one sentence each time: this is an open door, not a fault seen.
- **Fix:** Bound it where it is kept, so every path is covered (NPCReply, NPCReplyMany and the decision's answer all commit through apply_answer): one line, no square brackets, none of hygiene's machinery marks, cut to a length read from data/rules/memory.yaml, and dropped without a second call when it fails. A maxLength in the grammar, as they_promised has (contracts.py:1096), saves the tokens too; remember is bookkeeping, not speech, so this is no limit on a speaker. Do not reuse _clean_note as it stands: it drops any line with I, my or me, and a memory is rightly first person ('{them} told me their name is ...').
- **The finder's first fix:** Bound it in the grammar (maxLength, as they_promised has at llm/contracts.py:1096) and pass it through the note filter before it is kept (one line, no brackets), dropping what fails rather than calling again.
- **The check:** The code claim holds with no way out: a remember of 875 characters holding '[THE GAME HAS DECIDED: REMAINED IN CHARACTER as ...]' passes NPCReply, hygiene.problem returns ('', '') for it (remember is not a prose field), apply_answer keeps it as one told row of 875 characters, and npc/prompts.py memories gives it back whole in her next prompt (894 characters). The same text in the same reply's journal_note is dropped by _clean_note, and a hire's remember is held to 30 words. What bounds it today: the reply's 2048 tokens, and 16 told rows a person (the last 12 memories go into a prompt). What was not seen: no model wrote a long remember; in the runs it was one sentence every time (longest 134 characters, Gemma), though Gemma ran to 974 characters with bracketed text in journal_note of the same contract.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/contracts.py NPCReply (1099-1136) and CompanionReply (854-855), npc/life.py apply_answer (542-578), engine/memory.py keep (97-109), engine/hygiene.py prose_of and problem, data/rules/hygiene.yaml:10, data/rules/memory.yaml:16, npc/prompts.py memories (353-361), data/rules/reply.yaml:8 (decide_then_speak is false, so NPCReply is the live path). Ran a talk turn against the stub with a planted remember (check_llm_checks_2_endtoend.py, part 11). Measured remember in every accepted reply of the four runs (check_llm_checks_2_scan.py).
- **Already recorded:** Partly: docs/design/28_phase4_plan.md, A3 notes 'For A4, before the reply acts on the reading' (lines 204-207), says the guard does not read the reading's remember for another script. The missing bound and the bracketed text are not recorded. GOALS.md:119 (every store has a cap or a window) is the rule it touches.

Read played call 124 in scratchpad/trial3/play/warrior/gemma/play/llm_calls.jsonl directly. Searched tools/sim and docs/design for the heading.

## trace-save-3: What waits on the player's next line after a fight is on the scene only: the yielded foe's question and the road walk to resume are lost at a close

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/arc_actions.py:59`
- **Evidence:** scenes/arc_actions.py:59 `self.held_yield = list(foes)` followed by a plain note 'Spare it, or finish it? Say what you do.' (63-64), not a saved question (the f460 question store). scenes/road_actions.py:725-728: `self.resume_pending = (road["resume"], road.get("text", ""))` then `road["resume"] = ""`, so the saved road forgets where the walk was going while the scene alone remembers. Both are in engine/actor.py:132-133's rolled-back, never-saved scene attributes. Read, not run.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A foe yields at the end of a fight and the game asks 'Spare it, or finish it?', a natural place to stop for the night. Closed and reopened, held_yield is gone: 'I spare it' or 'I finish it' is read as a new line about nobody, the Spared event and the kill never happen, and no 'slips away' note is shown. If the fight was on the road, resume_pending is gone too and road['resume'] was already saved empty, so the walk that waited on the yield (world.py:1901, 2370) does not go on. The same after a crash between the fight's commit and its telling: f467 shows the question again, but nothing holds its answer.
- **Fix:** Keep what waits on a character's next line in the save by the mechanism already there: ask the yield through the question store (ask_next, scenes/world.py:2289, with the yielded fighters' rows as its data and an on_answer_yield that does what yield_intercept does, 'slips away' when the line is no answer), so run() asks it again at an open as it does any question; and read the walk to resume from the saved road (leave road['resume'] set, with a mark that the fight is won, until resume_road has run) instead of a tuple on the scene. Both keyed by the acting character.
- **The finder's first fix:** Ask the yield through the question store (engine/questions.py, save_question) with the foes' facts as its data, and leave road['resume'] in the saved road until resume_road has run, so both survive a close like any other question.
- **The check:** The quoted code is there (arc_actions.py:59-64; road_actions.py:725-728). held_yield is written at arc_actions.py:59 and nowhere saved, and its question is a plain note, not a saved question. What my run printed: hold_yielded shows 'The wolf has given up the fight and waits for you to decide. Spare it, or finish it? Say what you do.' with no saved question; after a close and a reopen through run(): held_yield None, the question not shown again, and yield_intercept('I spare it.') returns False, so the answer is read as a new line and neither the Spared event nor the kill happens. Road half, by reading: road['resume'] is emptied in the same step that sets the scene's resume_pending, and while a foe is held the walk waits for the next line, so a close there loses both; with no foe held the walk resumes inside the fight's own operation (world.py:2370) and there is no window. Reach is narrow: a foe is held only when it yielded and was not taken captive (not a person, or a fourth captive: services/fight.py:897-898, lifecycles.yaml most_escorted 3). The player loses one choice and must say again where to walk; nothing else is wrong in the save.
- **How it was checked:** Read hold_yielded and yield_intercept (scenes/arc_actions.py:54-89), road_fight_over and resume_road (scenes/road_actions.py:717-756), the two readers (scenes/world.py:1901, 2370), where a foe comes to yield (services/fight.py:793-810 and 889-910, engine/behaviors.py:52-77) and run()'s restores (world.py:1039-1057); searched tracked files for every use of held_yield and resume_pending. Ran the yield half in my own script (scratchpad audit/work/check_trace_save_1_count.py, last part, campaign audit_check_trace-save_1, removed). The road half is read, not run.

## leftovers-5: Several foes who yield in one fight each get the same label and the same note: the fight golden shows 'The captured one of Marrow Hask's guard is your captive now...' three times running

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/arc_actions.py:425`
- **Evidence:** scenes/arc_actions.py:425 `epithet = "the captured leader" if named else "the captured " + re.sub(r" ?\d+$", "", kind)` and :452 `console.note(f"{cap_first(npc.label(self.acting))} is your captive now, bound at your side. Question {w['them']}, let {w['them']} go, "`. The kept recording data/replay/sessions/stub_fight, input 15, shows the line three times for prisoner_wynn, prisoner_dorn and prisoner_sorin.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A boss's guards are each called 'one of <boss>'s guard'. When more than one yields, each is made a captive whose label is that phrase with 'the captured ' put in front, and each is told with its own note. The player reads one four-choice sentence three times, in words that do not parse ('The captured one of Marrow Hask's guard'), and then has three people under one label, so 'question the captured ...' cannot say which. The same holds for any two foes of one kind ('the captured bandit' twice). The golden pins this text as right.

The kept recording shows it: the turn row i=15 has 'The captured one of Marrow Hask's guard is your captive now, bound at your side. Question him, let him go, hand him to the watch, or put an end to it.' three times running (grep counts 3), for prisoner_wynn, prisoner_dorn and prisoner_sorin. Up to three can be taken at once (captive.most_escorted), and two foes of one kind ('bandit 2', 'bandit 3') both become 'the captured bandit' the same way. No test pins the repeat as meant: captive_test.py:76 asks only that the note is told for one captive. Not checked: which of three same-labelled captives a typed 'question the captured ...' reaches.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/arc_actions.py make_prisoner (414-454), scenes/combat_scene.py take_prisoners (1297-1311), services/fight.py captives (889-910), engine/bosses.py _guards (132-148), npc/models.py label (148-151), tools/sim/captive_test.py, and searched tools/sim for a test of the note. ## task-failures-7: When the audit's own model call fails, a line that was read rightly is asked back as unclear, and the turn is logged as stood

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/audit_actions.py:125`
- **Evidence:** engine/intent_audit.py:297-298 `if not bad:` `res.status, res.verdict = "unsure", "audit unavailable"`; scenes/audit_actions.py:125 `self.ask_back("audit_unsure", text, "the line looked like it might mean something else, and it could not be checked", res.meaning)`. Run (party, audit_meaning or audit_compare failing, each way): 'I give up the wolf contract.' (plan abandon_quest, done in the baseline) reads 'I'm not sure what you meant. Could you say it another way?'; pending_clarify is set; the turn row says stood all with the operations clarify and tail.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A flagged line whose audit_meaning or audit_compare answer is refused twice, cut off or too big. The player is told their words were unclear and, with a live model, is asked an in-character question about a line that had one reading (one more call); the next line is read joined to it unless it opens on a deed (f713). The same failure caused by the budget is already 'the line is not taken, not asked back' (engine/intent_audit.py:294, f468).
- **Fix:** In engine/intent_audit.py audit(), when the plan had no impossible step (`not bad`), let the exception out instead of setting 'unsure': understood() already takes an LLMError as 'the line is not taken' (a turn_not_taken line, the row marked as a model failure, no refusal of the player's words) and any other exception as the game's own fault in logs/crash.log. The plan still does not run, so f332's fail closed holds. The status 'unsure', the audit_unsure branch in scenes/audit_actions.py:123-126 and its kind in engine/refusals.py then go, and tools/sim/audit_test.py:80 pins the raise. For the other branch (an impossible plan whose second reading failed on the model, status 'failed') keep the ask-back but give it the plan's problems as the reason: today res.reason is the exception's text ('LLMError: interpret_action: ...') and is sent to the clarify prompt as WHY IT COULD NOT BE ACTED ON (audit_actions.py:121, 194).
- **The finder's first fix:** Treat the audit's model failure as the budget refusal beside it is treated: raise, so the line is not taken, the player reads a turn_not_taken line and the turn log counts a model failure. Failing closed (f332) is kept: the plan still does not run.
- **The check:** The quoted code is there: intent_audit.py:294-299 raises only when the exception carries `budget`, else `if not bad: res.status, res.verdict = "unsure", "audit unavailable"`; audit_actions.py:123-126 turns that into ask_back("audit_unsure", ...). My run printed, baseline: turn() True, turn 1 -> 2, audit 'unchanged'. With AuditMeaning failing: turn() returned True, turn 2 -> 2, shown [('note', "I'm not sure what you meant. Could you say it another way?")], refusals [('model_down','audit_meaning'), ('audit_unsure','I attack the silence and look around.')], pending_clarify {'text': 'I attack the silence and look around.', 'question': ''}, titles asked ActionPlan, AuditMeaning, AuditMeaning, Clarify (one more call), turn row audit 'unsure', reason 'LLMError: audit_meaning: no valid response after 2 attempts'. The next line 'the well, I think' was read joined: its row's text is 'I attack the silence and look around. - the well, I think'. AuditVerdict refused twice gave the same. The same deed typed again with the model back ran alone (f713). Nothing prevents it: understood() only catches what audit() lets out, and audit() swallows every exception but the budget's. It is the path f332 wrote on purpose ('the world asks instead', and engine/refusals.py:5 lists audit_unsure), and tools/sim/audit_test.py:80 pins only the status; but it now stands against two later rules: f437 (tools/sim/outage_line_437_test.py:60 'nothing is counted as a refusal of what the player typed' when the model failed) and GOALS.md:207 (a model failure inside a turn: rolled back, told in the narrator's words), and budget.yaml lists audit_meaning and audit_compare as required calls of 'understanding the line', whose other members (interpret_action, combat_interpret) are 'not taken'. Reach is small: in the tracked record 924 audit_meaning and 924 audit_compare calls had 0 errors, so this needs the server to fail between the interpreter's call and the audit's, or a request refused as too big.
- **How it was checked:** Read engine/intent_audit.py:250-301, scenes/audit_actions.py:92-127 and 179-223, scenes/world.py understood() (1675-1695), turn() (1799-1895) and understand() (2382-2412). (flag unmatched_verb:attack, no impossible step), failing AuditMeaning as unreachable or AuditVerdict as refused. Counted audit call errors in the tracked record (docs/measure/prose_baseline, prose_a1, prose_a2: 44 llm_calls.jsonl.gz). Ran no model.
- **Already recorded:** Not in GOALS.md or docs/design as a known fault. The path is f332's stated intent (engine/intent_audit.py:297, engine/refusals.py:5; tools/sim/audit_test.py:80 pins the status only). GOALS.md:182 (f559) records the owner keeping ask-back 'for now' for a failed ruling, knowing the player then reads the clarify note with the model down: the same trade, decided for rulings, not for the audit. ## scenes1-9: Only the last companion picked can ever bring up their motive: the loop variable is used after its loop

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/banter_actions.py:359`
- **Evidence:** banter_actions.py:349 `for m in pick:` ends at 355; then at 357-360, outside it: `mt = rules.P["motives"].get(m.get("motive", ""), "")` / `if mt and context.due(m, "motive", now):`.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** With two or three companions in an exchange on the road or at rest, the motive option is built for whoever the personal-topic loop ended on. The others' motives never come up unasked, and the due mark is only ever set for that one.
- **Fix:** Put the motive option back in a loop over `pick`, outside the `if job` block (as it stood before f382), the errand option left on its own. Add a test in tools/sim that, with three hires and no contract, each one's motive can be the hook, and that the mark is set for the one chosen.
- **The finder's first fix:** Loop over `pick` for the motive option, as the promotion, memory and personal options just above it do.
- **The check:** The fault is wider than reported. banter_actions.py:357-361: `if job and kind in ("travel", "rest"):` / `options.append((2, "errand", ...))` / `mt = rules.P["motives"].get(m.get("motive", ""), "")`: the motive lines sit inside the `if job` block and after the `for m in pick:` loop of line 349 has ended. In 2550c94 the two `job` lines were added between the personal-topic lines and the motive lines, which until then were all inside that loop. Printed: "no contract held; 600 hooks on the road -> motive hooks by whom: {} | at rest: {}"; "a contract in hand ... {'Corin Ash': 20} | at rest: {'Corin Ash': 40}" (Corin last of three); "the same three in another order [Corin, Bram, Isel] -> {'Isel Quill': 20}". So a motive comes up unasked only while an unfinished contract is held, and only for the hire listed last in the party.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/banter_actions.py banter_hook (279-383) and party_banter (609-654), data/rules/party.yaml max_party 3 and data/world/banter.yaml most_speakers 3 (so `present` is always the party in its own order, never a sample), and git blame and the f382 commit (2550c94), which put the errand lines into the middle of the per-companion loop. Searched tools/sim for a test of the motive hook: none (context_test only checks the concern list). Ran work/check_scenes1_2_b.py part B on the stub: three hires each with a motive that is due, 600 hooks drawn on the road and 600 at rest, with and without a contract, and in two party orders.

## scenes1-8: Model calls still made inside an operation's transaction in this area: camp_intent, discovery, arc_story

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `scenes/camp_actions.py:246`
- **Evidence:** scenes/camp_actions.py:246 `return generate("camp_intent", cpr.SYSTEM,`; scenes/explore_actions.py:119 `"discovery", SYSTEM,`; scenes/arc_actions.py:171 `story = generate("arc_story", SYSTEM, user(...), ArcStory, temperature=0.9, max_tokens=1800,`. All three are named in tools/sim/prepared_470_test.py RECORDED ('tasks still asked for inside an operation's transaction').
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A line typed at a camp, an exploration that invents a place, and accepting a missing-person contract each hold the turn's transaction open for the whole model call (arc_story is among the longest structured answers in the game). Anything that fails after the call rolls the operation back and throws the answer away, and invent_discovery keeps a world state loaded at line 108 across the call and saves it at line 150.
- **Fix:** As proposed: name the three in budget.yaml asked_outside and drop them from RECORDED (line, action:* and tail are all restartable, scenes/world.py:1822, 1836, 1888). One care the proposal misses: a rerun must ask the same request or it stops as a Drift, and both dress_arc (store.npc_names() at arc_actions.py:168) and invent_discovery (threads and names, explore_actions.py:114, 122) put live reads into the request; keep those reads with asked.compute so a resident written behind the scenes between the attempts does not lose the line. No prompt changes.
- **The finder's first fix:** Move each to the asked-outside path (data/rules/budget.yaml asked_outside, engine/asked.py) as the talk, naming and combat families were, and take them out of RECORDED. No prompt changes.
- **The check:** Printed: "ArcStory calls and the operation open at each: [('ArcStory', 'tail')]"; "CampIntent calls and the operation open at each: [('CampIntent', 'line')]"; "DiscoveryProposal calls and the operation open at each: [('DiscoveryProposal', 'action:explore')]"; "legacy tasks this session: ['arc_story', 'camp_intent', 'discovery', 'narrate']". One correction to the report: on that run the budget deferred arc_story out of the accept (budget.yaml arc_story need optional, later deferred; arc_actions.py:180-182) and it was asked in the line's tail operation, so it is the tail's transaction that waits, or the accept's when the budget allows it. What it costs: storage/campaign.py:357 `with self._lock:` holds the store's lock for the whole transaction, so every other thread's read or write of the save (the people written behind the scenes) waits for the length of the call; a failure after the call discards the answer. No wrong state was shown, and the load at explore_actions.py:108 saved at :150 is not overwritten by anything in between on that thread (PlaceDiscovered writes no world-state row). This is the f470 ratchet's known residue, so low.
- **How it was checked:** Checked the three call sites are real (scenes/camp_actions.py:246, scenes/explore_actions.py:118-124, scenes/arc_actions.py:171-174), that none of the three tasks is in data/rules/budget.yaml asked_outside (27-35), and the path in llm/gateway.py generate (179-185): a task not asked outside goes to operation.note_legacy and is called at once. RECORDED in tools/sim/prepared_470_test.py is only a ceiling (the test checks legacy <= RECORDED), so I ran the three for real on the stub: work/check_scenes1_2_f.py types lines through ws.turn with a spy over the stub that notes the operation open at each call (campaign audit_check_scenes1_2, removed). Also read storage/campaign.py transaction (355-371) for what an open transaction costs, and looked at the played run's summary (calls_gemma.md): none of the three tasks was called in its 42 lines.
- **Already recorded:** tools/sim/prepared_470_test.py RECORDED (lines 29-35: discovery, camp_intent, arc_story named as still asked inside an operation); docs/design/14_phase2_plan.md:35-37 (the f470 ratchet's legacy residue, there for ruling and event_judge); docs/design/12_foundations_survey.md:110 and docs/design/13_foundations_design.md:175 (the load and save pair held across the model call in scenes/explore_actions.py:105-147)

## scenes1-10: A camp guard numbered 10 or more is read as guard 1

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/camp_actions.py:260`
- **Evidence:** camp_actions.py:259-261 `for g in up:` / `if g["name"].lower() in hay:` / `return g`; guards are named `f"{tpl['minion_name']} {i + 1}"` (line 107) and a people camp has 8 to 14 (data/rules/arcs.yaml:41). Stub run (work/scenes1_check.py): camp_target for 'outlaw 12' -> outlaw 1.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player creeps up on 'outlaw 12' at a camp of twelve. The first guard whose name is a substring of the line is outlaw 1, so the takedown, with its check and its state change, lands on the wrong guard while outlaw 1 is still up.
- **Fix:** One matcher for a numbered name in a line (whole-name match on word boundaries, the longest name first), used here and at the other site of the same kind, scenes/combat_scene.py:520, where an order to a companion finds its foe by `e.name.lower() in low` or by the name's last word alone ('1' is found in 'wolf 12').
- **The finder's first fix:** Match guard names on a word boundary, longest name first (one small name matcher shared with the other places that find a numbered foe in a line).
- **The check:** camp_actions.py:259-261 `for g in up:` / `if g["name"].lower() in hay:` / `return g`, tried before the number. Printed: camp_target(text='I creep up on outlaw 12 and choke him out', named='outlaw 12') -> outlaw 1; the same with named='' -> outlaw 1; 'outlaw 10' -> outlaw 1; 'outlaw 2' -> outlaw 2; 'guard 11' (number alone) -> outlaw 11; with outlaw 1 already down, 'outlaw 12' -> outlaw 12. So guards 10 to 14 named by name are read as guard 1 for as long as guard 1 stands; the check's level modifier, the state change and the passage ('silently takes out outlaw 1') all go to the wrong guard. Guards differ only a little (one of two creatures, levels within a narrow band), so the harm is small.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/camp_actions.py camp_build (93-111: names are `<minion_name> <i + 1>`), camp_target (252-268) and camp_sneak (401-436), data/rules/arcs.yaml:40-42 (a camp of people has 8 to 14 guards) and scenes/camp_prompts.py:12, 23 (the model is shown the first twelve names and told to answer with the guard's name or number, so 'outlaw 12' is a target it gives). No test covers a two-digit guard. Ran work/check_scenes1_2_b.py part C on the stub.

## scenes1-13: A remade dungeon's stale delve postings are cleaned only from the board where the player stands, with every error swallowed

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/dungeon_actions.py:186`
- **Evidence:** dungeon_actions.py:186-192 `for pid in {self.player.location}:` / `ps.board = [q for q in ps.board if not stale(q)]` / `except Exception: pass`. The only note about a remake (lines 33-35) is in a branch that cannot run: lines 25-27 `continue` for exactly the case it tests.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A dungeon comes due and is remade with fewer floors while the player is anywhere but the hall that posted a delve for its lost floor. That posting stays on the other board, can be accepted, and names a floor that no longer exists. A held contract for a lost floor is taken out of the player's quests with no note printed here, and a failure reading the board passes silently.
- **Fix:** One rule for 'this delve posting names a floor the dungeon no longer has', used in the three places a posting is read: at the remake, in refresh_board's kept filter (guild_actions.py:125) and in on_accept_quest. At the remake, go over every guild-type place's board (not the player's location) and save a board only when it changed; drop the try/except, since load_place cannot fail on a missing row. In on_accept_quest save the struck board (state.board = board; save_place) so the clerk's strike is true. Tell a held contract that is let go, with the reason line obligations already draws for released/place_changed (as pulse.py does for issuer_gone), and go over every character's quests rather than self.player, since multiplayer is a goal. Delete the unreachable lines 33-35, or move that note to the case that can happen: a remake that wipes part-cleared progress (d['cleared'] != [-1, -1]) while the player is outside.
- **The finder's first fix:** Clean every board that holds a delve posting for that dungeon, print a note when a held contract is let go, and drop the bare except so a real failure shows.
- **The check:** Seen happen, with one clause of the scenario wrong. Script output: 'dungeon_willowmead_wetlands the Weeping Barrow: 4 floors now; at minute 33360 it is remade with 3'. CASE A, player at parth (hall_here() = guild_house, but player.location is not the hall): 'stale posting still on the hall's board: True [Clear floor 4 of the Weeping Barrow]'; 'held contract still in the player's quests: False'; 'lines shown to the player by the remake: []'. CASE B, player standing in guild_house: 'stale posting still on the hall's board: False'. So the loop `for pid in {self.player.location}:` (dungeon_actions.py:186) cleans a board only when the player stands inside the guild hall itself; boards live on guild-type places (guild_actions.py:103, load_place(gid)). The held contract for the lost floor is dropped with nothing shown (lines 182-185; obligations.close prints nothing; the issuer-gone case in engine/pulse.py:942-945 at least writes an item_history line). Lines 33-35 are unreachable: lines 25-27 `continue` whenever d is due and the player's delve is in it, and line 32 is reached only when d is due. The `except Exception: pass` is at 191-192; load_place returns an empty PlaceState for a missing row (campaign.py:727), so in practice it hides only a database fault. WRONG in the finding: the stale posting cannot be accepted. guild_actions.py:416-421 checks the floor against the dungeon at accept time; the script got 'That posting is out of date: the place has been remade. The clerk strikes it from the board.' and 'taken: False'. What the script found instead, not in the finding: the board pane lists the stale posting as takeable (board_data row 'ok'), and the strike at guild_actions.py:419 `board[:] = [x for x in board if x is not q]` edits a freshly loaded copy that is never saved: 'still on the saved board after the clerk strikes it: True', and a second try printed the same refusal. refresh_board (line 125) only drops postings whose dungeon id is gone, and the id never changes, so the posting leaves only by the daily 0.5 keep roll. No wrong game state results; the cost is a posting shown as open that is refused each time, and a contract that vanishes from the Quests pane unexplained. Also seen: the remake renamed the dungeon ('the Sunken Tomb'), so surviving postings and held contracts for it, and 'Slay the master of <old name>', keep the old name; that is outside this finding and the docstring limits voiding to lost floors.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/dungeon_actions.py 17-45 and 177-192, engine/dungeons.py generate (id stays dungeon_<place>, floors drawn 3..6 from a seed that includes the minute), scenes/guild_actions.py ensure_board / refresh_board / board_data / on_accept_quest, storage/campaign.py load_place, engine/obligations.py close, and the callers of ensure_dungeons (world_tick every line, world:open, camp_took). Searched tools/sim, GOALS.md and docs/design for void_dungeon_contracts, 'remade', 'out of date': no test pins it and no doc records it. Then ran a CPU-only script against simlib's stub (campaign audit_check_scenes1_3, removed afterwards; script at C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/scenes1_3_check.py): moved the clock to a minute where a dungeon near Parth's hall comes due and is remade with fewer floors, with one delve posting for its last floor on the hall's board and one held, and called ensure_dungeons with the player in the town and then void_dungeon_contracts with the player in the hall.

## scenes1-12: One dungeon chamber can be searched for coin without end

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/dungeon_actions.py:261`
- **Evidence:** dungeon_actions.py:261-262 `coins = self.rng.randint(1, 4) * max(1, d["floors"][self.player.delve["floor"]]["level"])` / `self.player.character.coins += coins`, with nothing kept of the chamber having been searched. Stub run (work/scenes1_check3.py, the check set to succeed as the taught passive second_look does: 'Searching a dungeon chamber always turns up something'): eight searches of one chamber gave [213, 142, 142, 142, 284, 142, 71, 213] copper, 1349 in 120 minutes, at floor level 71.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A player with second_look, or simply good perception, stands in one chamber and searches again and again: 'coin that others missed' every fifteen minutes, as often as they type it. Four successes match the chamber's one cache (5 to 15 a level, data/rules/dungeons.yaml) and the rate is far above a wage (20 copper an hour, data/rules/work.yaml).
- **Fix:** Mark the chamber searched on its own row, as `picked` and `disarmed` already are (it goes when the place is remade and is bounded by the chamber count), so each chamber yields once; put the 1 to 4 a level and the fifteen minutes in data/rules/dungeons.yaml. ## scenes2-6: A delve posting whose dungeon is gone is 'struck from the board' only in a list that is thrown away

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/guild_actions.py:419`
- **Evidence:** board[:] = [x for x in board if x is not q]
self.refuse("That posting is out of date: the place has been remade. The clerk strikes it from the board.")
return
- **What a player or the owner meets:** board is ensure_board()'s list from a fresh load_place(hall); this branch never saves the place (the accept path at 432-435 does). Probe (stub, seed 3): after the line was told, the posting was still on the saved board, so it is shown again, refused again each time it is picked, and holds a board slot until the board refreshes.
- **Fix:** One helper that takes a posting off a hall's board (load the place, change, save), used here and by the accept path. And close the source: stale delve postings are dropped where a board is read (ensure_board and refresh_board check the floor as well as the id), or void_dungeon_contracts goes through every hall's board instead of the player's place, so the branch at 418 is a guard that seldom fires. Test with a remade dungeon that lost a floor while the player was away from the hall.
- **The finder's first fix:** Remove it through the same load, change, save_place the accept path uses (one small helper for 'take this posting off the hall's board').
- **The check:** Printed, both times it was picked: 'That posting is out of date: the place has been remade. The clerk strikes it from the board.' | still on the saved board: True. How the state arises in play: a remade dungeon keeps its id, so the live case is the floor one (a posting for a floor the remade dungeon no longer has); void_dungeon_contracts cleans only the board of the place the player stands in (dungeon_actions.py:186), so a hall's board keeps such a posting unless the player was in the hall at the remake, and the daily refresh keeps it with chance 0.5 because it checks the dungeon's id, not the floor. Reach is small: one board slot for a day or two and a line that says what did not happen.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/guild_actions.py ensure_board (96-113: returns the board list of a fresh load_place) and on_accept_quest 416-435 (the stale branch changes that list and returns; only the accept path saves the place), storage/campaign.py load_place (no cache), scenes/dungeon_actions.py ensure_dungeons and void_dungeon_contracts (177-192), engine/dungeons.py:71 (a dungeon's id is dungeon_<place>, kept across a remake) and refresh_board (drops a posting only when its dungeon id is unknown). Ran audit/work/check_scenes2_6_struck.py (a delve posting for an unknown dungeon put on the saved board, picked twice; campaign removed).

## scenes2-10: Discard and show look among key items first, by substring of any one word, before the pack is looked at

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/inventory_actions.py:185`

find_key 98: hit = sum(1 for w in words if w and w in k.name.lower())

Discard it for good? (y/n)'; a yes destroys a quest item, a no keeps both and the ale cannot be discarded by that word. 'show the silver ring' shows a 'silver key'. When the interpreter leaves item empty the whole typed line is matched, so the word 'i' matches any key item with an i in its name. refuse_key (105) and on_give (650) look in the pack first; these two do not.
- **Fix:** One resolver for 'which carried thing do these words mean' over the pack, the key items and the things in hand (f592) together, matching whole words by the rule listening.said already has (a name's word, or one ending in the typed word, small words dropped), a thing named in full beating a partial match, and a true tie going to the store the action's own description names (key items for discard and show, the pack for drop, sell, store) or to a question (f460). (y/n)'; 'yes' printed 'Discarded: a cloth-wrapped key.' and the cloth was still x2. on_show(item='the sealed codex') told 'The player takes out a sealed letter () and looks it over.' The same words through on_drop (refuse_key, pack first) set down the cloth. find_key (line 98) scores by substring of any one word and drops only the/my/a/an/of, so with item empty the typed line's 'i', 'it', 'to' count too (by reading; my two names hold no 'i', so that call returned None). Corrections to the report: there is no ale good in data/world/goods.yaml, so its example needs other names, and the listening repair grounded_item does not help (it covers show but not discard, and on_show asks find_key first whatever the item says). The loss of a key item still needs a 'yes' to a question that names it; show has no question, and the person is told the wrong thing.

Two limits on the report. takes_oneself is called only from used_on, on a use step, so its yes on lines with no use changes nothing (in the replay: yes on 40 lines, none with a use step). ## scenes2-7: A picklock ability used on a lock is checked for its cooldown but never starts one

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/law_actions.py:315`
- **Evidence:** if not ab or self.field_ready_in(ab):
    return None
...
setattr(c, pool, pools.current(c, pool) - cost)
return ab
- **What a player or the owner meets:** on_unlock -> pay_picklock -> pay_field_ability('picklock'): the cost is paid and the tier's bonus added, and field_cooldown_start is never called (scenes/arc_actions.py:321 calls it for speak_corpse after the same helper; the ability's own use starts it at scenes/world.py:4151). So the same ability that waits cooldown_minutes between caches boosts every lock in a row, limited only by stamina or mana, and the readiness check in the helper can only fail because of a cache.
- **Fix:** It is a rule choice for the owner, so settle it in one place: make the helper one 'spend a field ability' step that pays and starts the cooldown together (and drop the separate call in arc_actions.py:321), or, if the edge is meant on every lock, drop the readiness test so a cache use does not silently switch it off. Either way let on_unlock decide whether the ability is used (Siege Breaker, a hopeless lock) before it is spent, and share the cost sum with world.py 4112-4117, which repeats it. Note a 60 minute cooldown against 3 to 20 minute tries changes the balance of retrying a jammed lock; test it on speak_corpse as well as a lock.
- **The finder's first fix:** Start the cooldown inside pay_field_ability, where the cost is paid, so no caller can pay without it (and drop the separate call in arc_actions).
- **The check:** Seen happening. A moderate picklock ability (cooldown rule 60 minutes) used on three locks in a row, 8 game minutes each: every try got bonus 20.0, paid its stamina, and left no cooldown entry (cd entry None, ready_in 0 each time). After field_cooldown_start(pl) the same call gave bonus 0.0, paid nothing and noted 'You try it by hand.', so the readiness test at law_actions.py:315 is live but only a dungeon cache use (field_apply, field_actions.py:73) can ever set it. speak_corpse through the same helper starts its cooldown in the caller (arc_actions.py:321). Nothing pins either reading: locks_test has no cooldown check, GOALS.md and docs/design do not mention it, and field.yaml is ambiguous (header: 'each ability then needs time to recover'; the picklock blurb: 'a strong edge on any lock you pick'). Adjacent fault on the same path, also run: with Siege Breaker ('need no tools') the ability is still paid for and still counted, because law_actions.py:367 adds boost into bonus before 370-371 zero it (base bonus 0.0, with Siege Breaker and the ability 20.0, stamina 20.0 -> 14.4, and the telling does not name the ability).
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/law_actions.py 310-394, scenes/field_actions.py 33-74 and 619-643, engine/field.py 25-36, scenes/arc_actions.py 314-328, scenes/world.py 4106-4153; searched every tracked .py for pay_field_ability, pay_picklock, field_cooldown_start (callers: field_actions 73 and 848, world 4151, arc_actions 321; none on the lock path). Read tools/sim/locks_test.py: it pins the boost, the cost and 'too drained, by hand', nothing about the cooldown. Ran a CPU-only script on simlib's stub (campaign audit_check_scenes2_2, removed): scratchpad/audit/work/check_scenes2_2.py and check_scenes2_2b.py.

Cover the class by the plan, not by words: a talk aimed at a companion stays theirs when the person the line names is already the target of another step of the same plan (true of all four logged cases; the rule used_on applies through rest_of_plan), and when the line speaks to the party (hold on a PARTY address instead of dropping it at line 66). The replay holds 4 firings (cases 1021, 1545, 1679, 1685) and all four re-aim words for the group at the innkeeper, butcher, chandler or tinker. One correction to the report's evidence: on those lines addressing.addressed returns nothing (printed: []), so lines 66-75 are not what moves the talk; the older rule at 79-84 does (named_here: the one person the line names). Line 66's filter matters only when a sentence opens with the party ('I nod to the innkeeper. Everyone, we leave at dawn.': ('*',) found, thrown away, then the old rule sends it to the innkeeper). No test pins this: the tests and corpus pin one-talk lines ('I ask the guard who he serves', 'I talk to the guard about the road'), and doc 21 B1 states the opposite intent ('a talk aimed at a companion is not turned to someone else only because the line names them'). ## unmeasured-tasks-11: Maren's first appearance: the model's passage is kept only if it spells 'greatsword' and 'crest' or 'badge', and the test meant for the enamelled A matches the article 'a'

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/mentor_actions.py:188`
- **Evidence:** `if not (text and "greatsword" in low and ("crest" in low or "badge" in low) and " a " in f" {low} " and "maren" not in low):` / `text = ""` (188-189). `" a "` is true of any English passage; the facts handed to the narrator say 'an enamelled A at its centre' (data/world/mentor.yaml:182).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The narrator writes 'a great sword', 'a two-handed blade' or 'the guild's emblem on her shoulder': a sound passage (about 1,750 tokens read and 155 to 260 written, 7 to 10 s on the minimum card, the first narration of the lesson) is thrown away for the written one. A passage that leaves the A out altogether passes. tools/sim/mentor_test.py:511 pins only the case where sword and crest are both missing.
- **Fix:** As proposed, with one precision: keep the must-show items and their accepted wordings in data/world/mentor.yaml beside look_event and check them in one small function. The letter has to be tested on the text as written, not lowered, and must not match a sentence that opens with the article 'A' (accept wordings such as 'enamelled A', 'an A', 'the letter A', quoted or not). Add the two missing test cases: a passage without the A falls back, a passage with 'great sword' is kept. Keep the fallback to the written passage; do not turn the check into a send-back, which would cost a second call.
- **The finder's first fix:** Hold the must-show items and their accepted wordings in data/world/mentor.yaml (greatsword, great sword, two-handed sword; crest, badge, emblem) and check them in one small function; drop the ' a ' clause or test for the letter as the facts give it.
- **The check:** The line is as quoted (mentor_actions.py:188, unchanged since the first commit). My script, using the same expression, printed: the test's good passage True; the same facts with 'a great sword' False; with 'the guild's emblem' for the crest False; a passage with a greatsword and a crest and no A at all True; a passage that shows the letter as an enamelled 'A' in quotes and happens to hold no article False. So the clause ' a ' in the lowered text tests for the article, not the letter. It lets through a passage without her rank, which mentor_test.py:87 ('her A rank is shown in the meeting, not repeated in the lesson') shows is meant to be seen there, and the lesson does not say it again. No test pins either case: mentor_test.py:511 covers only a passage with neither sword nor crest. How often the model writes 'great sword' or 'emblem' is not known (the facts it is handed say 'greatsword' and 'crest', and no recording holds the lesson); when it does, a sound passage and its call (7 to 10 s on the minimum card) are thrown away for the written one.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/mentor_actions.py 167-196, data/world/mentor.yaml 165-189, tools/sim/mentor_test.py 72, 87 and 499-517; git blame on line 188. Ran the line's own test on five passages (audit/work/um2_lists.py).
