## stale-copies-4: A failed haggle's cooling of the seller is never saved: the same line's pulse reads the people here again and the change is gone

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/pastime_actions.py:112`
- **Evidence:** scenes/pastime_actions.py:112-116 `regard.step(seller, self.acting, H['annoyed_trust'], cause='annoyed', ...)`, then advance, narrate and `return`: no save_npc and no notice. scenes/world.py:701 then replaces self.residents with fresh loads. Probe with the check fixed to fail: trust in the save 51 before, 51 after the haggle's line, 51 after a look and a wait, the scene's copy 51 too, moves [(1, 'talk')]. Harness: a held copy with a trust move that is in no save, just before run_pulse re-reads, in the town session and the routine probe.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Any haggle that fails. The player reads that the seller is a little cooler for being asked, and nothing has changed: data/rules/pastimes.yaml:19 `annoyed_trust: -2` has no effect in play, so haggling at every purchase costs nothing. tools/sim/pastimes_test.py:96 passes because it reads the scene's object straight after calling on_haggle, with no turn around it. By reading only: the All or Nothing perk's bad_trust (scenes/check_actions.py:54), set by the same failed roll, goes the same way here.
- **Fix:** The smallest right fix is what the other trust steps in scenes/ do: save the record after the step (on_haggle, and bad_failure for the perk). Publishing a deed through self.notice is right only if the owner wants a failed haggle remembered and seen by companions, and a new event saves nothing unless its reaction is in data. For the kind (a change on a held copy nobody saves) the check is stale-copies-6's comparison of the scene's held copies with the save where the scene re-reads them; run it over the regard.step sites (scenes/work_actions.py:163, scenes/passive_hooks.py:121, scenes/inventory_actions.py:529 and 657 show no save within four lines; I did not follow them further). Test through ws.play, reading the save: a failed haggle with a resident and with a seller on routine, and a failed insight check under All or Nothing.
- **The finder's first fix:** Send the deed through self.notice with a domain event of its own, as Gambled and Persuaded are, so the reaction saves the record it is handed. For the class (a change on a held copy that nobody saves), stale-copies-6: the commit writes every record that differs from what was read, and the suite's check fails when the scene re-reads a copy that differs from the save. Test through ws.play, reading the save.
- **The check:** A resident seller (the baker, trading_square, seed 7) and a seller here on routine (the herbalist, seed 11), the same in both: trust moves the engine made on the seller in that line: [(-2, 'annoyed')]; trust in each save of them in that line: []; save and scene before (51, [(1, 'talk')]), after the haggle's line (51, [(1, 'talk')]), one line later the same. tools/sim/pastimes_test.py:95-96 calls on_haggle directly and reads the scene's object, so it passes. Two corrections. 'Never saved' is 'saved only by accident': a resident's held copy would be written if something else saves it before the pulse re-reads (doings.assign when their doing changes during that advance); it did not happen in either run. The All or Nothing part was read, not run: bad_failure (check_actions.py:54) steps trust with no save; on run_checks' social path a later save usually carries it, on a haggle or an insight check nothing does.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/pastime_actions.py on_haggle (91-123), scenes/check_actions.py resolve and bad_failure (23-59), scenes/world.py run_pulse (699-702), engine/doings.py assign (line 84 saves a person whose doing changed), tools/sim/pastimes_test.py:93-96, and the 24 regard.step call sites outside tools/sim. Ran sk_stale_copies_1_people.py (argument haggle) through ws.play with the die (checks.roll) fixed to fail and the game's own resolve, with spies on regard.step and store.save_npc.

## scenes3-7: A walk to a kept landmark that is stopped by a won ambush resumes toward a stop already taken off the map

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/road_actions.py:546`
- **Evidence:** go_landmark lines 541-546: after `self.travel_route(stop["id"], text)` a walk stopped on the way runs `elif stop["id"] in self.world.places:` / `self.world.remove_place(stop["id"])`. A hostile road event on that walk kept `resume=(route[-1] if resume is None else resume)` (line 387), the landmark stop's id; road_fight_over line 725 puts it in resume_pending and resume_road line 756 calls `self.on_move(ActionIntent(kind="move", destination=dest), text)` with an id no longer in world.places. Read, not run.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player walks back to a sight kept on a road, is ambushed on the way and wins. 'You get your breath back and carry on.' is followed by a refusal that names a place id (road_ plus eight characters), and the walk does not go on.
- **Fix:** Make the resume name what survives: when go_landmark's walk is stopped short (me.location != stop id) and the stop the player now stands at carries resume or bound equal to the landmark stop's id, write the landmark's own id (m["id"], sight_...) there instead; in resume_road, a dest that is a kept landmark's id goes through go_landmark(mark, text) (the stop is made again), anything else through on_move as now. That covers the pane, the typed line and the way-out path alike, and keeps taking player_of(self.acting). As a guard for every case of the kind, resume_road should not hand on_move an id that is no longer on the map: say the held-walk line by name, or let the walk end quietly, never a refusal printing a raw id (line 752 has the same raw-id fallback when there is no room for a passage). Leaving the landmark stop on the map instead is the weaker choice: nothing would tidy it after a lost or fled fight.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the landmark's own id as the resume target and have resume_road go through go_landmark for it (the stop is made again), or leave the landmark stop in place while a resume names it.
- **The check:** The quoted code is there: line 387 `resume=(route[-1] if resume is None else resume) if hostile else ""`, lines 545-546 `elif stop["id"] in self.world.places:` / `self.world.remove_place(stop["id"])`, line 756 `self.on_move(ActionIntent(kind="move", destination=dest), text)`. The script printed, for the pane click: `ambush stop resume: road_d97ee1df | bound: road_d97ee1df | text: ''`, `resume target still on the map: False`, `after the fight: resume_pending = ('road_d97ee1df', '')`, `after resume_road: at road_35c9c568 (did not move) | minutes walked 0`, with the notes `You get your breath back and carry on.` then `You look about for road d97ee1df, but nothing here goes by that name. From here the ways you know lead to Parth.` The same happened for the typed line `Let's go back there.` (destination `the overturned cart`). One correction to the finding's reach: a typed line that itself names the sight wholly (`We go back to the overturned cart by the river.`) DOES walk on (216 minutes, standing at the sight), by accident: on_move finds no such place and line 3469 reads the kept text again with landmark_named, which calls go_landmark afresh. So the fault shows for the Places pane's Go button (go_landmark(mark, "") at world.py 3174) and for lines whose own words do not name the sight wholly. It also needs a walk of more than 6 hours to the sight (roads.plan_legs gives one leg, and so no event, up to 360 minutes) and a won ambush. No state is corrupted: the player stands at the ambush stop, joined to both real ends of the road, and can set out again; the refusal is also written to the turn's record and the refusal log. The ambush stop's `bound` names the removed stop too.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/road_actions.py (run_journey, road_event 293-420, go_landmark 527-546, road_fight_over 717-728, resume_road 747-756), scenes/world.py on_move 3438-3515 and places_click 3167-3175, engine/roads.py make_stop, world/campaign.py remove_place. Searched tools/sim for go_landmark / resume_pending: road_sights_702_test and road_seen_709_test never put a fight on the walk to a landmark, so nothing pins it. Then ran a CPU-only script against simlib's stub (scratchpad/audit/work/scenes3_2_landmark.py, campaign audit_check_scenes3_2, removed afterwards): a sight kept on the King's Road 432 minutes from Parth, road.yaml hostile and chance_per_leg raised so a leg brings an ambush, the fight ended by the real CombatScene.finish() with over='victory', then resume_road() called as scenes/world.py line 2370 does. Three ways of setting out: the Places pane's Go (#goto sight id), a typed line that names the sight wholly, and a typed line that does not name it (the interpreter's destination did).

## scenes3-9: A quiet shop-pane purchase calls the narrator when the Tavern Ear perk is owned

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/shop_actions.py:210`. **Same place:** scenes3-12
- **Evidence:** shop_click line 359 calls `self.buy_ware(seller, ware, quiet=True)`; buy_ware lines 209-210: `if ware.kind in world_perks.P["tavern_ear"]["wares"]:` / `self.tavern_ear(seller)` whatever quiet is, and scenes/passive_hooks.py:375 tavern_ear ends in `self.narrate("Over a drink the player picks up the talk of the room ...")`. The module's opening lines say a button click makes 'no narrated scene and no model call'. tools/sim/perks_world_test.py:133 calls tavern_ear directly, never through a pane click. Read, not run.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A player with Tavern Ear clicks to buy an ale in the shop pane at an inn. The click waits on a narrator call (which can fail or be refused for budget) although the note printed just before it already lists the troubles and who is hiring.
- **Fix:** Give tavern_ear a quiet argument and pass buy_ware's own through: on a pane click the note alone is shown (it holds the troubles, the hiring and who has something to ask), and the passage is asked for only on a typed purchase. This is engine code, no prompt rule, and covers both wares and every quiet caller. To keep the class shut, add to shop_click_test a click made while owning the perk that checks the stub's call counts did not move, so any later hook reached from a quiet purchase is caught too.
- **The finder's first fix:** Pass quiet through to tavern_ear: on a pane click show its note alone (it carries the facts) and skip the passage; a typed purchase keeps it.
- **The check:** The quoted code is there: shop_actions.py 209-210 `if ware.kind in world_perks.P["tavern_ear"]["wares"]:` / `self.tavern_ear(seller)` with no regard to quiet, and passive_hooks.py 375 `self.narrate("Over a drink the player picks up the talk of the room - " ...)`; the module docstring line 5 says 'A button click runs quietly: one line in the log, no narrated scene and no model call.' The script printed: `--- without Tavern Ear: paid 5; model calls made by the click: none`, `--- with Tavern Ear: paid 5; model calls made by the click: {'Narration': 1}` and the same again on a second click, each time after the note `Over the drink, the room talks (Tavern Ear): the town's troubles: ...; who is hiring: the guild board has ...`, which already carries every fact. The call is made only when there is something to tell (a trouble, a board row or someone with a request; otherwise tavern_ear prints one line and returns), and for a meal as well as a drink. It is not a call inside a transaction: a command sets collecting, so narrate becomes a passage operation run after the command commits (command_input's run_passages). So the cost is one narrator call per click (narrate in the played run: median 2.7 s, max 4.4 s, about 10,000 prompt characters) and a draw on the line's budget, on a path the module and its test say makes none. Wrong state: none.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/shop_actions.py (module docstring, buy_ware 142-227, shop_click 349-376), scenes/passive_hooks.py tavern_ear 350-376, scenes/world.py command_input 1116-1125, input 1074-1093 and narrate 3020-3035, data/rules/perks.yaml line 75 (`tavern_ear: {wares: [drink, meal]}`). Searched tools/sim: perks_world_test.py calls ws.tavern_ear directly with ws.narrate replaced by a lambda (line 116), and shop_click_test.py (whose docstring says 'no model call') never owns the perk, so no test pins a passage on a click. Ran a CPU-only script against simlib's stub (scratchpad/audit/work/scenes3_2_tavern.py, campaign audit_check_scenes3_2, removed afterwards): at Parth's inn, `ws.play("#shopbuy ware <innkeeper> ale")` through the real input path, counting the stub's calls by schema, without and with the perk. Read the played run's by-task summary for what a narrate call costs.

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `scenes/world.py:817`. **Same place:** world_py-8, llm-flow-6

## min-card-7: People a place still lacks are asked for after the line is typed and before its budget opens: up to three uncounted tries with only the 120 s hang guard

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1063`
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:1061-1063 `text = console.ask(main=True)` / `self.apply_backfill()` / `self.repopulate()`, and :847 `self.residents = populate_place(self.store, self.world, place_id, ...)`; budget.open() is in new_input (:1209), after it. engine/budget.py:266-267: deadline() is None with no budget open, so llm/llama.py:241 falls to config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT (120).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A place whose first people could not be written at an entry made outside a line (`_people_missing`, :823). Every line typed while the player stays there then starts with populate_place: 9.6 s at the recorded median on the minimum card, 29 s if all three tries are used, 94.6 s if one writes to its 3,000-token ceiling, none of it charged, and the line's own 55 s begins after it. Not run here; read from the code. The same kind as world_py-3 (a call made with no budget open), on a different path.
- **Fix:** Make it one rule, not this site: once the loop has begun, the main thread makes no model call with no budget open. (1) repopulate() stops asking in the foreground. backfill.start takes the place whose first people are still missing as well as a peopled one (today it returns at `not state.populated`), so the retry is always the background job start_backfill() already begins at :1060, and the edge only collects what has finished (apply_backfill), never settles or waits; the flag clears when the place gains people. A session that must replay exactly still takes them at the edge (wait_all=streams.STRICT), unchanged. If the owner would sooner have the people there for the line just typed, the other shape is the one f596 already has for its edge ask (take_up_acts at world.py:1815, docs/design/14_phase2_plan.md:144-148 'Its price falls on the next turn's budget as a required call'): an asked operation at the head of the input, never a bare call, because the write fence is armed there. Either way read the place from self.player_of(self.acting), not self.player. (2) Hold the kind with a ratchet beside operation.note_legacy in llm/gateway.py: note any main-thread call made with no budget open after the opening, and assert the set empty over a stub play that includes a pane walk, which also holds world_py-3; test it on that case, not this one.
- **The finder's first fix:** Ask it where the rest of the place's people are already asked: from start_backfill() on the background lane before the wait for the player's line (scenes/world.py:1060), so it is written while the player reads and never holds a typed line; or, if it must stay in the foreground, make it the input's first step inside the budget.
- **The check:** Seen happening. Opened standing in a town never peopled, the opening's three tries failing: after the line 'look around' was typed the next call was ResidentSet on the main thread with budget_open False, deadline None, in_operation False; only then ActionPlan with budget_open True and deadline 55.0. The same call was made when the player typed 'quit' (before the save) and for an empty line; with every try failing, each input paid three uncounted tries (an empty line, then two lines: 3 + 3 + 3) and each line's budget still began at 55.0. The quoted code is as stated: world.py:1061-1063, :847, budget.open() at :1209, budget.py:266-267, llama.py:241 `limit = float(self.no_deadline or config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT) if deadline is None else float(deadline)`; _ask passes max_tokens=3000 and retries defaults to 2. Price agrees: populate_place answers price at a median 9.8 s on the minimum card (9.7 s in the played session). What narrows it, and why it stays low: (1) a new game cannot reach it: it opens in south_fields, which has no residents (no ResidentSet call at a new game's opening in the probe); the only entry outside an operation in play is run():1000 at a load, so the state is a save loaded standing in a place that lacks people (a resident gone, a role the world added, a backfill unfinished) whose ask then fails every try. (2) None of the 263 recorded populate_place calls in the tracked runs, nor the 6 in the played session, failed even one try. (3) In that reachable state the finder's first fix is already what happens: with a peopled town, one resident marked gone and the load's ask failing three tries, start_backfill() at :1060 began a background ResidentSet, it answered while the player read, and the typed line made no ResidentSet call at all. The foreground ask at the edge came only when the background job failed too (seen: one main-thread ResidentSet, no budget, before ActionPlan); and when the line was typed while the background job was still writing (stand-in sleeping 1.5 s), the line's first budgeted call came 1.53 s after it was typed, so repopulate's settle waits on that job outside the budget as well. backfill.start refuses a place never peopled (npc/backfill.py:38 `if not (state.populated and slots): return False`), which is the case the stub test pins (tools/sim/goes_on_525_test.py:275-288 enters parth directly and asserts only that run() calls repopulate, not where). The title's 'every line typed while the player stays' holds only while the ask keeps failing: one answer clears the flag.

## trace-save-4: When a line's first operation fails and a later one stands, the input's count goes back and is never saved: the next line with the same words gets the same dice and the same operation ids

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1607`. **Same place:** trace-turn-4
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:1607 `self.store.reload_meta()                           # the clock the operation advanced goes back with it` also takes back meta.steps and story_steps that new_input added (1204-1206) and nothing has saved yet. asked_operation puts meta back after a stand-down (1471, 1486); abandon() (1447) does not. Run under the stub (scratchpad audit/work/trace_save_count.py): after a line whose waiting act's operation failed and whose other operations stood, steps stayed 1; the same words typed again: 5 of 6 operations carry ids already in the record (20 records, 15 distinct ids).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A character has an act waiting for its ruling (f596). On the next line take_up_acts runs it first; the model's answer fails or the code faults; the operation is rolled back and give_back reloads the saved meta; the branch at world.py:629-631 and the rest of the line go on and commit under the old count, with dice drawn at the new one. The save keeps count N for a line played at N+1, so the next line starts at N+1 again: typed with the same words (a second 'I look around', 'I wait') it draws the same dice and the same operation ids as the line before. find_operation and the presentation entry (keyed by id, f467) can then answer for the wrong operation, and engine/recording.py:272 and tools/rerun.py:413 pick a line's operations by a count two lines share.
- **Fix:** Keep the input's count apart from the clock, for every operation and not only the waiting act: new_input notes the count it gave on the turn's context; give_back, after reload_meta, puts that count back while the input is open; the input's close gives it back (reload_meta) only when no operation of the input stood, which replaces the give-back at understood() 1693-1694 and still covers a first deed that failed (turn() 1823 and 1839), so a line not taken and said again meets the same dice as today. The count then reaches the save with the first operation that stands, whatever its index (save_player already writes the meta at every commit). The proposed wording, leaving the give-back to understood() alone, would stop a failed first action giving its count back. Test with a faulting board refresh and clarify as well as the waiting act.
- **The finder's first fix:** In give_back keep the input's count (steps, story_steps) when the line goes on after the failure, taking back only the clock; leave the count's give-back to understood() at world.py:1694, which already does it when nothing of the line stood. Test it with a failing world operation other than the waiting act.
- **The check:** The quoted code is there (world.py:1607, 1204-1206, 1471 and 1486, 1447, 629-631, 1694; recording.py:272; rerun.py:413). What my run printed, with the fault: line 2 'I wait a while.' drew the dice key '3:2:I wait a while.', committed seven operations all recorded at steps 1, and the save kept steps 1; line 3 with the same words drew the same key '3:2:I wait a while.', 5 of its 6 operation ids were already in the record (20 records, 15 distinct ids), and find_operation answered with the older record (revision 10, the newest of that id 18). Control without the fault: keys 3:2 then 3:3, no id shared, 19 records and 19 ids. This breaks the rule written in engine/streams.py:13-14 (two inputs never share a key, ids from the ids stream never repeat in a save), so item, contract and thread ids made by both lines would repeat too. The trigger is narrower than reported: a model that gives no ruling does not fail the operation, because act.ask catches LLMError (engine/act.py:198-200) and take_up spends the try inside the same operation; my second run, with the ActRuling call raising LLMError, committed act:waiting first at steps 2 and saved steps 2. Only a fault of the game's own inside the waiting act's operation does it, and then only when the next line has the same words. Two more first operations can fail while the line goes on, each also only on a fault: the board's refresh during the understanding (scenes/guild_actions.py:108; engine/stakes.py:95 catches LLMError) and clarify (scenes/audit_actions.py:220, after which the tail commits). So the defect is real and seen, its reach small: low, not medium. Not recorded in GOALS.md or docs/design; docs/design/20_phase3_plan.md 415-417 notes only a neighbouring id collision (a typed #start).
- **How it was checked:** Read new_input, operation(), abandon, give_back, asked_operation, understood, take_up_acts and turn() (scenes/world.py:621-632, 1196-1310, 1440-1499, 1597-1625, 1675-1695, 1799-1895), save_player and commit_operation (storage/campaign.py:503-513, 586-612), engine/streams.py, engine/act.py ask/take_up/missed, engine/recording.py:265-275, tools/rerun.py:405-416; looked for every other operation that can be a line's first and fail while the line goes on. Ran two scripts of my own (scratchpad audit/work/check_trace_save_1_count.py and check_trace_save_1_count2.py, campaign audit_check_trace-save_1, removed): a real waiting act in the save with act.decide made to raise, a control without it, and the ruling's model call made to fail with LLMError.
- **Already recorded:** Not written down. docs/design/20_phase3_plan.md 415-417 notes only a neighbouring id collision (a player who types #start).

## trace-turn-4: An operation that fails before the line's first commit takes the input's count back while the line goes on: the input is never counted, and the next one shares its dice key and operation ids

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `scenes/world.py:1607`. **Same place:** trace-save-4
- **Evidence:** give_back: `self.session.rollback(self, op.id if op is not None else "")` / `self.store.reload_meta()   # the clock the operation advanced goes back with it` (understood() does the same at 1693-1694 for a plan of None). asked_operation puts the count back after a stand-down (1486 `self.store.meta = meta`); a failure does not. Stub run (audit/work/trace_turn_demo.py, case E): with an act left waiting and its operation failing at the next input, that input's operations (act:waiting:missed, action:look, passage, world, arrival, law, tail) all committed under steps 8, the previous input's count, and the saved steps/story_steps stayed 8; the same line typed again ran as steps 9 and drew seven operation ids identical to the earlier input's ('c83ee22a182f', '8d540699cdc8', '667a38d0061c', ...).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Any failure before a line's first commit when the line then goes on: the waiting act's operation (take_up_acts, world.py:628-631, after which act:waiting:missed commits), a board refresh during the understanding (scenes/guild_actions.py:105-109), or the audit's walk to someone across town failing (scenes/audit_actions.py:102, for one when populate_place fails at the door), after which the tail still commits. new_input's +1 is lost, every record of the input is filed under the previous input's steps, and the next input begins its streams from the same (seed, story_steps). Typed the same, the natural retry, it meets the same dice and the same ids from the 'ops' and 'ids' streams although state was committed in between. engine/streams.py:13 promises 'two inputs never share a key ... so ids made from the ids stream never repeat in a save'.
- **Fix:** The reporter's fix is right. In give_back, keep steps and story_steps across reload_meta (the clock and the turn still go back), and give the count back in one place, the close of the input (input()'s finally), when nothing of the line committed (understood()'s reload at 1693-1694 is the same give-back and belongs there too). save_player writes the meta inside every commit, so the kept count is saved by the next operation that stands even though it is not index 0. tools/sim/executor_463_test.py's 'count given back' case stays true because turn() closes its own input. Add a case: a world operation fails before the first commit, the line goes on, and the next input's key and ids differ.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the input's count across a failed operation while the line lives: after reload_meta in give_back and understood, put steps and story_steps back to the input's values (as asked_operation already does for a stand-down), and give the count back once, at the input's close, only when nothing of the line committed. tools/sim/executor_463_test.py's 'the input's count given back' case stays true.
- **The check:** My run: with one act left waiting, the next input 'I look around.' began its dice from (7, 3, 'I look around.'); act:waiting failed at index 0 carrying steps 3; act:waiting:missed, action:look, passage, world, arrival, law and tail then all committed carrying steps 2, the previous input's count; the scene's and the save's steps and story_steps stayed 2. The same line typed again began from the same key (7, 3, 'I look around.') and five of its operation ids were ids the earlier input had used; the save's record of operations then held five ids twice, each on two different operations (for one, 'd2502bca007c' on act:waiting:missed and on action:look). A third time, with nothing failing, the key was (7, 4, ...) and no id was shared. The cause is as reported: give_back reloads the meta from the save, which does not hold the input's count until an operation commits, and nothing puts it back as asked_operation does after a stand-down. Severity lowered: it needs a fault inside an operation that runs before the line's first commit (the board's stakes call catches its own model failure at engine/stakes.py:92-99, so there it takes a fault of the game's own), and the shared key needs the same words typed next; none of the 126 played lines had a rolled-back operation. One more effect the report does not name: engine/recording.py:272 and tools/rerun.py:413 collect an input's operations by steps == meta.steps, so after such an input they would also pick up the previous input's.
- **How it was checked:** Read new_input (scenes/world.py:1196-1209), operation() (1224-1309: the index, first_of_line, save_player before the commit), give_back (1597-1625), abandon (1440-1449), asked_operation (1466-1498), understood (1675-1695), take_up_acts (621-632), ensure_board (scenes/guild_actions.py:96-113), audit_plan (scenes/audit_actions.py:96-106), commit_operation and save_player (storage/campaign.py:586-612, 503-513) and engine/streams.py. Read tools/sim/executor_463_test.py and story_dice_639_test.py: they pin the count given back when nothing of the line stood, and that no two inputs share a key in ordinary play; nothing covers a failure before the first commit with the line going on. Ran my own stub script through ws.play() with a different fault from the reporter's (act.take_up raising a RuntimeError; audit/work/skeptic_trace_turn_c.py, campaign audit_check_trace-turn_1, removed). Looked for the state in three played sessions.

## trace-turn-3: The 'NOT DONE this turn' row for a fourth action and beyond is added after the line's passage is written, so the narrator never sees it

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `scenes/world.py:2466`
- **Evidence:** after_steps: `ledger.add("not_done", steps=undone, say="NOT DONE this turn, never show them done: " + "; ".join(undone) + ".")   # (f416)`. turn() calls after_steps at line 1872, after the 'passage' operation at 1857-1858 (handle() has the same order, 2329-2330); the narration request reads `told=ledger.told()` at 3077. Stub run (audit/work/trace_turn_demo3.py): order was 'passage written; ledger.told() then held: []' and only then 'ledger not_done row added'; the narration request held no NOT DONE and did hold the fourth thing ('wait an hour'), because it carries the typed line.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** 'I look around, search the stalls, look again, then wait an hour.' The plan is capped at three (llm/contracts.py ActionPlan), the passage is asked for with the whole typed line and the events of the steps that ran, and nothing tells the narrator the fourth was not done. Only afterwards is the row added and the player told 'Three things at a time. Left undone: waiting an hour.' The passage can show the wait done, against the state; the row is read, if at all, by a later world telling of the same turn.
- **Fix:** Add the row where the plan is accepted, at the end of understand() once audit_plan has returned a plan (dropped_steps is known there, and both turn() and handle() pass through it), so the line's passage is told it. Leave the note to the player and the refusals row in after_steps, after the passage, as f418 wants. Add a case to tools/sim/plan_limit_test.py that the line's narration request holds NOT DONE for the step left undone, through turn() and through handle().
- **The finder's first fix:** Add the not_done ledger row when the plan is taken, before step 0 runs (dropped_steps is known from the interpreter's answer), and leave the player's note and the refusals row where they are; no test covers the row today, so pin the order with one.
- **The check:** The code is as quoted (`ledger.add("not_done", steps=undone, say="NOT DONE this turn, never show them done: " ...)` in after_steps, called at 1872, after the passage operation at 1857-1858). In f416 the same row was added before the passage: that commit's turn ran the steps, added the row, ran the pulse and only then called self.flush(text). f463 moved the passage ahead of what became after_steps, so this is a regression of f416's own order. My run of 'I look around, search the stalls, look again, then wait an hour.' printed the order [('narration asked', False), ('not_done row added', 'NOT DONE this turn, never show them done: waiting an hour.')]; the narration request held 'wait an hour' (the typed line) and no NOT DONE; at the turn's end the row was still 'never told'; the player then read 'Three things at a time. Left undone: waiting an hour.' Severity lowered because the state it needs is rare: the interpreter is told 'at most three', and none of the 126 lines in the three played sessions gave a plan over three (no 'undone' row in any refusals.jsonl). When it does happen the passage can show the fourth thing done, which is the fault f416 was built against.
- **How it was checked:** Read turn() (scenes/world.py:1843-1872), handle() (2324-2330), after_steps (2455-2470), interpret's dropped_steps (3280), ActionPlan (llm/contracts.py:639-663) and ledger.told (engine/ledger.py:122-132). Read the commit that added the row (git show d72db5c, f416). Read tools/sim/plan_limit_test.py: it checks the note and the refusals row, not the ledger row or its order. Ran my own stub script through ws.play() (audit/work/skeptic_trace_turn_c.py, campaign audit_check_trace-turn_1, removed). Counted plans over three in three played sessions.

## typed-patterns-5: move_to_present drops what the player says when the words open with go, run, head, walk or take me: 'Go ahead and stamp it. Who else is around here...' is left as a look

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `scenes/world.py:2567`
- **Evidence:** 2567: `if re.match(r"^\s*(?:i\s+)?(?:go|head|walk|run|hurry|travel|make my way|set off|take me)\b", text.lower()) and any(echo(b) for b in plan):` / 2568: `return [a for a in plan if not echo(a)] or plan`. No step of the plan has to be a move.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Logged line (case 1597), said to the guild clerk: 'Go ahead and stamp it. Who else is around here that we need to talk to before we head out?' The model: a talk to the clerk with the whole line as speech, and a look. After the repair: the look only; the clerk hears nothing. Stub run (work/tp/verify_a.py): the same for 'Run that by me again, what does the contract pay?'. By reading, 3 of the repair's 16 firings on 1,888 real lines were wrong; the other two (cases 818, 1668: 'I turn away from the group and start heading toward the door.') lost the walk and kept a talk to someone here, by the repair's second rule (2573-2575).
- **Fix:** The report's fix stands: corpus cases with not_by: [move_to_present], and the two-steps-from-the-same-words rule of doc 29's R3 decides it. If the owner wants it held off before R3, without a word list: the first rule drops the echoed talk only when a going step (move, explore, delve) is among the steps kept, which is what its own comment describes ('go to smith: a journey'); a look or a deal beside the talk is no journey.
- **The finder's first fix:** Both rules are the case 'two steps made of the same words', which docs/design/29_one_reader_plan.md R3 settles in code once each step says its words; a step is then dropped only when another step claims the same words. Until then the lines are corpus cases with not_by: [move_to_present]; no new word list.
- **The check:** Bench run with the reading logged for case 1597 (a talk to the clerk holding the whole line, and a look): move_to_present changed 'talk:ella_walmore look' into 'look'. The same for 'Run that by me again, what does the contract pay?' and for a line of my own, 'Go on, tell me what the contract pays.'. With the talk as the only step the plan is kept (`or plan`), so the loss needs a second step; drop_restatements does not then remove the look, which is step 0. Of the 16 firings in the replay, 1597 loses the words, 818 and 1668 lose the walk to the door by the second rule (2573-2575), 1036 ('I head toward the gate and tell the guards...') arguably loses its walk as well, and the others are right (a walk up to someone here before a sale, a contract or a hand-over). The pinned shape still works: 'go to smith' read as talk + move became the move. Rated low: 3 or 4 of 1,888 lines, the words or the walk are lost and nothing else; the player types it again.
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/world.py 2561-2575 and the repairs around it (walk_after_word, drop_restatements at scenes/plan_repairs.py 396-435). Ran scratchpad/audit/work/check_typed_patterns_1_bench.py (bench on the stub, campaign audit_check_typed-patterns_1, removed) with the readings as logged and a line of my own, and read all 16 firings of move_to_present in the first reader's replay (work/tp/bench_out.jsonl).
- **Already recorded:** The function is not named in GOALS.md or docs/design. The class is: docs/design/29_one_reader_plan.md line 30 says 21 of the 36 wrong corpus cases are 'one line read as two steps made from the same words', and R3 (f733) is its proposed answer, waiting on the owner.

## stale-copies-3: A goodbye to someone who is here on their routine is saved on an object the scene has already replaced; the next word with them writes it away

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:4013`
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:4008 `self.advance(clock.TALK_MINUTES)` runs refresh_present, whose line 604 `v = self.store.load_npc(vid)` builds a new object for everyone here who is not a resident; 4012-4013 `partings.remember(npc, text, speech)` / `self.store.save_npc(npc)` then write the old one. Probe (seed 7, the Tilted Plough at 18:00, the guild contractor): after the goodbye the save's heard ends 'Good day to you.' and the scene's copy does not; after the next line the save's said and heard have lost the goodbye pair. Harness: lost write part_from, stale save npc/life.py:458 (converse). The stale held copy was seen 12 times in the bot and town sessions.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Evening at an inn; a guild contractor, a herbalist or anyone else who is there on their routine and lives elsewhere. Say goodbye, then speak to them again before the people here are next read from the save. What partings.remember keeps 'for the repeat guard and the written fallback' is gone, so the same parting line can come again. Small in itself; it shows that any handler holding its own reference across advance() writes to an orphan for routine visitors (604), visitors (591) and bound prisoners (584).
- **Fix:** Cover every handler, not part_from alone: refresh_present hands back the object the scene already holds for anyone it loads itself (lines 584, 591 and 604: keep the present by id and reuse it), and reads them anew only where the scene reads everyone anew (run_pulse, reread_here, enter, a give-back). Then advance() cannot orphan a handler's reference. Until then part_from takes self.partner again after advance (refresh_present has already re-pointed it). Test two cases through ws.play, reading the save: a goodbye to someone on their routine followed by a word, and the same with a summons visitor (ws.visit).
- **The finder's first fix:** The lasting fix is one live record per person for the length of an operation (stale-copies-6), so refresh_present cannot swap the object under a handler; until then part_from takes the person again from the scene after advance. Test a second case of the kind: a summons visitor or a moment's visitor.
- **The check:** Seed 7, the Tilted Plough, helwyn_born (guild contractor; on routine: True; a resident object of the scene: False). Goodbye taken by the intercept ('Good day to you.', ops ['line', 'tail']): the scene's object for them changed during the line: True; the save's heard ends 'Good day to you.' and the scene's copy does not; after the next word the save reads said ['Quiet enough, most days.', 'All my life.', 'Go on.'], heard ['Good evening.', 'How long have you lived here?', 'One more thing']: the goodbye pair is gone. ## world_py-7: craft_boost lives only on the scene: the ability's cost and cooldown are saved, the boost is gone after a reload; its numbers are in code

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `scenes/world.py:4133`
- **Evidence:** on_ability: `self.craft_boost = {"light": 8, "moderate": 15, "heavy": 25}[ability.tier.value]`. engine/actor.py:127 lists craft_boost as rolled scene memory (not saved); its only readers and reset are scenes/inventory_actions.py 886, 927, 937; no stored field holds it.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player uses a crafting-focus ability (resource spent, cooldown saved with the character), then goes to the menu or closes the game before crafting. On opening the save the boost is gone while the cost and the cooldown remain. Traced in code, not run.
- **Fix:** Keep the pending boost where the other pending field effects live: in the acting character's saved player.field (for example fld['craft'] = {'tier': ...}), written before the save_player already on world.py:4152, read and popped by craft_gear, and drop craft_boost from engine/actor.py ATTRS (the record is put back by the transaction). Move the three values to data/rules/field.yaml (a crafting boost table by tier) with an engine/data_check.py entry. Take the record by self.acting, not self.player. While there, decide the cooldown for abilities with no field_use (crafting, healing): either check field_ready_in for every out-of-combat ability before the cost is spent, or stop starting a cooldown nothing reads; that is one rule for the kind, not a case for this ability.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the pending boost on the saved character record and move the three tier values to data/rules with a data_check entry.
- **The check:** The quoted line is there: scenes/world.py:4133 `self.craft_boost = {"light": 8, "moderate": 15, "heavy": 25}[ability.tier.value]`, and engine/actor.py:127 lists craft_boost as ROLLED, VIEW (scene state, put back on a failed operation, never saved). The script printed: before `boost <unset> | stamina 66.0 | cd {}`; after use `boost 8 | stamina 63.55 | cd {'tempering_focus': 635}`; saved record `field keys ['cd']`, no craft_boost in the saved player; after reopening the save `boost <unset> | stamina 61.1 | cd {'tempering_focus': 640} | ready_in 30`. So the cost and the cooldown are saved and the boost is gone. The numbers-in-code half also holds: every other per-tier field number is in data/rules/field.yaml (haste, shadow, edge, treat and so on); these three are the only ones in world.py. It is an outlier, not a design: every other pending 'next thing' effect of a field ability lives in the saved player.field (haste, shadow, edge, tether; scenes/field_actions.py docstring 'State lives in player.field'), and the game tells the player 'Their next piece of work will be better for it' / 'Craft - improves the next thing you make' (engine/field.py:137). No test pins the loss as intended. What keeps it low: the script's second use straight after the first was NOT refused (`refused by cooldown: False`, stamina 63.55 -> 61.1), because on_ability only calls field_precheck when ability.field_use is set (world.py:4107) and crafting and healing abilities have none; the cooldown that line 4151 starts for them is never read outside a fight. So after a reload the player can use the ability again at once and has lost only one light stamina cost (2.45 of 66 here). Related, same store: crafting a consumable resets the boost to 0 without applying it (inventory_actions.py:886).
- **How it was checked:** Read scenes/world.py on_ability (4068-4153), scenes/inventory_actions.py 886/927/937, engine/actor.py ATTRS (127), engine/session.py begin_turn/rollback, engine/field.py and scenes/field_actions.py (cooldown store and its readers), data/rules/field.yaml. git grep over tracked files for craft_boost: five lines, all Python, none in a test, in data or in docs. Ran a CPU-only script against simlib's stub (scratchpad/audit/work/world_py_2_craft_boost.py, campaign audit_check_world_py_2, removed afterwards): a smith's Tempering Focus (crafting, light) set out_of_combat as creation gives it, used through ws.on_ability, the session closed, the same save opened again with fresh=False.

## pane-commands-4: refresh() overwrites what the fight has done to the fighter and follows only part of the character: one attribute click restores corroded armour, and after a gear change the fighter is a mix of old and new

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `services/fight.py:662`
- **Evidence:** services/fight.py:661  p.attrs = fresh.attrs
services/fight.py:662  p.ward, p.armor = fresh.ward, fresh.armor
engine/behaviors.py:247  target.counters["corroded"] = target.counters.get("corroded", 0) + step   (and the armour is cut on the next line)
Run under the stub (work/pane_commands/halfway.py): three of an ooze's after_hit calls took the fighter's armour from 5.0 to 3.893 with the counter at 24 of the cap 30; '#attradd constitution' put the armour back to 5.0 and left the counter at 24, so only 6 more can ever be taken. In gear_in_fight.py, after the gear was stripped, '#attradd strength' brought armour to 3.0 (the new gear) and left the weapon 'copper longsword' 7.0 (the old).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A player with points in hand fights an ooze, lets it corrode the armour to the cap, then spends one point: the armour is whole again and cannot be corroded further. Today this lasts only when the click is followed by a draught, because the refresh is otherwise dropped at the next typed line (pane-commands-2); once the row is saved after a refresh, as it should be, it lasts every time. Any other change a fight makes to armour or ward (a spell's shield, a sunder) goes the same way.
- **Fix:** Rather than applying differences (the ooze's cut is multiplicative, so a difference does not compose), stop changing the fighter's base armour in a fight: keep what the fight has taken as a factor on the fighter that is applied where protection is read, as Fighter.corroded already is for acid (engine/combat.py:1112-1114). Then the one Character to Fighter step can rebuild every base field at any time and lose nothing. Keep the factor exact (the product of the steps, not the percent counter) so no fight number changes. Do it with pane-commands-2, or the row save makes this one last.
- **The finder's first fix:** Make the one Character to Fighter step apply the difference between a fighter built fresh before the change and one built after it, for every field fighter_from_character sets, so what the fight itself changed is kept; fix it together with pane-commands-2 so the two are not traded for each other.
- **The check:** Printed: 'an ooze's touch three times: armor 5.0 -> 3.893, corroded counter 24 of cap 30'; 'after #attradd constitution (stood True): armor 5.0, corroded counter 24; fresh armor 5.0'. After '#gearunequip body' then '#attradd strength' the fighter's armor went to 0.0 (the new gear) while refresh by its code leaves weapon_name, weapon_damage, reach, bonuses and moves as they were. The reach is narrower than 'any other change a fight makes to armor or ward': corrosion is the only such change that lands on a player fighter. As the finder says, today the restored armour lasts only when the row is saved before the next typed line (pane-commands-2).
- **How it was checked:** Read FightService.refresh (services/fight.py:650-663: sets the three maximums, attrs, ward and armor from a fresh fighter and nothing else) and engine/behaviors.py after_hit (245-248: the counter rises and target.armor is multiplied down). Searched engine, services and scenes for every write to a fighter's armor or ward in a fight: behaviors.py:248 (ooze corrosion, can land on the player) and combat_perks.py:837 (Curse of Rust, the attacker's perk on a foe). Ran my own stub script (work/check_pane_commands_1_fight.py warrior corrode).

## aged-save-5: RE-RATE people-3: the sixteen captive names are used up between lines 1,000 and 1,500 of a fighter's play, not in 'a long campaign'; by line 6,000 ninety-two captives share them

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `services/fight.py:905`. **Same place:** people-3
- **Evidence:** services/fight.py:905 `free = [n for n in R["prisoner"]["names"] if n.split()[0].lower() not in taken] or R["prisoner"]["names"]`. Captive rows in the registry by lines played: warrior 3 at 1,000, 18 at 1,500, 52 at 2,000, 92 at 6,000; priest 4 at 1,000, 16 at 1,500, 29 at 2,000; mage 5 at 1,500, 15 at 2,500, 27 at 3,000. No people row is ever deleted (128 of 249 gone at 6,000 lines), so a name never comes free.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** From the seventeenth captive (game day 36 to 65 for the warrior, level 9 to 13) every captive takes a name an earlier person in the save had: at least 76 of the warrior's 92 by line 6,000. The earlier namesake is gone by then as a rule (all 92 were let go, killed or escaped), so what the player meets is the same sixteen names over and over, and journal and memory rows of different people under one name, more often than two of a name present at once. people-3 rated it low because the reach looked small; measured, the reach is every save after a few evenings.
- **Fix:** people-3's fix as written: build the captive's name with npc/names.py where its people and gender are decided, apart from every name in the save, so the source cannot run dry; the same call should name plain_story's people (aged-save-6). people_422_test's source check ('store.npc_names()' and 'taken.add(' in services/fight.py) has to move with it. Test with more than sixteen captives in one save, two taken in one fight among them.
- **The finder's first fix:** people-3's fix as written (the name built by npc/names.py where the captive's people and gender are decided, apart from every name in the save); aged-save-7's trim would also free the names of captives long gone.
- **The check:** The reach is as measured. Captive rows 0 / 3 / 18 / 51 / 68 / 81 at lines 500 to 3,000; all sixteen names used and fight.py's free list empty from line 1,500; captives past the first of their name 2 / 35 / 52 / 65 at lines 1,500 to 3,000 (Jessk nine times, Tobren eight by line 3,000); 88 of 180 people rows gone and none deleted, so no name comes free. The test pins the intent the other way ('a captive's name is drawn apart from every name already in the save'), so the repeat is not meant. I checked the warrior only, not the priest or the mage. Why I leave it low: at every checkpoint no two captives of one name were present together (none was held at all), every earlier namesake was gone, and an ordinary captive's name is not shown to the player until it is learned (make_prisoner sets name_known only for a leader; label() gives 'the captured bandit' until then). What the player can meet is a repeated name in a captive's own talk and in memory rows. The heavy consequence of the names running out is aged-save-6's crash, counted there. And 1,000 to 1,500 lines is the bot's pace, and the bot is built to fight (I did not measure a person's rate): at the record's 9.5 model seconds a line on the fast card that is by my estimate ten hours of play or more, not a few evenings on the minimum card.
- **How it was checked:** Read services/fight.py 889-910, scenes/arc_actions.py make_prisoner (414-454) and drop_prisoner, npc/models.py label (148-151), storage/campaign.py npc_names, data/rules/arcs.yaml:80 and tools/sim/people_422_test.py. In my 3,000-line stubbed play (warrior, seed 7, the finder's play, same day and level at every checkpoint) I read the npcs table at every 500 lines: rows of role prisoner, the names they carry, fight.py's free list and how many captives of one name were not gone.

## people-3: Captive names come from a list of sixteen, so the 'named apart from every name in the save' promise fails from the seventeenth captive

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `services/fight.py:905`. **Same place:** aged-save-5
- **Evidence:** fight.py:902-906: `taken = {n.split()[0].lower() for n in self.store.npc_names() if n}` then `free = [n for n in R["prisoner"]["names"] if n.split()[0].lower() not in taken] or R["prisoner"]["names"]` and `name = rng.choice(free)`. data/rules/arcs.yaml prisoner.names holds 16 names (Dorn, Kell, Marek, Sorin, Vask, Tobren, Hale, Garrick, Brannoc, Ferrow, Jessk, Orlen, Ruddick, Skarn, Teague, Wynn). store.npc_names() keeps every person ever made, the dead and gone included, and prisoner.chance is 0.35 a qualifying fight. The list is also one gender-neutral, people-neutral pool, though the captive's gender and people are rolled (scenes/arc_actions.py:424).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A long campaign that has freed sixteen captives: `free` is empty, the `or` falls back to the whole list, and the next captive shares a name with an earlier one (or with a resident whose first name is on the list). Two people with one name break name resolution in talk and in memories.
- **Fix:** Drop the list and build the name with npc/names.py where the captive's people and gender are decided (scenes/arc_actions.py make_prisoner rolls them after captives() has named the person): names.pick(folk, store.npc_names(), rng) gives a name of that people, apart from every name in the save, and the gender to use with it, so name, people and gender agree. pick returns a first and a family name; if captives are to keep one name, take names.build(folk, gender, rng) in the same keep-apart loop.
- **The finder's first fix:** Build the captive's name with the engine's own name builder (npc.names.pick(people, store.npc_names(), rng)), which already draws by people and gender and keeps names apart; drop the fixed list.
- **The check:** Printed: 20 captives, one a fight: Kell, Jessk, Marek, Brannoc, Teague, Garrick, Hale, Skarn, Vask, Orlen, Wynn, Dorn, Ferrow, Tobren, Sorin, Ruddick, then Hale, Ruddick, Ruddick, Marek: the 17th is the first repeat, and from there every captive repeats. With every list name already someone's first name the next captive is 'Teague' all the same. Reach is small: 16 captives at 0.35 a qualifying fight is a long campaign, and the earlier namesake has usually been freed, handed over or killed by then.
- **How it was checked:** Read services/fight.py:889-910, scenes/combat_scene.py:1297-1311 and scenes/arc_actions.py:414-449 (the name goes into NPC(name=name) unchanged; only the id is made unique), storage/campaign.py:966-968 (npc_names is every row of npcs; no code deletes a person) and data/rules/arcs.yaml:80 (16 names). Ran the real FightService.captives twenty times with a stand-in store that keeps each name given (scratchpad/audit/work/check_people_1_plain.py). tools/sim/people_422_test.py:39 only checks that the source text holds 'store.npc_names()' and 'taken.add('; nothing pins the fallback.

## shell1-4: The bot reads npc.work_offer, npc.quest_offer and npc.trust, fields the NPC record has not had since f480 and f481

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `simbot.py:1520`

- **The check:** On an NPC record: `work_offer -> AttributeError: 'NPC' object has no attribute 'work_offer'`, the same for quest_offer and trust. In the loop: `AttributeError: 'NPC' object has no attribute 'work_offer'` twice, from simbot.py:1503 cycle -> :1520 social_stop (first on day 21). rearm (:866) and befriend_master (:1564, :1572-1573) read the same missing attributes and were traced, not run. Severity lowered: it never stopped a run (2 raises in 40 game days, each costing one cycle), rearm is now rare (a death no longer takes the weapon: scenes/world.py:293 'a lighter purse and nothing else lost'), and the bot's talk and gift rows are still filled by people_pass; what is lost is the work and request rows and the allies a cataclysm's boss fight should have.
- **How it was checked:** Read simbot.py:852-870, :1509-1524, :1547-1573 and npc/models.py:100-150 (no work_offer, quest_offer or trust field; offers are in the registry since f481, trust is in regard per character since f480). Saw it in the bot's loop in the run of check_shell1_1_bot.py with only the fight wrapper fixed (warrior 3), which lives long enough to reach social_stop.

Only a tool or test that opens a folder by name reaches _import_legacy. So importing at v1 would recover the renames and the memory typing, not the offer.

Nine call sites make a memory with no minute (engine/mentor.py:491-497, scenes/banter_actions.py:215, scenes/inventory_actions.py:131 and :984). The same memory given a minute is kept and visit 0 goes. So a crafter the player has dealt with often keeps no memory of a paid commission.
- **Fix:** The report's fix is right in kind: in _trim order by a time every row has, the row's minute when it has one, else the last minute of its day. Build that from engine/clock.py's constants, not a literal day * 1440: clock.day is (WAKE_HOUR*60 + minute)//1440 + 1, so day*1440 lands WAKE_HOUR hours into the next day. Stored rows are unchanged, so no recording moves unless one trims a mixed set. Add the mixed case (a person at the cap with minutes, then a memory without one) to tools/sim/memory_rows_478_test.py. The cause at the source is that these nine sites build Memory by hand though engine/memory.py says keep() is the one way a memory is made; routing them through keep() with the minute is the fuller repair but changes stored rows, so it needs the recordings re-blessed on purpose.
- **The finder's first fix:** Order by a time every row has, in _trim: CASE WHEN minute >= 0 THEN minute ELSE day * 1440 END (stored rows unchanged). The alternative, _keep_row stamping a missing minute from store.meta.minutes, changes stored rows and so needs the goldens re-blessed.
- **The check:** Quoted lines are there (campaign.py:844-845, models.py:28). Printed: 'A. rows at the cap: 40 of 40 | commission (no minute) kept: False | visit 0 (day 1) kept: True'; 'B. mixed weights (half the rows importance 2): commission kept: False'; 'C. importance-2 gift (no minute) kept while routine rows remain: True'; 'D. all rows without a minute: commission kept: True | Visit 0 kept: False'; 'E. first to go by today's order: commission | by the proposed order: Visit 0.' The nine sites are as listed: engine/mentor.py:491-497 (six), scenes/banter_actions.py:215, scenes/inventory_actions.py:131 and :984. Reach is narrower than the title: Maren's six are her first rows (oldest anyway), the gift at :131 is importance 2 and survives while any routine row remains; the two that vanish on the save that wrote them are the commission (:984) and the clerk's (:215), both importance 1, and only on a person already holding 40 experienced rows that carry minutes. The same deed again counts up on one row (about), so 40 distinct rows on one person takes a long campaign. Rows from a save older than v10 and every hire's row are all -1 and fall to id order among themselves, which is right.
- **How it was checked:** Read storage/campaign.py save_npc, _keep_row, _trim (781-845), npc/models.py Memory, engine/memory.py, data/rules/memory.yaml; listed every Memory( and memory.keep( outside tests (git grep) and read each; read tools/sim/memory_rows_test.py (every row made without a minute) and memory_rows_478_test.py (every row with one): neither mixes the two, so no test pins this. Ran my own script audit/work/check_shell2_1_trim.py on a scratch store (removed afterwards).

## shell2-6: The check of a hire's opinions has a branch that can never report: an opinion about an id nobody has passes

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `storage/invariants.py:111`
- **Evidence:** elif aid not in ("player", "maren") and aid not in member_ids | ids and aid == x.get("about"): | pass  (lines 111-112)
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The module note lists 'a hire's opinions must be of someone' among what validate_campaign finds. Only the empty case is reported: the elif's body is `pass` and no else follows, so an opinion whose about_id names a hire who left or a person no longer in the save is never a Problem, in the tests, the long-campaign fixture or #check. The condition also builds `member_ids | ids` (every person's id) anew for each opinion, to decide nothing.
- **Fix:** Delete the no-op elif; the module note ('a hire's opinions must be of someone') already matches the one check that reports. A dangling-id check cannot be written soundly from what the save keeps today: the save has no list of former hires' ids (party_used holds 'hall:offer' keys, capped at 80, services/party.py:77-78), so an opinion of a hire who left cannot be told from an opinion of nobody. If the owner wants that check, it needs the former members' ids kept first (with a cap), then one set built before the loop (members, former members, people, every character id, Maren) and a report for an about_id that differs from its about and is in none of them.
- **The finder's first fix:** Report what the condition was written to set apart (an about_id, not a bare name, that is no member, no person and no character) in an else branch, or delete the elif.
- **The check:** Quoted lines are there (invariants.py:111-112); the elif's body is pass and no else follows, so it decides nothing. Printed: 'problems found: [party h1: an opinion of nobody: Someone is a liar.]': the opinion with about_id 'h_nobody_77' (about 'Ghost') passes unreported, as does the bare name, which is meant to. This is dead code more than a wrong result: no code path I found writes an about_id that names nobody (keep_opinions takes ids from the scene's map of the party, Maren and the character), and an opinion of a hire who has since left is legitimate and is never cleaned. The proposed else branch would be wrong as written: member_ids is filled as the loop goes, so a member's opinion of a member later in the party would be reported; it would also report opinions of hires who left, and the literal 'player' misses any other character id.
- **How it was checked:** Read storage/invariants.py whole, engine/canon.py about_id, keep_opinions and opinions_of (309-348), scenes/world.py name_ids (1187-1191), and tools/sim/safety_test.py:77-106 (it checks opinions are kept by id; it never gives validate_campaign an opinion). Ran validate_campaign in my script audit/work/check_shell2_1_legacy.py on a scratch save whose one hire holds three opinions: about an id nobody has, about nobody, and about a bare name.

## shell2-3: discard() erases a save that has a character when its database cannot be read or is from a newer build

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `storage/saves.py:169`
- **Evidence:** s = summary(name, saves_dir) | if s is not None and s["ready"]: return False | shutil.rmtree(Path(saves_dir) / name, ignore_errors=True)  (lines 168-171)
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The docstring promises 'A game with a character is never discarded', but the guard is summary()'s `ready`, which is also False when sqlite raised ('the save could not be read') and when the save is from a newer version. Checked in a scratch folder (audit/work/shell2_store_checks.py, part 4): a played save whose file was cut short reads ready=False; discard() returned True and the folder was gone, by rmtree and not by the move to _deleted that delete() makes. Latent today: the one caller (main.py:160) passes a game made in the same run. A second caller, or a database that stays locked past summary's 2 second timeout, meets it.
- **Fix:** Have summary() say which of the three it is (no character, unreadable, newer build) as a field, and let discard() erase only on a positive 'no character'; for the other two move the folder aside as delete() does and return that it was not discarded. Moving aside, not refusing, keeps main.py's path clean (a refused folder would stay in the index and show in Load as unreadable). Add the two cases to home_test.py section 8.
- **The finder's first fix:** Have summary() say which it is (no character, unreadable, newer) and let discard() act only on a positive 'no character'; otherwise refuse, or move the folder aside as delete() does.
- **The check:** Quoted lines are there (saves.py:168-171). Printed, for a save with a character: 'marked as from a newer build: ready = False | why: made by a newer version of the game: update to play it | discard() -> True | folder still there: False | in _deleted: False'; 'file cut short: ready = False | why: the save could not be read (database disk image is malformed) | discard() -> True | folder still there: False'. So the function does what the report says and its docstring's promise does not hold. But nothing in the game can reach it today: discard has one caller, main.py:160, under kind == 'new' after creation returned None, on a folder new_name() made in this run; creation never saves a player, and a new database is made at the current version. In that one path an unreadable new database being erased is the right outcome (there is no character in it). The 'locked past the 2 second timeout' route in the report therefore loses nothing today either. This is a guard on a function that erases with rmtree, to harden before a second caller arrives, not a fault a player can meet.
- **How it was checked:** Read saves.summary and saves.discard, the one caller (main.py:156-161) and scenes/goddess.py (creation never calls save_player and returns None on Main menu), and tools/sim/home_test.py:173-176 (pins discard of a game with no character, and refusal for a readable game with one; nothing unreadable or newer). Ran my own script audit/work/check_shell2_1_saves.py part 4 in a scratch folder.

For a recording with no server counts (a stub night) read_tps is None too, and engine/budget.py:42 float("None") raises ValueError at import (PROFILE = load_profile(), line 64), before engine/data_check.py can say what is wrong. In engine/budget.py load_profile take a value only when it is an int or float above 0, else the default, so a bad file reaches data_check's own line 851 and the player reads which key is wrong. Then drop the load measure in one go: card_profile.py (loads, load_s, the console's `a load`), tools/latency.py:78 and its Loads column, and tools/rerun.py:505-506 and 524-525; tools/sim/card_profile_443_test.py:34 checks load_s and changes with it.

Two corrections to the report: not every recording lacks a load (an old `tokens` row has load_duration, and tools/rerun.py:505 and 524 still add load_ms to timed.jsonl when the server was loading), and the crash needs a recording with no server counts at all (a stub recording, or a re-timing where every chat failed), which is a rare thing to --write. No test pins it: budget_data_459_test, windows_565_test and card_profile_443_test all pass numbers. ## tools1-8: The day-by-day report drops every news row that had not yet reached the town on the day it was made

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/event_trial.py:207`
- **Evidence:** for n in st.get("news", [])[was["news"]:]:
    if n["minute"] + pulse.travel_delay(self.world, n["origin"], town) <= self.t:
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A row from another town is seen once, on the day it is made, fails the arrival test and is never looked at again (the slice starts past it next day); the slice is also by the remembered length of a list the pulse caps and folds. Probe (audit/work/tools1_news.py, invasion_nobody_meets, 112 days): 285 news rows made, 283 reached the character's town by the end, the report shows 150; 131 never reported, 127 of them from another town. The judge and the owner read these lines to say what the player would have heard.
- **Fix:** Report by arrival, not by position in the list: each diff() reports every row whose minute plus travel_delay to the character's town is at or before now and whose identity (origin, text, minute) is not yet in a reported set, and prunes that set to the rows still in the list (so it is capped by NEWS_KEEP). That covers late arrivals, the cap, a folded row and the second diff() of a day in one rule.
- **The finder's first fix:** Key rows by identity (minute, origin, text), keep those not yet arrived as pending, and report each on the day it arrives.
- **The check:** Lines 207-209 are as quoted. Probe printed: `news rows made during the run: 43; reached the character's town by the end: 36; 'news in' lines in the report: 18`, `reached the town and never reported: 18; of those with a travel delay above 0: 18; with delay 0: 0`, `rows with a travel delay that WERE reported: 0`, delays of the unreported 0.5, 0.6 and 5.3 days. So every row from another town is lost, even one half a day away, because the row is looked at once and the slice starts past it the next day. The module's docstring says the report holds `the news that reached their town`. The list never reached NEWS_KEEP (300) in this run (max 43); at the cap the length stops growing and the slice would be empty from then on, and a tale told again is moved to the end without the length changing. A tool's report only: no game state, and event_eval's `lines: [news in, ...]` only needs one such line.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/event_trial.py take() and diff() (154-217), engine/pulse.py travel_delay (191-199), add_news and cap_news (954-1003), tools/event_eval.py judge (the `lines` expectation). Ran my own probe (audit/work/skeptic_tools1_8.py) on a case other than the reporter's, war_talked_through, with the Trial's diff() unchanged and the news list watched beside it; save audit_check_tools1_2, removed.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/12_foundations_survey.md:115 (section I, world_state) lists tools/event_trial.py:198-210 among the tools that slice lists by remembered length; the rows lost to travel delay are not written down anywhere.

## tools1-12: travel_line gives up by adding a spawn, person, hall or town id to given_up, which is only ever read as path ids

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/eventrun.py:396`
- **Evidence:** if self.stuck[key] > 12:
    self.given_up.add(key[1] if isinstance(key[1], str) else "")
# line 241 and others: p["id"] not in self.given_up
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Only the species, clear and find goals pass the path id as key[1]; hunt passes a spawn id, persuade an npc id, contract a hall id, learn and stand a town id. For those the note "cannot reach X: giving up on hunt" is written, the counter resets and goal() hands back the same goal: 12 more lines, forever, never trying the event's other paths. The counter also counts lines typed, not hops that failed (the docstring says three times). Traced in code, not played; the world is at most 8 hops from Parth, so it shows when a hop keeps failing.
- **Fix:** travel_line returns three things apart: arrived, a line to type, or gave up; act_on never treats gave up as arrived. Count only hops after which the character did not move (compare the location with the one before the last hop). On giving up, record what the goal is about in the table that goal() reads for it: avoid_until for a spawn (as the deaths rule already does), tries for a person, given_up for a path id, a skip set for a town, so the next goal() moves on to another path.
- **The finder's first fix:** Pass what is given up explicitly (the path id, or an avoid entry for a spawn or person) and count only hops that did not move the character.
- **The check:** Real campaign: the game refused the hop (`The way through Ironvein is closed: a blockage. It should open again in about 30 days.`, still at parth); in 40 turns the bot wrote `cannot reach Ironvein: giving up on learn` three times, `given_up now: {'ironvein'}`, `any path given up: False`. Hunt, 120 turns: `goals: {('hunt', 'sp1'): 120}`, typed `{'move': 111, 'hunt': 9}`, nine give-up notes, `given_up: {'sp1'}` while the path ids are kill_boss and talk_warden: the second path is never tried, and after each give-up the bot types a search for the boss where it stands (travel_line returns None, which act_on reads as arrived). Persuade, 120 turns: `{('persuade', 'n1'): 120}`, 111 moves and 9 waits, a find path in Parth itself never tried. One refinement to the report: learn and contract are not forever. After a give-up act_on falls through as if arrived, so learn asks whoever is present and counts learn_left down (about 39 lines for the three), and contract counts a search and gives its path up after four (about 52 lines); hunt, persuade and stand never end. The counter counts every call that has not yet arrived, a hop that succeeded included, where the docstring says a hop that leads nowhere three times. A measuring tool: what it costs is the rest of a run of up to 400 lines and four hours of model time, and a report of an event the bot never reached.

Reach is small today: every caller is a process of its own, the tests that call evaluate() twice on one name (deal_first_667, line_patterns_648 six times) pass because each case re-dresses the scene, and tools/live_gate.py plays its script in a child process after reading(). What it costs: a save folder left per caller on Windows, and a later use of the model or of engine.party.remember in the same process silently gets the stub and a no-op.
