## tools2-2: An answer taken only on the gateway's relaxed last pass is written into the training set as a first-try example

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `tools/lora_dataset.py:67`
- **Evidence:** lora_dataset.py:67 `if r.get("attempt", 0) == 0 or key not in open_calls:` opens a new call; llm/gateway.py:197-198 logs the relaxed pass from attempt 0 again: `with backend.task(task), tagged(relaxed=True):` / `return _generate(task, system, user, schema, temperature, 1, relaxed_context, max_tokens)`. Reproduced (audit/work/tools2_lora_relaxed.py): three strict tries refused, then the same text taken relaxed: counts {'calls': 2, 'gave up': 1, 'sft': 1, 'sft (first try)': 1}, the refused text in npc_conversation.sft.jsonl, no pairs file.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A speaker's reply refused on every strict try and then taken with the looser checks (npc_conversation at npc/life.py:446, hire_chat at scenes/party_actions.py:802, npc_parting at engine/partings.py:105: all three are lora.yaml tasks) becomes a call of its own. build() learns from the answer the validators sent back (the repeat it was refused for is exactly what the adapter is meant to unlearn), counts the strict call as given up, and forms no rejected/chosen pair. tools/prose_measure.py:246 already treats a relaxed row as the same call; this tool was not brought along.
- **Fix:** In calls_of a row carrying relaxed joins the open call of its key and never opens one (what prose_measure.py:246 does). In build, an answer whose accepted row is relaxed is left out of sft under a count of its own, and is never the chosen side of a retry pair: once the row joins the call, the pair loop at 193-202 would otherwise pair the last strict draft with it. 'First try' is attempt 0 and not relaxed. Add the case to tools/sim/lora_test.py.
- **The finder's first fix:** In calls_of a row carrying `relaxed` joins the open call of its key and never opens one; in build an answer accepted only on the relaxed pass is left out of sft under its own count. Add the case to tools/sim/lora_test.py.
- **The check:** Output: calls_of groups [[(0, True, False), (1, True, False), (2, True, False)], [(0, False, True)]]; counts {'calls': 2, 'gave up': 1, 'sft': 1, 'sft (first try)': 1}; no pairs file; prose_measure.acceptance on the same rows gives calls 1, first_try 0. Two limits on the claim. The relaxed pass is a new draw (gateway._place gives it a new place, so request_seed differs), so the answer taken is not necessarily the refused text: it is one that passed only the looser checks. And it is rare: the played run has 154 rows, 3 with an error, no call that gave up and 0 relaxed rows. So a few rows a night are miscounted and learned from; severity low, not medium.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/lora_dataset.py calls_of (57-73) and build (184-244); llm/gateway.py generate (187-198), _generate (239 on: the relaxed pass counts its tries from 0 again with the same system and user messages) and _log (514: the row carries relaxed: true); tools/prose_measure.py:246. Searched lora_dataset.py, lora_eval.py, tools/sim/lora_test.py, tools/LORA.md and data/rules/lora.yaml for 'relaxed': no mention. Ran audit/work/check_tools2_2_lora.py (no model, no campaign): three strict tries refused, then a row with attempt 0 and relaxed: true. Counted the played run's log with the tool's own calls_of.

## tools2-6: Any conversation counts the bot's report as made: the report goal is popped by whoever it is talking to

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/nightbot.py:439`
- **Evidence:** nightbot.py:439-443: `if g.get("kind") == "report":` / `self.stats["goals_done"]["report"] += 1` / `self.goals.pop()`, with no check of who the partner is or where the player stands. Reproduced (audit/work/tools2_bot_posting.py, part 2): a report goal for guild_house on top, talking with a farmer at parth -> ("Thanks, I'll let you get on.", 'leave'), goals [], goals_done {'report': 1}.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** choose() opens a chat on arrival before it pursues goals (375-377), and talk_step runs for any open conversation. With a report goal on top (the whole way home from a finished contract) the first reply of any chat counts the report done, drops it and takes its leave. The contract has not been reported; with continuity on, _issuer_goal(g, "done") (444-445) then sends the bot to tell the issuer the work is done and logs the visit. new_goal finds the finished contract again later (goal_contract 659-665 counts goals_done.contract a second time), so the pay is collected in the end, but the bot's counts and the continuity log are wrong and every arrival chat on the way home is one line long.
- **Fix:** goal_report keeps who it reported to in the goal (g['told'] = clerk.id), and talk_step takes the report branch only when the partner is that person; any other chat goes on to the ordinary talk step with the report goal left on the stack. This holds for whoever a report is ever made to, not the clerk alone. Count report and contract done where the game shows it (watch's guild_done rising), not at the hand-over, so nothing is counted twice.
- **The finder's first fix:** Take the report branch only when the partner is the clerk of the goal's hall (ws.clerk_here() is the partner and the player is at g["place"]); otherwise go on to the ordinary talk step. Count a goal done where its real end is seen (the watch's guild_done), not at the hand-over.
- **The check:** Output: '1. ("I go to the adventurers' guild house.", move, report) | goals [report] | done {contract: 1}'; '2. talking with farmer at parth -> ("That's all I wanted to know. Good day.", leave, report) | goals [] | done {contract: 1, report: 1}'; '3. ("I go to the adventurers' guild house.", move, report) | goals [report] | done {contract: 2, report: 1}'; 'still held, never handed in: [q_audit] | guild_done: {}'. So each such chat counts one report and one more contract done than happened, and ends the chat after one line; the bot does get to the hall afterwards. The chance of the arrival chat is P.chat * 0.35 at each arrival among people not yet spoken to (0.105 hunter to 0.7 talker).
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/nightbot.py choose (364-377: any open conversation goes to talk_step; a chat is opened on arrival before goals are pursued), talk_step (439-446), goal_contract (659-665), goal_report (717-728) and _issuer_goal (1358-1370). Searched tools/sim: nothing pins the report branch (night_continuity_473_test calls _issuer_goal directly). Ran audit/work/check_tools2_6_report.py under simlib's stub (campaign audit_check_tools2_1, removed): a finished contract not handed in, then a chat with a farmer at Parth.

## tools2-7: A run given an out folder that already holds a run appends to its logs; the live gate then measures both runs as one

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/nightrun.py:97`
- **Evidence:** nightrun.py:97 `self.turn_file = (out / "turns.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` (98-99 the same for transcript.md and errors.log; llm/gateway.py:520 appends llm_calls.jsonl); tools/live_gate.py:130 `rows = [json.loads(l) for l in (out / "turns.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()]`.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** nightrun clears the save it names (636) but never its out folder. A second run with the same --out (nightrun --out X, or live_gate --out X, which plays into X/play) leaves both runs' rows and calls in the files. live_gate.play reads them all: times, passages, the speakers' first tries and the leaks count both runs, while run.json's checked counts are the last run's alone; ended_early cannot see it (there are more rows than wanted, not fewer). A whole gate run with a reused --out writes those numbers into data/measured/live_gate.yaml and the dated report.
- **Fix:** Opening the three files with "w" would not be enough: llm_calls.jsonl, pulse.jsonl, turns_game.jsonl, refusals.jsonl, sessions.jsonl and crash.log are appended by the game's own writers. One helper in the shared harness, called by nightrun.main and eventrun.main before config.LOG_PATH is set, refuses an out folder that already holds a run (turns.jsonl, llm_calls.jsonl or run.json) unless told to start over, as tools/situation_ab.py already does for its folder (--force; pinned by situation_ab_543_test.py:319). The gate gets it through the night run. Test: a second stub run into the same folder is refused.
- **The finder's first fix:** A run owns its out folder: nightrun refuses an out folder that already holds turns.jsonl (or moves the old run aside) and opens its logs fresh, so no reader downstream can meet two runs in one file.
- **The check:** The script printed: 'rows the gate reads: 6 | run.json turns: 3 | ended_early: ''', 'timing: inputs 6 median 27.5 p95 50.0' against 'the new run alone: inputs 3 median 5.0 p95 5.0', and 'leaks over the folder: lines 2, leaked 2' against 'leaks, the new run alone: leaked 0'. One correction to the finding: the leak count is not both runs' but the OLD run's alone. speech() pairs a row with its script line by the typed text and removes the line (230-232), so the second run's rows match no line and are never counted: a clean new run reports the stale run's leaks. Times, passages shown, replies and the speakers' first tries do count both. The likely way in is a retry into the same --out after an attempt that died: its partial rows plus the full new run pass ended_early (more rows than wanted, reason 'turn limit'), and a whole gate then writes data/measured/live_gate.yaml. The default folders (stamped to the second for the gate, to the minute for a night) avoid it. tools/eventrun.py:513-562 builds the same Run on its --out the same way.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/nightrun.py main (597-609: out.mkdir(exist_ok=True); the only thing cleared is saves/<save> at 636), Run.__init__ (97-99, mode "a"), llm/gateway.py:520 (appends llm_calls.jsonl), tools/live_gate.py play (130-134), ended_early (289-294) and speech (229-247). Searched tools/sim for a test that pins the append as intended: none, every test passes a folder of its own. Ran a scratch script (scratchpad/audit/work/tools2_2_run_check.py) that builds the real Run class twice on one scratch folder with a stand-in bot and reads the folder with live_gate's own timing, speech and ended_early. nightrun.py and live_gate.py themselves were not run (ground rules).

## tools2-8: On Windows with the output piped, one character outside the code page in a progress line ends the night with a turn written twice and no run.json

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/nightrun.py:250`
- **Evidence:** nightrun.py:250-253: `print(f"#{row['n']:<4} {row['seconds']:6.1f}s  {row['kind']:<8} {row['text'][:60]:<60}  "` ... then `self.current = None` only after the print; the tool never sets its streams as main.py:43-44 does (`s.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")`). This audit's own check died the same way printing 'Ş' (data/rules/currency.yaml) through a pipe: UnicodeEncodeError, 'charmap' codec.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** nightrun.bat --hours 6 > night.log, or a pipe from another tool without PYTHONUTF8: stdout is cp1252. A typed line with a character outside it in its first 60 (the model writes the bot's lines; the game's data holds such characters: the coin signs of currency.yaml, weather.yaml's signs), or the error print at 704, raises UnicodeEncodeError. In close_turn the row is already written and self.current is still set, so the handler at 705-707 closes the same turn again (a second copy of the row, the same error inside the handler), the loop is left, and finish() (354) raises a third time before run.json is written: no run.json, no summary. Read from the code and from the encode failure met here; the night itself was not run.
- **Fix:** The helper exists: main.py utf8_streams (f565, lines 37-44) does this for the game. Move it to a shared module and call it first in every tool's main (nightrun, eventrun, live_gate, latency and the rest) instead of a second copy; and in close_turn clear self.current as soon as the row is written, before the progress line, so no failed print can write a turn again. Test: close_turn with a cp1252 stdout and a line holding an arrow writes one row and leaves current None.
- **The finder's first fix:** One shared helper, called first in every tool's main, that sets stdout and stderr as main.py does (utf-8, errors="replace"); and clear self.current before the progress line, so a failed print can never close a turn twice.
- **The check:** The script printed: steps ['ask: UnicodeEncodeError', "handler's own print: went through", 'handler: UnicodeEncodeError (leaves the loop)', 'finish: UnicodeEncodeError'], 'rows in memory: 3 | lines in turns.jsonl: 3 | all turn n: [1, 1, 1] | run.json written: False | current cleared: False'. So the turn is written three times, not twice (at the prompt, in the handler, in finish), and the run ends with a traceback, no run.json and no summary.md; server.close() at 742 is skipped, but the Windows Job Object (llm/runtime.py:275-301) stops the server with the process. What limits it: a console window is UTF-8, the gate's child and the suite set PYTHONUTF8, so it needs a night or event run redirected or run from an agent's shell on Windows. The character has to come from the model: no tracked tool source holds one, the played run had none in 154 replies or 42 typed lines, and the guard (engine/guard.py foreign, f390; player_line is guarded) sends back other alphabets. The guard check showed an arrow, and 'T\u014dru' with a non-breaking hyphen, pass both the contract and the guard and do not fit cp1252. Not observed in a real night. Same class, read not run: live_gate.py:429 prints the report, which quotes spoken replies (365), after its files are kept, so there a stray character only turns a passed gate into a traceback and exit 1.
- **How it was checked:** Read nightrun.py close_turn (213-253), ask (188-211), the loop and its handler (691-742) and finish (353-362); scenes/world.py run (1059-1061: console.ask is in no try). Measured this machine's piped stdout with PYTHONUTF8 unset: 'cp1252 surrogateescape', and print('a \u2192 b') through a pipe raised UnicodeEncodeError (exit 1). Ran scratchpad/audit/work/tools2_2_run_check.py: the real Run class, a cp1252 stdout, a typed line holding an arrow, then the handler's and the finally's steps line for line. Ran tools2_2_guard_check.py: the bot line's contract (PlayerLine) and the content guard on four lines. Scanned the played run (154 calls, 42 typed lines) and tracked data for characters outside cp1252. nightrun.bat sets no PYTHONUTF8 and no code page; only live_gate.py:126 and run_suite.py:273 set it for their children.

## leftovers-3: prose_baseline.sh deletes the game's own call log twice and leaves none behind: its two measuring tools can only write to logs/llm_calls.jsonl, so the script clears and carries off the shared file

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/prose_baseline.sh:16`

- **What a player or the owner meets:** The header says 'a machine with the model files in place (a pod)', but nothing checks that, and the owner's machine is such a machine. Run there, it removes the call log of the owner's own play before live_check starts (the log #report takes its calls from, scenes/audit_actions.py:158), removes it again before interp_eval, and moves what the tools wrote out of logs/. With set -e a live_check that fails stops the script after the delete. It also leaves saves/prose_live_check.md, live_check clears saves/live_check, and the five plays clear saves/prose_<persona>_<seed> (all.json tools2-3). The file holds two calls of fresh_log, not three.
- **Fix:** As proposed: give live_check and interp_eval the out folder nightrun and eventrun have, through the one harness helper of all.json tools2-7 (it sets config.LOG_PATH and the other log paths for a run and refuses a folder that already holds one), and write live_check's report there. The script then has no rm and no mv on the shared log, and the same helper covers every measuring tool, not this script alone.
- **The finder's first fix:** Give live_check and interp_eval the out folder nightrun and eventrun already have, through the one harness helper all.json tools2-7 proposes (it sets config.LOG_PATH and the other log paths for a run), and write the live_check report there too. The script then needs no rm and no mv on the shared log.

Neither tool sets config.LOG_PATH or takes an out folder (live_check has --report, a file name in saves/; interp_eval has --live, --only, --promote, --corpus), so both write the shared log and the script can only clear it and carry it off. Nothing checks where it runs; with set -e a failed live_check stops after the delete. scenes/audit_actions.py:158 reads the last 400 lines of config.LOG_PATH for #report. It also leaves saves/prose_live_check.md and clears saves/live_check (138, 728). The reach is small, hence low: the tracked records of its use are rented pods (docs/measure/prose_baseline/README.md:4, prose_a1 and prose_a2 READMEs, tools/runpod_night.sh:19 and runpod_jupyter.py:190 pass it as the THEN command), and the call log is a diagnostic the game itself trims at 5 MB. The harm needs the script run in the owner's own working tree.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/prose_baseline.sh whole, tools/live_check.py (the arguments 31-40, saves handling 62, 93, 138, 148, 728), tools/interp_eval.py (79, 87, the arguments 348-352), config.py (LOG_PATH at 30 has no environment override; only DND_LOG_MAX_MB at 43), scenes/audit_actions.py:150-165, and searched every tracked file for prose_baseline.sh. Not run: both tools start the model server.
- **Already recorded:** GOALS.md:179 names docs/measure/prose_baseline new1 and new2 as the measure's baselines; nothing there or in docs/design on what the script removes.

## tools2-5: The pulse preview crashes on every run after the first: each run's first situation gets the same id

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/pulse_preview.py:96`
- **Evidence:** pulse_preview.py:96 `th = next(x for x in state["threads"] if x["id"] not in before)`; engine/pulse.py:371 `thread_id = streams.new_id(8)`. Three runs in a row on one scratch world under the stub (audit/work/tools2_pulse_ids.py): `streams key: unseeded | ids ['b5b2d1bc']`, then StopIteration twice with the same single id kept.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The tool never begins the streams (engine/streams.py begin), so the ids stream is seeded "unseeded:ids" in every process and the first situation of every run has the same id. The scratch world (saves/pulse_preview) is kept between runs unless --fresh, so from the second run on the new situation's id is already in `before`, next() finds nothing, and the tool dies with StopIteration before it prints or saves anything, at every tier. No test runs the tool, so nothing showed it.
- **Fix:** Begin the streams for each event from the scratch campaign's own count of inputs, advanced and saved as a turn does (store.meta.steps), not from the number of situations the world holds: finished ones are trimmed to pulse.FINISHED_KEPT (30), so that number stops rising and the ids would repeat again. Take the new situation as the one start_thread added, not by id. A stub test that runs main() twice on one scratch world.
- **The finder's first fix:** Begin the streams once per event from the run's seed and a count that goes on from the scratch world (the number of situations it holds), as a turn does, and take the new situation by position (the one start_thread appended) instead of by id. Add a stub test that runs main() twice on one scratch world.
- **The check:** --tier normal: 'run 1: key: unseeded | failed: no | events printed: 1 | ids saved: [("b5b2d1bc", "resolved")]'; runs 2 and 3: 'failed: StopIteration at pulse_preview.py:96 `th = next(x for x in state["threads"] if x["id"] not in before)` | events printed: 0', the one id kept. --tier uncommon --place parth --template: the same id b5b2d1bc, the same StopIteration on runs 2 and 3. A preview tool with a way round (--fresh), no game state touched: low.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/pulse_preview.py main (66-96: the scratch world is kept unless --fresh; the streams are never begun), engine/pulse.py:371 and engine/streams.py (reset leaves the key 'unseeded'; new_id draws from the ids stream). Searched tracked files: no test or tool runs pulse_preview. Ran the tool's own main() with --stub three times, a process each, on one scratch world, its fixed save name redirected to audit_check_tools2_1 (audit/work/check_tools2_5_preview.py, removed after), with two sets of arguments.

## tools2-14: The preview's fast-forward finds new news by the list's remembered length, which folding and the cap do not change

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/pulse_preview.py:119`
- **Evidence:** pulse_preview.py:114 `seen_stage, news_n = 0, len(state["news"])`, 119 `for n in state["news"][news_n:]:`, 121 `news_n = len(state["news"])`; engine/pulse.py:984-996 add_news moves a retold item to the end without lengthening the list and trims through cap_news.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A stage whose news is a retelling, or any news once the list is at its cap, changes the list without making it longer: the fast-forward prints nothing for it, or the wrong rows after a trim. (seen_stage is set and never read.)
- **Fix:** Print the rows whose minute is this tick's: add_news stamps a new row and a retold one with t, and t rises every tick, so it holds through folding and the cap. Put it in engine/pulse as one reader (news since a minute) so no tool slices the list by length; drop seen_stage. pulse_preview is the last such slice on the news (git grep over the tools and simbot.py found no other).
- **The finder's first fix:** Remember the last minute printed and print the rows newer than it; drop seen_stage.
- **The check:** The script printed: 'A3 campaign model ticks 168 -> ended printed 1 arrived 4' on a fresh world (the rows show times 2 and 3: stage tellings folded), where campaign is the tool's default tier and --stub its documented self-check; with the list at its cap 'B0 normal printed 0 arrived 1 | list length now 300' and 'B1 campaign printed 0 arrived 4'; and 'C. after a retelling: list length 2 | the slice the tool prints: []'. seen_stage is assigned at 114 and read nowhere. Two corrections: at the cap the slice is empty, so the tool prints nothing for the news rather than wrong rows (the length never falls below the remembered one); and with the real model a fold needs the same words twice from the same place, which the stub's stage texts do and a model's seldom would, so in real use the cap is the main case. A preview tool's report only: no game state is touched.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/pulse_preview.py 113-121 and engine/pulse.py cap_news and add_news (957-1003): a retelling pops the row and appends it again (994), and both paths end in cap_news (300, pulse.yaml news.keep). Searched engine, scenes, npc, storage and world for any other writer of state["news"]: only cap_news, so the list never shrinks by age, and the tool keeps its scratch world between uses unless --fresh (66-73, 131). Ran scratchpad/audit/work/tools2_2_preview_check.py: the tool's loop copied line for line on campaign audit_check_tools2_2 under simlib's stub (removed afterwards; the tool itself writes saves/pulse_preview, so it was not run), counting what the slice prints against the rows stamped with each tick's minute.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/12_foundations_survey.md, section 'I. world_state' (line 115): 'Tools that slice lists by remembered length (survey: tools/event_trial.py:198-210, tools/pulse_preview.py:98-118, simbot.py:258).'

- **Evidence:** UNWALKED = {"__pycache__", "saves", "logs", ".git", ".claude", ".venv", ".buildenv", "runtime", "models", "build", "dist"}
dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d not in UNWALKED and not (here / d / ".git").exists())

Add the cases to suite_loop_717_test (a tracked folder named runtime below data/, a changed .json a test opened).
- **The finder's first fix:** Skip those folder names at the root only, walk every file under data/ whatever its suffix (and the page's folder), and pick a test for a changed data file that is not YAML by the record's 'data' set.

One more gate the finding only half states: quick_suite.sh leaves at once unless git status shows a changed *.py, *.yaml or *.js, so a change to a .json, .html or .css file alone never starts the quick run. ## tools3-7: Hard-coded /tmp defaults land in C:/tmp on Windows, a different folder from Git Bash's /tmp

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/run_suite.py:371`. **Same place:** suite-speed-6
- **Evidence:** ap.add_argument("--outdir", default="/tmp/meravia_suite")
# tools/runpod_jupyter.py:161
out = Path(os.environ.get("TMPDIR") or "/tmp") / "dnd_ai_head.tar.gz"
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Python on Windows reads /tmp as the root of the current drive (C:/tmp/meravia_suite), while Git Bash rewrites an argument /tmp/... to %TEMP%. Both C:/tmp/meravia_suite (last written 17 November 16:57) and %TEMP%/meravia_suite (18:11) exist on this machine, so after a run without --outdir the line '(see /tmp/meravia_suite/<test>.out)', followed from Git Bash, opens another run's output. runpod_jupyter's archive_repo writes C:/tmp/dnd_ai_head.tar.gz and works only because C:/tmp happens to exist (git archive fails where it does not). The two scratch probes open /tmp/camp.out and /tmp/p.out the same way.
- **Fix:** In run_suite.py make the default Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / 'meravia_suite' (and the docstring at line 19), print outdir.resolve() in the FAILED line, and use tempfile.gettempdir() in archive_repo; it honours TMPDIR/TEMP, so Bash's /tmp and Python then name one folder. Do the same for the rest of the kind in one pass: the two tools/scratch probes, and tools/sim/pulse_budget_test.py:10, which writes its log to a hard-coded /tmp/claude-0/... path left from another machine's session (use tempfile.mkdtemp).
- **The finder's first fix:** Use tempfile.gettempdir() for both defaults and print the folder as resolved.
- **The check:** python: str(Path('/tmp/meravia_suite')) is '\\tmp\\meravia_suite', resolve() is C:\tmp\meravia_suite; tempfile.gettempdir() is C:\Users\tstil\AppData\Local\Temp. The same text passed as an argument from Git Bash arrives as 'C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/meravia_suite'. Both folders exist, each a full set of .out files: C:/tmp/meravia_suite newest file 2026-11-17 16:57:55, %TEMP%/meravia_suite newest 18:11:03 (the finder's times hold). The two come from the project's own instructions: .claude/agents/suite-runner.md:7 passes --outdir /tmp/meravia_suite through Bash (converted to %TEMP%), while CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/feature/SKILL.md:18 and the blocked-push message in .claude/hooks/before_bash.py:10 run it with no --outdir (C:\tmp) and tee the summary to Bash's /tmp. Nothing guards it: outdir.mkdir(parents=True) creates C:\tmp silently, and no test pins the default (suite_loop_717_test and CI pass --outdir). One correction to the finding: on Windows line 431 prints '(see \tmp\meravia_suite/<test>.out)', not '/tmp/meravia_suite/...'; the consequence is the same. runpod_jupyter: C:/tmp/dnd_ai_head.tar.gz exists (11 November), so archive_repo did fall to /tmp; git archive -o into a missing folder printed 'fatal: could not open ... for writing: No such file or directory', exit 128, so on a Windows machine with no C:\tmp and no TMPDIR the 'night' command stops there (in this Git Bash session TMPDIR is set, so it goes to %TEMP%). tools/scratch/prop_probe.py:4 and camp_probe.py:5 open /tmp/p.out and /tmp/camp.out as quoted. tools/sim/party_test.py:7 already carries '(f573) /tmp is not a folder on every machine' and uses tempfile.gettempdir(): the class was fixed for one file only.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/run_suite.py 364-432, tools/runpod_jupyter.py 159-205 and the two probes in tools/scratch; searched tracked files (git grep) for every caller of run_suite and every use of --outdir and /tmp; ran python to resolve the default path; ran python with /tmp/meravia_suite as an argument from Git Bash; listed C:/tmp and %TEMP%; ran git archive -o into a folder that does not exist (scratchpad, nothing written). Did not run run_suite itself: without --outdir it writes outside the audit folder.

## tools3-9: The blind reads parser takes the word 'a' after any number as a vote for A, on comment lines too

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/situation_ab.py:492`
- **Evidence:** core = text.lstrip("#").strip().split(" #", 1)[0]
found = READ.findall(core)
# READ (line 65): an optional 'pair', a number, any of : . ) or a dash, then (a|b|tie), case ignored
- **What a player or the owner meets:** read_reads run on a sample file (audit/work/tools3_reads.py): '# reader two, pack 3: a first pass' is a vote (3, A); '# I read pack 1 a week ago' is (1, A); '15 a tie really' is (15, A); '16 A, though 16 b reads cleaner' is two votes. decide() tallies them all, so a reader's note can move the share that decides whether an arm passes. The test pins '#13 B' and '## Pair 12: A' as reads, which a fix must keep.
- **Fix:** Take a line as reads only when the whole of it (after leading #s, before ' #') is one or more reads; otherwise a # line is a comment and any other line is named as unread, which the decision already refuses. Tried in the script with fullmatch of (?:(?:pair\s*)?(\d+)\s*[:.)\-en-dash em-dash]*\s*(a|b|tie)\b[\s,;]*)+ : all nine pinned reads and the 'felt thin' case come out as the test expects, the two comment lines give no vote, and '15 a tie really' and '16 A, though 16 b reads cleaner' are named as unread. Also refuse a pair read twice in one reader's file. This is simpler than the finder's three-part rule and covers every stray sentence, not the sampled ones.
- **The finder's first fix:** Take a read only when the choice ends it (the end of the line, a comment, or the next pair's number), take a # line only in the pack's own heading form, and refuse a pair read twice in one reader's file.
- **The check:** Printed by the script: '# reader two, pack 3: a first pass' -> [('3','a')]; '# I read pack 1 a week ago' -> [('1','a')]; '15 a tie really' -> [('15','a')]; '16 A, though 16 b reads cleaner' -> [('16','a'),('16','b')]; also '# read 17 a.m., second sitting' -> [('17','a')] and '# 7 - a close one, see below' -> [('7','a')]; none is reported as unread, so finish_decision's refusal (line 694) does not catch them. decide() counts each: with slot A 3 of 6 and slot B 3 of 4 the verdict is 'off' (6 of 10); adding the one line '# reader two, pack 3: a first pass' makes it 'budget_1024' (7 of 11, slot A 4 of 7). The other way, 6 of 10 passing becomes 'off' with the note '# pack 4 b side read first, then a' (slot A 3 of 6). The docstring says a line that begins with # is passed over, which the code does not do (it has to read '## Pair 12: A' and '#13 B', both pinned by the test). Reach is small: pair numbers run from 1, so any small number in a note is a real pair, but it takes a note of that shape and a borderline tally. The one real decision (data/measured/situation_thinking.yaml, 7 November) could not have been moved by it: shares 0.293 to 0.4 against a floor of 0.6, and every arm also kept fewer parts than off. docs/design/09_prose_and_dialogue.md (lines 119, 167) names this readers' protocol for later comparisons, so the parser will be used again.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/situation_ab.py line 65 (READ), 481-498 (read_reads), 417-450 (pack), 558-612 (decide), 681-696 (finish_decision) and the test's reads section (tools/sim/situation_ab_543_test.py 451-470). Ran my own CPU-only script, audit/work/check_tools3_2_reads.py: read_reads on sample lines, then decide() on planted rows and a key built as the test builds them, with and without one comment line. No campaign opened.

## tools3-5: The voice report no longer tells hires apart: its two patterns do not match the hire prompt, so every hire is one speaker, 'a hire'

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `tools/voice_report.py:61`
- **Evidence:** m = re.search(r"WHO YOU ARE\n\s*(.*?)\n", u)
who = (re.search(r"A hired \w+, (.*?)\.", m.group(1)) if m else None)
hires[(who.group(1) if who else "a hire")[:40]].append(sp)
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The hire's request now opens 'WHO YOU ARE: A hired archer (she, human), a keen-eyed hunter with a bow. A human.': no newline after the heading, and a bracket between the trade and the comma. Run on the measured session's llm_calls.jsonl, the five hire lines of two hires (an archer and a mage) come out as one row, 'a hire  5 lines', so the HIRES section says nothing of how each sounds. The townsfolk pattern still matches (12 of 12 rows).
- **Fix:** Make every speech call (npc_conversation, hire_chat and the other speaker tasks) under gateway.tagged(speaker=<the speaker's id>, speaker_name=...), which the log row then carries, and key the report on it for townsfolk and hires alike, falling back to the prompt's heading only for logs made before. No change of prompt wording can break it then, and no prompt is touched. Add a test that feeds load() a row built by the real prompt builder for two hires and holds two keys.
- **The finder's first fix:** Have the call's log row carry who spoke (the speaker's id) and key the report on it, so no change of wording breaks it; until then read 'WHO YOU ARE:' to the end of its line.
- **The check:** Printed: hire keys: {'a hire': 5}; the hire_chat requests open 'WHO YOU ARE: A hired archer (she, human), a keen-eyed hunter with a bow. A human.' (3 rows) and 'WHO YOU ARE: A hired mage (he, orc), a battle-wizard in a patched robe. An orc.' (2 rows). The first pattern wants a newline straight after 'WHO YOU ARE' and the second wants a comma straight after the trade; neither matches, so the five first-try lines of two hires are one row. The townsfolk pattern matched 12 of 12 npc_conversation rows. Even when it matched, the key was the blurb cut to 40 characters, not the person: two hires of one trade and blurb would have been one speaker. ## trace-threads-8: Closing the window in the middle of a turn cancels no model call: the process lingers up to 10 s, then the game thread is cut off wherever it is

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `ui/gui/__init__.py:41`
- **Evidence:** bridge.close()
t.join(timeout=10)
srv.shutdown()
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player closes the window while the narrator is writing. bridge.close() ends only the next wait for input; the request in flight keeps generating, the hidden process stays up to 10 s, and when the join gives up the daemon game thread dies at exit in the middle of the turn. SQLite rolls an open transaction back, but writes made outside one (the background apply of trace-threads-1) can be cut in half. llm/runtime.py:31 says the window's close reaches the server 'through llm.backend.close()', and the game's code makes no such call.
- **Fix:** In launch()'s finally call backend.close() before the join, so the call in flight ends Cancelled and the turn unwinds at once through its own rollback (main.guarded already passes Cancelled); that makes llm/runtime.py:31 true. Use the same single stop function as trace-threads-7. From reading only: a call begun after the close gets 'unreachable' from Runtime.chat_call (lines 996-1007), which the gateway counts as a failed try; it should end Cancelled too.
- **The finder's first fix:** On window close, cancel the calls in flight first (the worker's close, which raises Cancelled in the game thread) and then join, so the turn unwinds at once through its own rollback; correct the docstring.
- **The check:** Printed: '[as launch() does it: bridge.close(), join] the game thread ended 3.5 s after the close: the call ran to its end, then the prompt answered quit' and '[with the interface's close() first] the game thread ended 0.0 s after the close: the call Cancelled'. So a turn with under 10 s left finishes and is saved unseen, and one with more is cut when main.py's finally stops the server and the daemon thread dies at exit. The save stays whole either way (an open transaction is rolled back; the half apply of trace-threads-1 would need the exit to land inside a 2.6 ms apply, so that part of the scenario is negligible). The real cost is a hidden process holding the card and run/game.lock for up to 10 s, during which a relaunch is told the game is already open, and a turn in progress that is kept or lost by how long it had left.
- **How it was checked:** Read ui/gui/__init__.py:12-61, ui/gui/bridge.py:222-259 (ask and close), main.py:71-75 and 182-187 (the finally; guarded passes Cancelled in silence), llm/runtime.py:28-31, 993-1015 and 1075-1097. Searched every tracked .py for backend.close(): only the docstring at llm/runtime.py:31 names it. Ran scratchpad/audit/work/check_trace_threads_8_close.py: the Bridge as launch() builds it, a stand-in source whose chat takes 4 s, then the two steps launch() takes when the window is gone, with and without the interface's close() first.

## shell2-5: With the browser standing in for the window, closing the tab leaves the game and its model server running with nothing to stop them

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `ui/gui/__init__.py:67`. **Same place:** frontend-shipping-2
- **Evidence:** webbrowser.open(url) | while not bridge.finished.is_set(): | time.sleep(0.5)  (lines 67-70)
- **What a player or the owner meets:** When pywebview is missing or cannot open a window (_window's two except branches) the page opens in the default browser. The window path hooks window.events.closed to bridge.close(); this path has no equivalent, and the page sends nothing on unload (ui/gui/web/app.js has no beforeunload). Closing the tab ends the /events stream; the game thread stays in inbox.get(), the main thread sleeps in this loop and llama-server keeps the model in VRAM. From a terminal Ctrl+C ends it; the built windowed app has no console, so only Task Manager does. Traced in the code, not run (it needs the model server).
- **Fix:** As proposed, with the detail filled in: the server counts live /events streams; in the browser path only (the window path already has window.events.closed), the wait loop at __init__.py:69 calls bridge.close() once a page has connected and none has been connected for N seconds, N in data/ and long enough for a refresh or the page's own reconnect (the server notices a gone page only at its next write, up to since()'s 15 seconds). The same count lets the loop end when no page ever connects (the browser did not open). bridge.close() is what the window's close does, so the game saves and ends the same way.
- **The finder's first fix:** Let the server count the connected /events clients and, in the browser path, call bridge.close() once one has connected and none has been for some seconds (the number in data/).
- **The check:** Quoted lines are there (__init__.py:67-70). Printed: 'the game is waiting at its prompt: True'; 'the page's stream opened: HTTP/1.1 200 OK'; '33s after the page went: bridge.closed = False | finished = False | the game still waiting = True | what it was handed = []'; and for comparison 'after bridge.close(): the game was handed [quit]'. The rest traced with no way out: _events only returns when its write fails; launch()'s finally and main()'s finally (which stop the model server, main.py:71-75) run only after _window returns, and in the browser path that is when the game ends or on Ctrl+C. Reach: the built app is --noconsole and bundles pywebview (build_exe.bat) and the installer puts WebView2 in, so there the browser path needs the window to fail to open; run from source without pywebview it is the normal path and Ctrl+C ends it. One cost the report misses: a second copy of the game is refused (run/game.lock, llm/launch.py:237-248), so the process left behind also blocks the next start until it is ended in Task Manager. Reopening the closed tab's address does reconnect (the stream replays from the log).
- **How it was checked:** Read ui/gui/__init__.py, ui/gui/server.py (_events, 172-196), ui/gui/bridge.py (ask, close, since); searched ui/gui/web for beforeunload, pagehide, unload, sendBeacon, visibilitychange (no match) and every caller of bridge.close (the window's closed event, launch's finally, the updater). Read main.py:59-75, build_exe.bat, installer/meravia.iss and llm/runtime.py GameLock. Ran my own script audit/work/check_shell2_1_browser.py: the bridge and the local server alone (no game, no model, no save), a thread waiting in bridge.ask(main=True), a socket that opens /events and is then closed.

## pane-commands-5: Once the bridge is closed and the game thread has not finished, the event stream writes pings with no pause: 89,449 in one second and a core and a half busy

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `ui/gui/bridge.py:121`
- **Evidence:** ui/gui/bridge.py:121  if not any(i > last for i, _ in self.log[-1:]) and not self.closed:
ui/gui/server.py:190  elif bridge.closed and bridge.finished.is_set():      (return)
ui/gui/server.py:192  chunk = ": ping\n\n"
Run against the real server with a socket (work/pane_commands/ping_loop.py): bridge open and idle for 1 s: 0 pings, 0.00 s of process CPU; bridge closed with finished not set, 1 s: 89,449 pings, 715,592 bytes, 1.56 s of process CPU. When the page stops reading, the write blocks (0.06 s).
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The player closes the window, or installs an update (core/updates.py:134-135: quit_game() closes the bridge, the process leaves 10 s later), while a turn is being answered. Until the game thread finishes, each open event stream spins: the Python process takes the interpreter lock and a core away from the turn that is still being finished and saved, for up to the 10 s the launcher waits (ui/gui/__init__.py) or the rest of the turn.
- **Fix:** As proposed: in since(), wait on the condition with a short timeout when the bridge is closed (for example self.cv.wait(timeout if not self.closed else 0.25)), so the stream ticks a few times a second until finished is set.
- **The finder's first fix:** In since(), wait on the condition with a short timeout when the bridge is closed (or have the event loop wait on bridge.finished.wait(0.25) before a ping once closed), so the loop ticks a few times a second until finished is set.
- **The check:** Printed: 'open and idle 1 s: 0 pings, CPU 0.00 s'; 'closed, finished not set, page still reading, 1 s: 84998 pings, 679984 bytes, CPU 1.59 s' (my reader shares the process, so the server's share is about a core); 'after the page's socket is closed, 1 s: CPU 0.00 s'. So the loop is real, but the scenario is narrower than written: when the player closes the window the page's connection goes with it and the handler returns at its next write, and when the game waits at a prompt close() makes it return at once and finished is set. The spin lasts only while a page is still connected and a turn is still being answered: an update handed over in the middle of a turn in the built Windows app (the window stays up to 10 s until _leave), or Ctrl+C in the browser fallback in the middle of a turn (join timeout 10 s).
- **How it was checked:** Read Bridge.since and close (ui/gui/bridge.py:119-127, 255-259), the stream loop (ui/gui/server.py:172-196), launch/_window (ui/gui/__init__.py) and the update hand-over (server.py:220-229, core/updates.py:112-136). Ran my own script against the real local server with one socket and no game (work/check_pane_commands_1_ping.py), adding the case the finder did not measure: the page's socket closed.

## frontend-shipping-10: esc() does not escape quotes and is used inside attributes: a place name with a double quote breaks out of the tag

- **Checked:** confirmed. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `ui/gui/web/app.js:67`
- **Evidence:** ui/gui/web/app.js:67 `const esc = (s) => s.replace(/[&<>]/g, ...)`; :1128 `<span class="spot" title="${esc(s.spot)}">${esc(s.spot)}</span>`; :78 writes a token's id raw, `data-hit="${id}"`. Run in the real page: a status whose spot was `Ashford — The "Rusty" Nail" data-audit="broke-out` gave the span a data-audit attribute and a title cut at the first quote; a hit token id with a quote did the same.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A place the model named with a double quote in it (a nickname, a quoted inn sign) has its tooltip cut short and the rest spilled into the tag as attributes; text shaped like an event-handler attribute would run as script in the page that holds the input token. The names come from the local model and the player's own words, so the reach is the player's own window, but the escape is wrong in every attribute it is used in.
- **Fix:** Add the double and the single quote to esc() (one line; it covers :1128 and any later use). Do not also pass the id through esc() at :78: the id is cut out of text that has already been through esc(), so it is then already escaped, and escaping it twice would break the hitsMap lookup by dataset.hit. Add to an existing page check that a status whose spot holds a quote keeps its whole title and gains no attribute.
- **The finder's first fix:** Escape the two quote characters in esc() as well (one line, every use covered), and pass the token id through it at :78.
- **The check:** Seen in the page: a status whose spot was `Ashford — The "Rusty" Nail" data-audit="broke-out` gave span.spot the attributes class=spot, title='Ashford — The ', rusty"='', nail"='' and data-audit='broke-out'; a text line holding the token ⟦h-9" data-audit2="broke-out|(16 damage)⟧ gave the .dmg span data-hit='h-9' and data-audit2='broke-out'. So the escape is wrong inside an attribute, as claimed. The reach is narrower than 'every attribute it is used in' suggests: esc() is used inside an attribute in exactly one place (1128, the strip's tooltip), and the token id at :78 is the engine's own (h-N, combat_scene.py:109), so real text reaches only :1128, and only through a place the model named with a double quote (DiscoveryProposal.name has no check on quotes; no authored name has one). Script would need the model to write an event-handler attribute into a name: today that is the player's own window, but with several players (GOALS.md checklist 8) one player's words could shape a name shown in another's window. server.py sends no Content-Security-Policy.
- **How it was checked:** Read app.js:67 esc, every use of esc( and of innerHTML (grep), decorate (72-82) and Strip.update (1124-1131). Traced the spot: bridge.status_block from scenes/world.py show_header and place_lines (232-236); place names from the model in engine/discovery.py:65 and the contract DiscoveryProposal (llm/contracts.py:1927-1950); the token ids in scenes/combat_scene.py:109 and 958. Searched data/world for a name holding a double quote (none). Ran the real page with the scratch script above. Note: before I moved to a tab of my own, one typed line ('token') went to another auditor's scripted page in the shared Browser tab; nothing in the repository was touched.

## trace-turn-5: A check on a search or an improvised act replaces the action: on_search and the act's ruling never run, yet the step is recorded as done

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `scenes/check_actions.py:81`
- **Evidence:** run_checks: `events, handled = [], intent.kind in ("look", "other", "search") or not intent.kind` ... `return handled and bool(events)`; scenes/world.py:2426 `if not self.run_checks(intent, text):` gates `getattr(self, f"on_{intent.kind}")(intent, text)`. Stub run (audit/work/trace_turn_demo.py, cases B and C): the same search step called on_search without a check and never with checks=['perception']; the same `other` step called act.act without a check and never with one; both operations still said 'searched the trading square' and 'tried something of your own'. No repair strips checks from these kinds and no test pins the behaviour for them.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The interpreter's prompt offers perception for 'searching carefully for details' (scenes/world_prompts.py:48). 'I search the cellar carefully' read as search + perception rolls Perception and narrates what is noticed, but skips all of on_search: what the part holds (search_part), a matter's find (matters.try_find), a person sought by name, the trail and the encounter roll with their minutes. 'I study the door and wedge it shut' read as other + perception never reaches engine/act.py (f603: the one ruling outside combat): no ruling, no change, no refusal. The played session reviewed had no such plan, so how often the model attaches a check there is unmeasured.
- **Fix:** Do it for the class, as run_checks already does for steal and unlock ('a theft rolls its own bar'): a field on the kinds table in engine/actions.py for a kind whose handler makes its own roll (steal, unlock, search, other), read by run_checks in place of the two tuples of kind names, so a check named on such a step never stands in for its handler and nothing is rolled twice. Keep the check standing in for a look and for a step with no kind. For a search with stealth, set self.sneaking as the attack path does. Test with a search and an improvised act carrying a check: on_search and the act's ruling run. Before building, a count of such plans over the night logs would say how often it has cost a player; that needs logs I was told not to read.
- **The finder's first fix:** For search and other, let the check feed the handler and not stand in for it: keep `handled` for look and a step with no kind, and pass the check's outcome on as a beat (pending_beats, as the other kinds do) or hand the named check to the act path so nothing is rolled twice.
- **The check:** The code is as quoted: `events, handled = [], intent.kind in ("look", "other", "search") or not intent.kind` and `return handled and bool(events)`. Under the stub, in the Greywood: a search with checks ['perception'] never reached on_search, took no minutes (a plain search took 20 and began a fight), and the narrator was told only 'The player looks carefully but notices nothing out of the ordinary.'; did was still ['searched the Greywood']. ## frontend-shipping-4: The installer copies the 8 GB of model files out of the temp folder without checking the copy, asks Setup for no room for them, and takes 'the file exists' for 'the file is whole'

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** medium. **Place:** `tools/installer_files.py:50`
- **Evidence:** tools/installer_files.py:49-50 writes `if FileExists(ExpandConstant('{tmp}\<file>')) then` / `FileCopy(ExpandConstant('{tmp}\<file>'), Dir + '\<file>', False);` with the result thrown away; :45 ModelsPresent is `FileExists(...)` joined by `and`; installer/meravia.iss [Setup] (lines 13-27) has no ExtraDiskSpaceRequired. The game's own check (llm/runtime.py:163-169) is is_file() only.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The files are downloaded to {tmp} and then copied to {app}\models, both under the user's profile by default, so for a while the drive needs twice their size while Setup's free-space check counts only the game. On a drive with about 12 GB free the copy fails, nothing is said, Setup ends as a success and the game then fails its start with the reason hidden (frontend-shipping-2). A file left short by an installer killed during the copy is 'present' to ModelsPresent and to the game, so 'run the installer again' fetches nothing and the model server fails on load instead. Read from the generated Pascal; no installer was run.
- **Fix:** Rename the file out of {tmp} first (same drive: at once, no second 8 GB, no minute of copying); only when that fails copy to '<file>.part' in {app}/models and rename after FileCopy returned True, so a file under its real name is whole by construction. Check each result and say a failure in the box the download's failure uses. Have installer_files.py write the models' total into ExtraDiskSpaceRequired. A size comparison in ModelsPresent and runtime_problems is cheap and catches a short file, but should not be the only guard: Windows may set the destination's length before the bytes arrive, and a sha256 of 8 GB at every start is too slow.
- **The finder's first fix:** Move the file instead of copying it (RenameFile on the same drive, a copy only as the fallback), check the result and tell the player in the box the download failure already uses; have installer_files.py write the models' size into ExtraDiskSpaceRequired; and compare each file's size with the pinned one in ModelsPresent and in runtime_problems.
- **The check:** The four code facts are as quoted: the generated FileCopy's result is unused (installer_files.py:49-50); ModelsPresent is FileExists joined by 'and' (:45); [Setup] has no ExtraDiskSpaceRequired; the game's check is is_file() (runtime.py:165). What follows from them rests on Inno Setup's behaviour, which I know but could not run: the download page saves into {tmp}, FileCopy returns False and raises nothing, and Setup's free-space check counts [Files] plus ExtraDiskSpaceRequired. So a copy that fails for room (free space between about once and twice the models' size) is silent and Setup ends well, while a download that fails is told (meravia.iss:154). The short-file case needs Setup killed during the copy.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/installer_files.py:35-52, installer/meravia.iss whole (the [Setup] section, CurStepChanged 93-103, NextButtonClick 125-160), llm/runtime.py:163-169, installer/README_testers.md:5 ('about 8 GB'). No installer was run and no Inno Setup is to hand; data/runtime/server.yaml was not read (rule), so the sizes are the readme's.

## typed-patterns-11: RE-RATE engine2-4: hour_named said yes on none of 1,896 real lines while the model filled the time on every timed wait; the override should go, not be narrowed

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `engine/clock.py:72`. **Same place:** engine2-4
- **Evidence:** scenes/world.py:4406: `named = clock.hour_named(text)` overrules intent.wait_until and intent.wait_minutes. On the logged lines (work/tp/h2.py): hour_named yes on 0; 123 waits read by the model, 17 with wait_until and 4 with wait_minutes of their own.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** The first round's fault stands ('wait until two guards pass' is two o'clock), but its fix was a tighter pattern. The measure says the pattern adds nothing on typed lines and can only take a right reading away: the plan's field carried the time each time it was typed. What the field cannot say today is a clock hour ('until 3'), since wait_until is a closed list of eight parts of the day.
- **Fix:** Keep engine2-4's fix (a number is an hour only by a positive rule): it needs no model. The hour as a field of the wait step belongs with the review's 5.1 point 3 behind the reader's switch: add it to the contract's grammar there, put the lines in the corpus ('until eight in the morning', 'till 3 pm', 'until 8:00', 'until two guards pass'), and take hour_named's override out only when the live run shows the field filled right; f687's test then moves from the pattern to the field.
- **The finder's first fix:** Give wait_until its clock hours (or a wait_hour field) in the contract's grammar and drop hour_named's override in on_wait; rest_asked's 'until <part of day>' search (scenes/world.py:4521) goes the same way.
- **The check:** The count holds (hour_named says yes on 0 of 1,886 lines) and so does the first round's fault ('I wait until two guards pass.' gives (2, True); 'We wait until six riders have gone' gives (6, True)). The count cannot carry the conclusion, though. Only 6 logged lines say until or till at all and none names a clock hour (the timed waits are 'for a minute', 'a few minutes', 'until the sun comes up'), so the sample holds no line the pattern is for, and none it harms. The one played line on record that named an hour is why the pattern exists: tools/sim/wait_hour_687_test.py keeps 'We wait here until eight in the morning.', read by the model as wait_until dawn and stopped at 6:00, because wait_until is a closed list of eight parts of the day (llm/contracts.py:474). 'The plan's field carried the time each time' is loose too: 'close my eyes for a few hours' came back wait_until morning with wait_minutes 120, and on_wait takes the until. Dropping the override before the model is shown to fill an hour brings f687's fault back and fails its test, which pins the reading as intended. rest_asked cannot go the same way as said: its three callers (scenes/world.py:4066, 4534, 4537) run where the plan has no wait step to carry a field (a room bought, an 'other'). Whether the hour should be a field rather than a pattern cannot be settled without the model; it is the plan's own form, already written. engine2-4's own rating is not changed by this.
- **How it was checked:** Ran clock.hour_named over the 1,886 logged lines of my replay, listed every line holding until, till or til and every logged wait that carries a time (C:/Users/tstil/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/dad68772ed0cbd02/d2ae1f65-36c6-4be3-9744-2919d03b2cce/scratchpad/audit/work/tp2/read2.py, argument wu); called hour_named on probe lines; read on_wait, rest_asked and their three callers, llm/contracts.py:473-474 and scenes/world_prompts.py:36-37; ran tools/sim/wait_hour_687_test.py (ALL PASS); read docs/design/21_play_faults_plan.md A4.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/21_play_faults_plan.md A4 ('The contract keeps the named periods and gains an hour of the clock'; 'Left, and why. The hour: the plan's way is a new field of the contract ...'; f687 then built it as a pattern); docs/design/26_approach_review.md 5.1 point 3 ('a count, an hour, a camp, a room'). The first round's fix for engine2-4 already names the field as the form that removes the override.

## engine5-4: start_thread indexes world.pressures with a queued pressure id it never checks; a follow-on whose pressure the world lacks raises KeyError inside the pulse

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `engine/pulse.py:358`
- **Evidence:** pulse.py:357-358 `elif pressure_id:` / `pressure = world.pressures[pressure_id]`; start_queued (pulse.py:549-551) passes `pressure_id=q.get("pressure") or ""`, and engine/threads.py:387 queues `"pressure": pid` from the ended thread, which for a consequence thread is `consequence:<rule id>` (engine/consequences.py:65), never a key of world.pressures. Reproduced (engine5_checks.py, check D): `start_queued raised KeyError: 'consequence:hunters_want_you'`.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Latent today: the three templates consequences use (social_hunters, social_watch, work_hall) carry no `then`, so nothing queues such a row. It becomes live with a data-only change (a `then` on one of those templates, or a consequence rule pointed at one of the 13 templates that have `then`), or with an old save whose queued row names a pressure since renamed or removed from data/world. The row is taken off the queue before the call, the transaction rolls back and restores it, so the pulse fails again on every following line.
- **Fix:** In start_queued, look the pressure up with world.pressures.get; when it is missing start the follow-on from the row's place and template with no pressure (start_thread needs a branch for that: its place_id branch picks another pressure standing at the place). Add to engine/data_check.py that a template marked consequence carries no `then`, or give a consequence's follow-on its pressure-shaped record again through consequences.pressure_for.
- **The finder's first fix:** Use world.pressures.get(pressure_id) and, when it is missing, fall back to the queued row's place with pressure=None (start_queued already carries `place`); add the case to engine/data_check.py so data cannot queue what cannot start.
- **The check:** Printed: start_queued raised KeyError: 'consequence:hunters_want_you'. But also: rules hunters_want_you, watch_asking and hall_notices use social_hunters, social_watch, work_hall, each then=False, and follow_up for a consequence thread on today's data queues: None (even with always=True). So the KeyError path at pulse.py:358 is real and no data check forbids a `then` on a template marked consequence (threads.py:610-618 checks only that the named template exists), but shipped data cannot produce the row. The finding's second route is half wrong: a consequence rule pointed at a template that has `then` is refused by consequences.problems (consequences.py:117) unless that template is also marked consequence. The old-save route has one precedent, and it was handled: pressure valecourt_court was renamed in 4552b72 and migration v5 (storage/migrations.py:64-85) rewrote the old name wherever the save held it. If the state ever did arise the cost would be high, not low: the world operation rolls back, the row returns, and every later pulse fails the same way.
- **How it was checked:** Read pulse.start_thread and start_queued, threads.follow_up and its four callers, consequences.pressure_for, tick and problems, and threads.problems for a data rule. Ran section 4 of my script: a hand-built queued row through start_queued, then follow_up on today's data for a consequence thread. Looked in git history for a pressure id ever removed.

## llm1-3: In the built game the audit log is written inside the bundle, not beside the exe with the other logs

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/audit.py:45`. **Same place:** dead-switches-15, dead-switches-3, llm1-4
- **Evidence:** `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` (line 21) and `folder = ROOT / A.get("folder", "logs/audit")` (line 45). core/paths.py: 'BUNDLE is where the packaged game data is unpacked and APP is the folder holding the exe, where saves/ and logs/ are kept'; llm/runtime.py:652 uses `Path(paths.APP) / "logs"`; main.py:25 does os.chdir(paths.APP) for the relative log paths in config.py.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** build_exe.bat builds --onedir with an unpinned PyInstaller. With PyInstaller 6 a bundled module's __file__ is under <app>/_internal, so the audit log goes to <app>/_internal/logs/audit/ while turns.jsonl, llm_calls.jsonl and crash.log go to <app>/logs/. A tester who sends logs/ (and docs/design/11's Send logs bundle, which lists logs/audit/) leaves the audit log behind, and #audit names a folder inside the bundle. From source both folders are the project folder, so it never shows there. I did not build an exe to watch it happen.
- **Fix:** Build the folder from core.paths.APP (folder = paths.APP / A.get('folder', 'logs/audit')), as llm/runtime.py does, and read data/rules/audit_log.yaml from paths.BUNDLE as llm/launch.py and llm/runtime.py read their data, so no module works out the two folders from __file__. From source both are the project folder, so audit_log_test.py is unaffected. A line in tools/sim/frozen_531_test.py (which already fakes sys.frozen and sys._MEIPASS) can pin that the audit folder is under APP.
- **The finder's first fix:** Build the folder from core.paths.APP, as llm/runtime.py does for its logs, and keep ROOT only for reading data/rules/audit_log.yaml.
- **The check:** Traced, not seen. audit.py takes ROOT from __file__ and both reads data/rules/audit_log.yaml from it (line 22, at import) and writes the log under it (line 45). Since the game imports audit and data/ is packed only into the bundle (build_exe.bat --add-data "data;data"), ROOT is necessarily the bundle in any built game that starts, so the audit log is under BUNDLE/logs/audit, while every other log is under APP: config.py's paths are relative and main.py:25 does os.chdir(paths.APP) ('saves/ and logs/ live beside the exe'); llm/runtime.py:652 uses paths.APP / 'logs'. Nothing overrides the audit folder when frozen (the only writer of audit.A['folder'] is tools/sim/audit_log_test.py). BUNDLE and APP differ only when PyInstaller unpacks into a sub-folder, which is the default for --onedir from PyInstaller 6 (<app>/_internal); build_exe.bat does not pin the version or pass --contents-directory. With PyInstaller 5 the two folders are the same and nothing is wrong. The one step I could not observe is which layout the owner's build has. The installer puts the game in {localappdata}\Programs\Meravia (meravia.iss:17), which is writable, so the folder is made silently. docs/design/11_send_logs_feature.md lists audit/ among the files under logs/ beside the exe.

## llm1-6: vectors() reads the cache again after the server call: a cached text trimmed meanwhile, or a short answer, is a KeyError

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/embed.py:89`
- **Evidence:** `want = [t for t in dict.fromkeys(texts) if t not in _cache]` (line 66, outside the lock) and, after the call, `out = [_cache[t] for t in texts]` (line 89). Checked with a stand-in embedder: when another vectors() request adds CACHE_SIZE texts while this one waits on the server, the read raises KeyError('an old line said long ago'); an answer with one vector fewer than the texts raises KeyError too.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Needs a second thread embedding while the turn's thread waits on the embedder, with the cache at its 2,000 cap: a background lane whose contract judges speech by meaning, or a second character's turn. Today only the turn's thread embeds (the two background lanes ask for ResidentSet and MechanicSet, which do not), so it is latent. The KeyError would be raised inside a contract's validator (banter.repeats, answers_first), where llm/gateway.py catches only ValidationError, so it leaves generate() as a crash, not a failed try. The comment on lines 88-89 ('a long game can never drop a vector mid-request') holds for one thread only.
- **Fix:** As proposed, for when a second thread does embed (multiplayer, or a background contract that judges by meaning): take the hits into a local dict under the lock at the first look, add the new vectors to it, and build `out` from that dict; then write the new ones to the cache, mark as used and trim under one lock. vectors() then never re-reads the shared cache for its own answer. Return None when the count of vectors differs from the texts asked (the live source already refuses that). Correct the comment on lines 88-89.
- **The finder's first fix:** Keep the hits found at the first look in a local dict and build the result from it and the new vectors under one lock; treat an answer whose length differs from the request as a failed call (return None).
- **The check:** The mechanism is real: with the cache at its 2,000 cap and the hit its oldest entry, ONE new text embedded by a second thread while the first waits on the embedder is enough (not CACHE_SIZE texts): the first thread's read at embed.py:89 raised KeyError('an old line said long ago'). One thread alone at the cap is fine. But the state does not arise in the game today: the only threads beside the turn's that call the model are npc/backfill.py (populate_place, ResidentSet) and character/creation.py (generate_passive_mechanics, MechanicSet), and neither contract nor the gateway's checks for those tasks embed; the report says so itself. The second half is refuted for the real server: llm/llama.py:441-442 raises Failure('server', 'N embeddings for M texts') on a short answer, which vectors() catches and returns None for. Only a stand-in or a recording could hand back fewer (my stand-in did: KeyError('second text')). A KeyError in a validator is not wrapped by pydantic, so it would leave generate() as the report says.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/embed.py whole, llm/backend.py StandIn/embed, llm/llama.py embed (429-444), llm/runtime.py embed_call, and every thread started in game code (npc/backfill.py, character/creation.py, ui/gui, llm/launch.py, core/updates.py) with what each asks the model for. Ran work/llm1_1/check_mentor_and_embed.py with a stand-in embedder and two threads.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/17_multiplayer_survey_and_plan.md (the survey table lists embed's one process-wide state, 'One failed embedding turns embeddings off for everyone', as work for multiplayer); the cache read after the call is not written down.

## silent-excepts-6: The mends of an answer already taken (no dashes, names put right, the A1 mend count) can stop half way with no record (gateway.py 371 and 379)

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/gateway.py:371`

So the half mend and the lost count are real under an injected fault, and on everything the model wrote in the tracked record neither mend raises. ## leftovers-6: An embedding answer with status 200 and wrong-shaped vectors is taken as real: empty, short and all-zero vectors are cached and every check by meaning answers 'nothing alike'; nulls raise a TypeError outside the handler. The fake never answers so

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/llama.py:443`. **Same place:** llm2-2
- **Evidence:** llm/llama.py:441-443 refuses only a wrong row count, then `return Embedding(vectors=[r.get("embedding") or [] for r in rows], ...`. llm/embed.py:86-87 `n = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in v)) or 1.0` / `_cache[t] = [x / n for x in v]` is after the try that ends at :81. Run against tools/sim/fake_llama.py: [] or no key gives likeness 0, [1.0] against a three-number vector gives 0.6, all zeros 0.0, nulls a TypeError.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** When the embedder answers 200 with a vector that is empty, short, all zero (what llama.cpp's server sends when it could not get an embedding, as far as I recall; not run here) or null, the text is cached as if embedded. Each check that asks by meaning (a repeated line, a claim against what is known, an answer on the subject) then finds nothing alike for that text and passes, where a failed embedder would have fallen back to shared words. Nulls raise a TypeError that is no Failure, so it leaves through a contract's validator as a crash (llm/gateway.py catches only ValidationError there, as all.json llm1-6 notes). tools/sim/fake_llama.py answers well-formed vectors unless scripted, and no test scripts these, so the suite passes.
- **Fix:** Put the check where every source passes, not in the llama adapter alone: in llm/embed.py vectors(), before anything is cached, refuse an answer whose count differs from the texts asked or that holds a vector that is empty, not all finite numbers, of another length than the embedder's (the first good vector's length, kept with _state['model']), or of zero norm; treat it as the failed call the function already knows (return None, the callers' word fallbacks), and move the norm arithmetic inside the guarded part so nothing but an Interrupt can leave. That covers the stand-in and a replay as well as LlamaServer, and the short answer of all.json llm1-6. Add the five answers to llama_adapter_521_test.py or embed_review_524_test.py. Whether one bad vector turns embeddings off for the session or only fails that call (as too_big does) is a choice to make there.
- **The finder's first fix:** In LlamaServer.embed refuse a vector that is empty, holds anything but finite numbers, differs in length from the first, or has zero norm, with Failure('server', ...): llm/embed.py already turns that into embeddings off and the word fallbacks. Add the five answers (tables/leftovers.md section 4) to the adapter's test.
- **The check:** The handling is as the finder says, and I saw it through the real path, not a copy of the arithmetic. Printed: an empty embedding, or none -> whole() [0], the text cached with a vector of length 0, embeddings failed False; a short one ([1.0]) -> [0.6]; all zero -> [0.0]; nulls -> 'TypeError left llm/embed.py: unsupported operand type(s) for *: NoneType and NoneType' (embed.py:86 is after the try that ends at 81). One thing more than the finder had: a text cached with an empty or zero vector scores 0 against itself, so a line said twice word for word reads as nothing alike until it leaves the cache. llama.py:441-442 refuses only a wrong row count, and no test scripts any of these answers. What I could not show is the real server answering so: the tracked call logs keep no vectors and llama.cpp's source is not in the tree. From memory, as the finder also says, llama-server fills a vector with zeros when it cannot get an embedding; empty, short and null vectors I know no cause for. So the path exists and the state is not shown: plausible, and low.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/llama.py embed (429-444), llm/embed.py whole, llm/backend.py embed and facts, tools/sim/fake_llama.py, and the embedding checks in tools/sim/llama_adapter_521_test.py (281-292). Ran scratchpad/audit/work/skeptic_leftovers_1/embed_end_to_end.py: the game's own path (llm.embed.whole -> backend.embed -> LlamaServer.embed) against tools/sim/fake_llama.py scripted with each shape; no model, no campaign.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/17_multiplayer_survey_and_plan.md:130 lists 'One failed embedding turns embeddings off for everyone' (the shared state, not the answer's shape). The shape is not written down.
