## suite-speed-5: A killed run frees the lock at once while the tests it started run on in saves/, and the record of what it had finished is lost

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `tools/run_suite.py:285`. **Same place:** suite-speed-9
- **Evidence:** `rc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(test)], cwd=root, env=env, stdout=fh, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=timeout).returncode` (285): nothing ties the test's life to the runner's; `keep_ran(root, record)` (423) is reached only when every test is done. Probe on a made-up tree with the real runner, on Windows: the runner killed while one test slept; busy() was False at once and a second take() succeeded at once; the orphaned test ran on and wrote into saves/ 11 s after the kill; .ran.json was not written though another test had finished; out/ran/<test>.<pid>.json stayed behind.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A stopped background task, a time limit or a closed terminal kills run_suite. The Stop hook's --busy check then finds the suite free and starts a run while up to -j tests of the dead run still use the same save folders: the collision the lock was built to end (about 55 false failures on 16 November, docs/design/27). The 900 s limit on an orphan is no longer enforced by anyone, and a full run killed near its end keeps no record of the 500 tests it ran.
- **Fix:** Cheap half first: write the record as tests finish, or in the finally, so a stopped run keeps what it ran. For the orphans, tie the tests to the runner (a Windows job object with kill-on-close; a process group killed on exit elsewhere), which covers every way the runner can die; worth doing only if a single-process kill is seen in practice.
- **The finder's first fix:** Tie the tests to the runner (a Windows job object with kill-on-close; a process group killed on exit on Linux), or write the children's process ids in the lock file and have take() wait for them; keep the record as tests finish, or in the finally.
- **The check:** The mechanism is real but the named ways of killing do not reach it here. Runner's process alone killed: busy() False 0.3 s later, a second take() succeeded at once, the sleeping test wrote into saves/ 11.4 s after the kill, .ran.json was not written though another test had finished, and out/ran/s_test.py.<pid>.json stayed behind. Whole tree killed (taskkill /T): the test died with the runner and wrote nothing. In this session a stopped background task took the child with it (no late write 33 s after the start of a child that sleeps 20 s), and a command that passes its time limit is not killed at all: it is moved to the background and runs on. So an orphan needs a kill of the one process: Task Manager's End task, kill or taskkill without /T, GNU timeout, or a crash of the runner. I could not show that any of the owner's usual routes does that; the Stop hook's own time limit was not tested. The lost record is confirmed for every kill: keep_ran (line 423) runs only after the last test, so a run stopped near its end keeps nothing of what it ran and the older record stays. The test pins only that a dead holder frees the lock.
- **How it was checked:** Read tools/run_suite.py 271-295, 304-361 and 395-425, tools/sim/suite_loop_717_test.py 201-230 and docs/design/27_infrastructure_plan.md f717 item 4. Ran scratch script ss5_kill.py: the real runner on a made-up tree in the scratch folder, killed while one test slept, once by its own process and once by its whole tree (taskkill /T). Then tested how this Claude Code session ends a command: a parent that starts a child as run_one does (ss5_parent.py), run past a time limit and stopped as a background task.
- **Already recorded:** docs/design/27_infrastructure_plan.md, f717 item 4: a run that dies or is killed lets go of the lock at once, so there is nothing to go stale; the tests it started are not mentioned.

## frontend-shipping-5: Without the WebView2 runtime the window opens on the old Internet Explorer engine and stays blank: the browser fallback is taken only when pywebview raises

- **Checked:** plausible. **Weight:** low (first given as medium). **Place:** `ui/gui/__init__.py:49`
- **Evidence:** ui/gui/__init__.py:49-50 `import webview` / `window = webview.create_window(title, url, ...)`, with the browser path only under `except ImportError:` (:62) and `except Exception as e:` (:64). installer/meravia.iss:139-143 downloads Microsoft's bootstrapper when the runtime is missing and, when a download fails, says the game is installed anyway (:154). pywebview 6.2.1 (the version installed here), webview/platforms/winforms.py:131-155, picks the MSHTML renderer without raising when WebView2 is absent.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** A Windows 10 machine without the runtime where the bootstrapper could not be fetched or its silent install failed, or anyone running play.bat on such a machine: the window opens, the old engine cannot parse app.js (async functions, fetch, EventSource), and the player looks at the bare page for good while the game and the model server run behind it. Not run: this machine has WebView2.
- **Fix:** The proposed probe works. A wider one needs no registry key kept in step with the installer's: the page asks /prefs and opens /events as soon as its script runs, so let the bridge note the first /events request and, when none has come some seconds after the window shows, open the browser path that is already there with a plain line saying why. That covers a missing runtime and any other cause of a page whose script never ran.
- **The finder's first fix:** Before create_window on Windows, ask what the installer asks (the EdgeUpdate client key) and, when the runtime is missing, take the browser path that is already there with a plain line saying why.
- **The check:** winforms.py: when _is_chromium() is False it imports the mshtml renderer with only logger.warning('MSHTML is deprecated...') and raises nothing, so _window's two except arms (ui/gui/__init__.py:62-65) are never taken and the browser path is not reached. Internet Explorer's engine parses neither async functions nor arrow functions and has no EventSource, so app.js would not run and index.html:49's 'Loading...' would stand. Reach is small, hence low: Windows 11 carries the runtime, Windows 10 has been sent it by Windows Update, and the installer fetches it when it is missing; what is left is a Windows 10 machine without it where the bootstrapper's download or its silent install (meravia.iss:40, result unchecked) failed, or a run from source there.
- **How it was checked:** Read ui/gui/__init__.py:47-72 and pywebview 6.2.1 as installed in the Python on PATH (site-packages/webview/platforms/winforms.py:68-155). Counted the page's syntax: app.js has 166 lines with async functions or arrow functions, fetch at :14, EventSource at :1545. Read installer/meravia.iss:40, 110-118, 139-143, 154. Not run: this machine has WebView2, and forcing the old renderer would open a window on the owner's desktop.

## leftovers-2: Setup downloads Microsoft's WebView2 bootstrapper with no hash and runs it silently: the one unpinned file on a page whose header says each is checked against its sha256

- **Checked:** refuted. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `installer/meravia.iss:141`
- **Evidence:** installer/meravia.iss:141 `DownloadPage.Add('https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703', 'MicrosoftEdgeWebview2Setup.exe', '');` (the third argument is the hash, empty) and :40 `Filename: "{tmp}\MicrosoftEdgeWebview2Setup.exe"; Parameters: "/silent /install"`. Line 4 of the header: 'files are downloaded here, each checked against its sha256'.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** On a machine without the WebView2 runtime, Setup fetches whatever that forwarding link answers and runs it with no window. The model and runtime files on the same download page are refused when their sha256 differs; this one cannot be, because the link serves whatever Microsoft's current bootstrapper is. Not run here (code read only).
- **Fix:** None needed. If the owner wants one download fewer during Setup, the bootstrapper (under 2 MB) may be carried in [Files] with dontcopy and extracted when the runtime is missing; that removes a failure point, it does not pin the runtime.
- **The finder's first fix:** Carry the small bootstrapper inside the installer, so the installer's own digest covers it and nothing unpinned is downloaded; or pin a fixed-version bootstrapper by sha256 in the same table the other downloads are pinned from. A moving link cannot be pinned.
- **The check:** The two code lines are as quoted: meravia.iss:141 adds the bootstrapper with an empty hash and :40 runs it with /silent /install. But the finding's ground, that the header says every file is checked, is a cut quote. The header reads (lines 2-4): 'offers to install Microsoft's WebView2 window component when it is missing. ... the model files are downloaded here, each checked against its sha256'. The promise is for the model files (line 3 ends 'the model', line 4 begins 'files are downloaded here'); the WebView2 step is named apart and promised nothing. So the unpinned download is as written, not an oversight. The link is Microsoft's own forwarding link for its current bootstrapper, fetched over https, and as the finder says a moving link cannot be pinned. No way for a wrong file to arrive was shown. The proposed fix would prove little: a bootstrapper carried in the installer, or pinned, still downloads the runtime itself from Microsoft with nothing of ours checking it. What is left is a choice, not a defect; all.json frontend-shipping-5 already covers the case where this step fails and the window stays blank.
- **How it was checked:** Read installer/meravia.iss whole (the header 1-5, [Run] 40, HaveWebView2Setup 105-108, WebView2Installed 110-118, NextButtonClick 125-160) and tools/installer_files.py (the model downloads). Searched GOALS.md and docs/design for WebView2 and sha256. No installer was run and no Inno Setup is to hand.

## llm-flow-9: think_room measures a thinking call against both slots' context (32,768) where one slot holds 16,384

- **Checked:** refuted. **Weight:** low. **Place:** `llm/backend.py:157`
- **Evidence:** llm/backend.py:157 `fits = int(config.NUM_CTX) - chars // 3 - int(max_tokens) - 256`; config.py:14 `NUM_CTX = int(__import__("os").environ.get("DND_NUM_CTX", "0") or 0) or 32768`; llm/runtime.py:227 `ctx = int(s["slots"]) * int(s["slot_ctx"])` (the run's log: n_ctx 32768, n_slots 2, n_ctx_slot 16384); llm/llama.py:124 sends `"n_predict": int(req.max_tokens) + room`.
- **What a player or the owner meets:** Only when DND_THINK_TASKS names a task (a measuring night; thinking is off in play), so nothing in this run. A request past about 6,100 tokens with max_tokens 2,048 is still given the full 8,192 of room, more than the slot has left; at npc_conversation's ceiling (36,500 characters, 9,125 tokens) the slot has about 1,900 beside the prompt and the answer, so the thinking can run to the slot's end and cut the answer. The largest request in this run was 4,848 tokens.
- **Fix:** Nothing to fix now. Keep one line with f544's 'for the owner, not built' note: if the adapter is ever made able to think (a thinking call's shape sent as response_format), think_room must then take the slot's context (LlamaServer.slot_ctx(), which already reads the machine's value or the server's /props) in place of config.NUM_CTX, and config.NUM_CTX / DND_NUM_CTX can go with it since the runtime never reads them.
- **The finder's first fix:** Take the context from the slot (LlamaServer.slot_ctx(), or the settings' slot_ctx) instead of config.NUM_CTX, as tools/situation_ab.py:181 does for its replays.
- **The check:** The arithmetic is as stated and I saw it: with DND_THINK_TASKS=npc_conversation and a 36,500-character request (its ceiling, data/measured/prompt_ceilings.yaml:16), think_room gave 8,192 and the body carried n_predict 10,240, where a 16,384 slot would allow 1,914 by the function's own estimate; the run's server log reads 'n_slots = 2, n_ctx_slot = 16384'. config.NUM_CTX is a leftover of the old model server's per-call num_ctx (f534, 2026-11-05, the day before f527/f532): nothing in llm/runtime.py reads it. But the harm described cannot happen as the code stands. The same script shows the game's body carries 'grammar' and no response_format with enable_thinking true, and the f544 commit records from a real pod session: 'a raw grammar binds from the first token, so the model can only write the JSON ... the probe wrote 667 tokens and none of them thinking ... DND_THINK_TASKS has done nothing on llama-server since f527 for the same reason' (also tools/situation_ab.py:11, 178, 307). So on the game's path no call thinks, the room is never thought in, and no thinking can run to the slot's end and cut an answer; the oversized n_predict is only a higher ceiling on a grammar-bound answer that ends by itself, and the server stops at the slot's end regardless. Thinking is also off for every task by the owner's decision (GOALS.md:184), and the one tool that does make the model think (tools/situation_ab.py, response_format) sets the slot's context itself (line 181). tools/sim/thinking_room_534_test.py:73-78 pins that the room follows DND_NUM_CTX.
- **How it was checked:** Read llm/backend.py:153-169, llm/llama.py:115-136 and 308-427, llm/runtime.py:86-101 and 223-229, config.py:1-14, tools/situation_ab.py:1-39, 172-190, 280-314, tools/think_ab.py:150-198, tools/sim/thinking_room_534_test.py, GOALS.md:184, and the f544 commit message (git show --no-patch e822daf). Checked the run's llama-server.log for the slot size. Ran scratchpad/audit/work/llmflow2_think.py (CPU only, no server, no campaign): think_room and llama_body for a task named in DND_THINK_TASKS at several request sizes.
- **Already recorded:** GOALS.md:184 (owner's decisions, 'Thinking, the owner on 2026-11-08': off for every task, the per-task switch kept as a measuring tool). The f544 commit message (e822daf) records that DND_THINK_TASKS does nothing on llama-server since f527. The context mismatch itself is written down nowhere in GOALS.md or docs/design.
